## 2026-08-10 - ENG-93989 scope trim: PR #997 reduced to the feature

Context: 21 commits had accreted onto one feature commit — a bespoke advisory-redaction mechanism, two foreign tickets, and a family-wide contract test — leaving 318 lines of product code against ~2140 of tests.
Decision: reverted `clio.tests/CreatioPkgTests.cs` (a CI-flake fix for package tests) and `clio.tests/Theming/GoogleFontsCatalogTests.cs` (ENG-93985 parallelism cap) to master; both need their own pull request. `UpdateThemeTool.cs`'s description trim stays by owner's call.
Decision: the branch had appended its brand-mode fixture to master's existing `ThemingVersionFloorContractE2ETests.cs`, whose family-wide "every gated theming tool advertises the floor" fixture predates this work. Master's file is back to byte-identical, and the new fixture moved to its own `ThemingVersionFloorBrandModeE2ETests.cs` — one fixture per file, as the rest of clio.mcp.e2e does. Before treating an e2e file as this branch's, check `git ls-tree origin/master` on it: a large one-hunk `+` stat can be an append to a pre-existing file, not a new one.
Decision: `BuildThemeAdvertisedRosters_ShouldListEveryThemeBrandArgsProperty` moved from `CreateThemeToolTests` to `BuildThemeToolTests` — it asserts only about build-theme. `System.ComponentModel.DescriptionAttribute` must stay fully qualified there: a plain `using` collides with NUnit's `Description`/`Category`.
Discovery: the `ThemeBrandArgs` base record and its eight reflection guards are not feature work — they exist because Sonar's duplicated-lines gate failed at 3.2% against a 3% threshold. Kept, because splitting a finished deduplication costs more than it returns, but the PR description must name it as a quality-gate change rather than part of the feature.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/ThemingVersionFloorBrandModeE2ETests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/{BuildThemeToolTests,CreateThemeToolTests}.cs, clio.tests/{CreatioPkgTests,Theming/GoogleFontsCatalogTests}.cs
Impact: the PR carries the feature plus its own coverage; three unrelated concerns leave with their own reviews instead of riding this one.

## 2026-08-05 - ENG-93989 review fixes: build-fault taxonomy, warnings redacted at the MCP boundary

Context: review found thrown build-phase faults escaping the `theme-build-failed` taxonomy, and the advisory non-redaction contract enforced only by a Debug assert, which is a no-op in Release.
Decision: brand mode tracks whether a fault belongs to the build phase and prefixes it `theme-build-failed` — no broad catch, no soft fallback.
Decision (supersedes the 2026-08-07 "Release containment for advisories" entry and the containment hardening in 7f77b936): the strip-and-announce mechanism inside `CollectWarnings` is removed, not privatised. `CollectWarnings` is static and single-purpose again and the command layer carries no MCP-transport concern. Redaction stays OUT of both theme tools' result factories, per the review comment that removed it from this layer in the first place — the one advisory that needs it is redacted where it is composed, in `BuildThemeTool.ResolveVersionSettings`.
Discovery: the guard could not prevent a leak, because the channel it protected already ships the same text unprotected. `create-theme` had no warnings channel at all before this branch, while `build-theme` has carried one on master all along — unredacted, same four advisories from the same shared `CollectWarnings`, and the same raw `environment-name` interpolation. So either those advisories were never a risk, or master has been leaking through build-theme the whole time. The only reachable outcome of the guard on today's inputs was a false positive: a grammar-valid family beginning with "Bearer " trips the redactor's Bearer-token rule, which mangled a legitimate advisory AND told the caller to report a clio defect. Future-edit protection stays where it belongs — the trio of tests that drive real builds with trip text in every option field.
Discovery: the brand-parameter guard and its rosters were reflection over `ThemeBrandArgs` — `MetadataToken` ordering, an `IsSupplied` value-type/boxing switch, two derived static fields. No review comment asked for it. Replaced by nine explicit checks and two consts: the existing per-property tests already fail when a new `ThemeBrandArgs` property is missing from the guard, so reflection bought nothing they did not, while costing the unreachable boxing arms, a static-initializer-order workaround, and a caller-facing parameter order resting on metadata layout.
Discovery: byte identity between the two tools has to be asserted across `BuildThemeTool` and `CreateThemeTool` over one shared `BuildThemeCommand`. Asserting the create path against the command alone leaves a drift in either tool's hand-written `BuildThemeOptions` initializer invisible.
Deferred: a latest-fallback advisory on the brand-mode version probe (would change build-theme's observable warnings); a TimeProvider seam for the shared fonts cache; the 512-cap saturation signal; the sync-over-async probe bridge; one duplicate ApplicationInfoService probe per brand-mode call.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/{CreateThemeTool,BuildThemeTool}.cs, clio/Command/Theming/BuildThemeCommand.cs, docs/McpCapabilityMap.md
Impact: an unexpected build fault reaches agents inside the documented error taxonomy, and no warning entry crosses the MCP boundary unredacted in any build configuration.

## 2026-07-31 - ENG-93989: ThemeBrandArgs extraction, build seam removal

Context: Sonar failed the quality gate on duplicated lines between the two theme tools' brand-argument blocks.
Decision: the seven shared brand properties moved to an abstract `ThemeBrandArgs` record; `primary` and `version` stay on each concrete record because their required-ness and resolution rules differ per tool. `virtual` removed from `TryBuildTheme` — tool tests wire a real `BuildThemeCommand` to substituted engine/template/version-resolver dependencies instead of widening a production contract for a test seam.
Discovery: inherited init-only properties DO reach the SDK-generated MCP schema — verified against the real server over stdio. Only property order changes, which JSON Schema ignores.
Discovery: the `hash` in `list-themes`' `cssFilePath` is the MD5 of the stored CSS, so hash-to-hash comparison across two themes is a valid byte-identity proof. Never compare it against a locally rebuilt file — the rebuild differs for the reason below.
Discovery (pre-existing bug, own ticket): with a custom font and no weights argument the MCP tools emit `wght@400;500;600` while `clio build-theme` emits no weights at all. `FontImportBuilder.DefaultFontWeights` applies only when the weight list is null, and the CLI passes an empty list — so the CLI contradicts its own help, which documents the 400/500/600 default.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/{ThemeBrandArgs,CreateThemeTool,BuildThemeTool,UpdateThemeTool}.cs, clio/Command/Theming/BuildThemeCommand.cs
Impact: brand arguments are declared once, so a new one cannot reach one tool and miss the other.

## 2026-07-30 - ENG-93989: create-theme brand mode (one call, no CSS across the model boundary)

Context: the branding flow spent ~46% of its agent time re-emitting build-theme's ~16.5 KB CSS back into create-theme's `css-content`.
Decision: extend the existing `create-theme` MCP tool with brand parameters and compose the build server-side — no new tool and no CLI verb (MCP-only, precedent `advise-theme-palette`). `update-theme` keeps the inline path; its brand mode is out of the ticket's scope. No `css-content-file` on this tool — it would knot a three-way XOR.
Decision: brand mode runs inside the existing `ExecuteResolved` executor, so it inherits the per-tenant lock, the `MarkInUse` reservation and the fail-closed version gate — a below-floor environment is refused before any build work runs.
Discovery (costs hours to rediscover): when mapping brand args onto `BuildThemeOptions`, `EnvironmentName` must stay unset. The environment reaches the build only as `resolvedSettings`, and copying it alongside an explicit `version` trips `ResolveVersion`'s mutual-exclusion guard on every version+environment call.
Discovery (local toolchain): `clio.tests` needs C# 13 — NUnit 4.6.1 disambiguates its `Assert.Throws` overloads with `[OverloadResolutionPriority]`, so an SDK 8.0.4xx default fails 27 pre-existing files with CS0121. CI is unaffected.
Measurements (same stand, model and inputs, explicit id): whole flow 97.0s -> 20.5s; `create-theme` arguments 17,350 -> 268 chars (~4,957 -> ~77 output tokens); round trips 2 -> 1.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/{CreateThemeTool,BuildThemeTool}.cs, clio/Command/Theming/BuildThemeCommand.cs, docs/McpCapabilityMap.md, spec/adr/adr-theming.md
Impact: no-code theme creation is one MCP call from palette hexes, fonts and a caption.

## 2026-07-31 - ENG-93985 rework: probe-driven import suppression replaces local-font-families

Context: PR #993 review (plus toolkit PR #68) rejected the `local-font-families` design: clio already probes Google Fonts for the warning, so it can make the suppression decision itself, and after ENG-93989 the agent may build without a pre-warning step, so the confirm-then-rebuild round trip no longer fits. Owner constraints: no hardcoded font list, no CLIO_FONT_IMPORT_POLICY env off-ramp, no full-catalog download for case correction; the agent still checks availability up front and asks explicit confirmation for non-Google fonts, but clio must handle it independently; warnings arrive post factum. Full rationale + verified endpoint contract in spec/adr/adr-ENG-93985-google-fonts-availability.md.

Decision: the metadata probe now DRIVES the import, not just the warning. GoogleFontsCatalog rewritten async (`LookupAsync(family, ct)`, typed HttpClient via BindingsModule AddHttpClient with 3s ProbeTimeout + UA `clio` + AllowAutoRedirect=false, TimeProvider injected): 200+JSON content type -> InCatalog (JSON gate keeps consent/bot pages from reading as published); 404 -> NotInCatalog -> @import suppressed for that family + case-sensitivity/rename warning; anything else -> Unverified -> FAIL-OPEN (import kept + could-not-verify warning) so firewalled hosts keep Google fonts working. Definitive verdicts memoized 5 min; Unverified memoized only 30 s, long enough to absorb one build's burst of families without pinning a transient outage for the definitive TTL. Ordinal end-to-end: probe cache, suppression list, ThemeCssBuilder matching (FontsInput.LocallyInstalledFamilies renamed SuppressedImportFamilies, matching flipped case-insensitive->Ordinal). BuildThemeCommand: LocalFontFamilies option deleted; NormalizeFamily (trim + FontImportBuilder.CollapseWhitespace, new) canonicalizes before probe/build; ResolveFontAvailability probes ordinal-distinct requested families concurrently, harvests per-task (faulted task degrades to Unverified alone, probe can never fail the build). MCP tool: OpenWorld=true, description discloses the probe + that CSS varies with probe outcomes; removed-arg pre-check on ExtensionData (all 3 spellings, GuidanceGetTool.cs:61-69 precedent) returns a loud failure naming the replacement. Guidance + SKILL.md (toolkit pr-68): agent probes exact spelling (%20), one knowledge-based retry (roboto->Roboto, Muli->Mulish; Title-Case heuristic falsified by PT Sans/Pt Sans), then the USER resolves via fonts.google.com/?query=<name>; confirmed-local warning = expected echo, anything else relay + restyle.

Discovery: css2 lies both ways (Verdana -> 200 with /l/ lookalike that would SHADOW the locally installed font — the reason suppression matters; pre-rename Muli -> genuine /s/ files), so only the metadata endpoint classifies. NSubstitute auto-wraps `Returns(value)` for Task<T> methods, so the async catalog stubs stayed one-liners. NUnit runs [Explicit] tests when a --filter matches them by name — the live canary (GoogleFontsCatalogEndpointCanaryTests) executed under `FullyQualifiedName~Theme` and PASSED 2026-07-31, re-verifying JSON-200/404/case-sensitivity. ThemeCssBuilderTests' case-insensitive-match test had to be INVERTED (ordinal now): a case-folded match would fabricate an answer the catalogue never gave.

Files: clio/Theming/{GoogleFontsCatalog,FontImportBuilder,ThemeCssBuilder}.cs, clio/BindingsModule.cs, clio/Command/Theming/BuildThemeCommand.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/BuildThemeTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Resources/ThemingGuidanceResource.cs, clio/docs/commands/build-theme.md, clio/help/en/build-theme.txt, spec/adr/adr-ENG-93985-google-fonts-availability.md (new), clio.tests/Theming/{GoogleFontsCatalogTests,ThemeCssBuilderTests}.cs, clio.tests/Command/BuildThemeCommandTests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/BuildThemeToolTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/BuildThemeToolE2ETests.cs; toolkit repo skills/creatio-branding-orchestrator/SKILL.md.

Impact: one build instead of build->warn->confirm->rebuild. Full Unit suite green 7109/0/23 (net8.0) after all review rounds; live canary green. Post-review fixes (creatio-code-review, same day): (1) the availability memo moved from a per-instance field on the transient typed client (where it could never hit across calls) into a singleton IGoogleFontsAvailabilityCache shared by transient catalogs — ICurrentUserCultureCache shape; (2) probe uses HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead (verdict needs only status+Content-Type); (3) FontImportBuilder.ValidateFamily now runs BEFORE the probe in ResolveFontAvailability so unvalidated caller input never reaches the outbound URL. Second (full 5-lens) review pass fixes: mixed faulted+definitive probe test pins per-family fault isolation; cache evicts expired entries on hit (internal EntryCount for tests); LookupAsync self-canonicalizes via CollapseWhitespace(family.Trim()); ValidateFamily caps family length at 100; GoogleFontsDiRegistrationTests pins singleton-cache/transient-catalog lifetimes; orphaned LegacyAliases comment moved; intercepting-proxy-404 recorded as accepted risk in the ADR consequences. Third (full 5-lens) review pass fixes: the Google Fonts probe is now HOISTED OUT of the MCP execution lock — BuildThemeTool.ExecuteWithCleanLog() with no options takes McpToolExecutionLock.SharedFallbackKey (process-wide, shared by every env-less tool), so up to 3s of network sat inside it and, since Unverified is never cached, re-paid on every call from a firewalled host; the tool now calls the public BuildThemeCommand.ResolveFontAvailability BEFORE the lock (narrow ArgumentException catch for INVALID_FONT_FAMILY) and passes the verdicts in via an optional probedFontAvailability parameter threaded through the settings-aware overloads; RequestedFamilies normalizes internally so the pre-lock keys match. Also: bare catch(Exception) around Task.WhenAll replaced by a non-faulting ContinueWith + per-task Exception observation (the log-only advisory that bypassed the warnings channel is gone); LookupAsync enforces the family grammar+100-char cap itself (FontImportBuilder.IsValidFamily) instead of trusting callers; the availability cache gained a hard MaxEntries=512 bound with an expired-entry sweep; the family-name contract is now documented in help/docs/tool descriptions and SKILL.md no longer claims fonts never fail the build; ADR flipped to Accepted + spec/sprint-status.yaml entry added; DI test moved its static-FileSystem mutation inside try/finally and builds with ValidateOnBuild/ValidateScopes; new coverage for the probe client guards (budget/UA/no-redirect), 3xx and no-content verdicts, invalid/over-length families issuing no request, cache capacity, the MCP Unverified warning channel, probe-once-per-call and the malformed-family failure at the tool boundary; duplicate fault-isolation test replaced by the mirror-slot case; all new assertions carry AGENTS.md-mandated because. Fourth (full 5-lens) review pass fixes: hoisting the probe had put it BEFORE css-class-name and version/environment validation, flipping MCP error precedence and sending caller font names outbound on requests that could never build — replaced by a new public BuildThemeCommand.TryResolveFontAvailability that normalizes+validates first (RejectAmbiguousVersionSource extracted so both entry points reject in the same order) and only then probes, so the tool no longer needs its own ArgumentException catch. Also: probe handler gained UseCookies=false (matching the two adjacent hardened registrations — a pooled consent/NID cookie would otherwise be replayed across every caller and tenant); the family-name contract was stated STRICTER than the code on four surfaces (padding and internal whitespace are normalized, not rejected) and is now one sentence across SKILL.md, help, docs, both MCP arg descriptions and ThemingGuidanceResource; probedFontAvailability documented on both public overloads; IsValidFamily null-handling made explicit; DI fixture marked [NonParallelizable] (fourth fixture mutating the process-wide SettingsRepository.FileSystem static under Parallelizable(Fixtures)); the "both remote steps run before the lock" comment corrected — the tenant version probe still runs under the shared lock (pre-existing, now documented instead of denied). New coverage: MCP-surface normalization canary (the CLI test is idempotent-blind), workspace-write probe-once canary, validation-before-probe canary, and the cache sweep/refresh-at-capacity branches. BMAD artifacts added: spec/stories/story-google-fonts-availability-1.md + spec/test-plans/tp-google-fonts-availability.md, sprint entry fixed to file:/test_plan:/note:. Fifth review pass (3 of 5 lenses; security/bug-risk hit the session limit) fixes: the ContinueWith that settles the probes used the 2-arg overload, so an already-completed set (every cache hit) still queued a thread-pool work item the caller then blocked on — switched to the 4-arg ExecuteSynchronously overload; the BindingsModule comment still justified the budget with "the build runs under the MCP per-tenant lock", wrong on both halves (it is the process-wide SharedFallbackKey, and the probe is no longer inside it) — rewritten; ResolveVersion(options) kept a verbatim third copy of the version-ambiguity rule — now calls RejectAmbiguousVersionSource like the other two entry points; ResolveFontAvailability was public for a caller that never materialized (the tool calls TryResolveFontAvailability) — made private, stale rationale deleted; both probing TryBuildTheme overloads now disclose the network step in their summary; the CLI [Option] HelpText/summaries carry the family-name contract like every other surface. New coverage: UseCookies=false (the fourth probe guard, previously unasserted), the pre-probe version-ambiguity gate, warnings on the workspace-write path (where css/descriptor are omitted so warnings are the only disclosure), and a non-tautological TryGet eviction test (EntryCount==1 held even without the TryRemove). Sixth (full 5-lens) review pass fixes: AC-7 had claimed "a request that cannot build sends nothing outbound", which three lenses showed is false — TryResolveFontAvailability validates only the request SHAPE (css-class-name, version/environment pair), while colour parsing and the workspace/package existence checks stay inside the build, so those requests do probe first; the claim was narrowed in all three places it appeared (tool comment, command summary, story AC-7) and the ACTUAL order is now pinned by a test rather than implied away (hoisting those checks was judged scope expansion, and the filesystem ones mutate the singleton RootPath). Also: a canary now proves the probe runs BEFORE the shared lock is taken (the test holds McpToolExecutionLock.GetLock(SharedFallbackKey) and asserts the probe still fires — every prior count/precedence assertion would survive moving the call back inside the lambda, so the placement was guarded only by a comment; fixture marked NonParallelizable for it); the loose XML prose about the network step sat between </param> and <returns> as untagged character data and would have been dropped from generated docs — wrapped in <remarks> on all three probing overloads; the removed-argument comment claimed the key would otherwise "fall silently into ExtensionData", false since BuildLegacyAliasError already rejects unknown keys — the pre-check exists for the migration hint, and the comment now says so. New coverage: the rewritten theming guidance clauses (consent gate, fonts.google.com/?query= resolver, could-not-verify + restyle remedy, family-name contract) which are now the ONLY control for that gate since --local-font-families is gone; the AC-5 probe-disclosure sentence in the tool description; and the AC-8 contract in both font argument descriptions. Seventh review pass: docs/McpCapabilityMap.md still told agents "build-theme and advise-theme-palette run offline" and "build a theme offline" — false the moment OpenWorld flipped to true; the file is source-driven from the MCP tool surface but sits outside the working diff, so the staleness was silent. Corrected in all three places, with the fail-open caveat spelled out (it still works without connectivity — import kept + warning). Also: the test plan now lists the lock-placement canary as the ONLY guard against the probe drifting back inside ExecuteWithCleanLog (every other AC-7 test would stay green) and stops understating AC-8 automation; Contain("restyle") was near-tautological (the verb appears three times in the resource, twice in unrelated flow prose) so it now matches "restyle once connectivity is back"; the removed-argument rejection test gained the no-probe assertion its three sibling rejection tests already carried. Eighth pass (whole-tree review against master rather than another delta round) fixes: the availability cache was registered with AddSingleton, but BindingsModule builds a FRESH ServiceCollection and provider on every call and the MCP resolver builds one container per tenant — so "singleton" meant per-container and every rebuild started cold; the instance now lives in a static field that the registration hands out. Unverified went from never-cached to a 30 s transient TTL for the reason above. The toolkit SKILL.md capability gate read a surviving @import as proof the family is published, which fail-open makes false (an unverifiable probe also keeps the import) — it now keys on the absence of a warning naming the family. The capacity-bound assertion could not fail single-threaded and was replaced by a concurrent one. Verified against clio 8.1.0.1006 on ts1-infr-web04/sae_m_seeenu_15821904_0803: mixed Verdana+Inter suppressed only Verdana's import and warned by name, padded "  Open   Sans  " normalized into the import URL, a malformed family failed with INVALID_FONT_FAMILY, the removed argument returned its migration hint over MCP, and build-theme → create-theme registered the theme end to end. ClioRing compatibility reviewed, no Ring-consumed contract changed. Inspected clio-ring/ClioRing.Ipc, clio-ring/ClioRing and clio-ring/ClioRing.Desktop/actions.json: Ring’s consumed surface is get-tool-contract (full catalog and per-tool detail), list-environments, and clio-run dispatch of deploy-creatio / describe-environment / preflight tools. It never invokes build-theme, create-theme or advise-theme-palette — every "theme" hit under clio-ring is Avalonia UI theming (FluentTheme, ThemeVariant), so the removed argument, its three rejected wire spellings and the pre-lock validation error envelope are unreachable from Ring. The OpenWorld flip is likewise invisible to Ring: ClioIpcModels.ClioCatalogEntry projects exactly Name, Purpose, ContractAvailable, Resident and Destructive — there is no OpenWorld field; Resident comes from McpCoreToolProfile.IsResident(name), which does not list build-theme (long-tail, not in tools/list), and Destructive comes from the tool attribute, unchanged (the attribute diff is OpenWorld false->true and nothing else). The one Ring-consumed field this change does touch is the catalog Purpose string for build-theme, which now discloses the probe; Ring surfaces it as opaque display text and branches on none of its content. ## 2026-07-10 - ENG-93089: implement parallel-contention guard + contention reclassify/retry (A+B+C)
Context: Implemented the ADR (spec/adr/adr-create-app-section-parallel-guard.md) for ENG-93089 on branch feature/ENG-93089-create-app-section-parallel-guard. All 5 BMAD stories in one branch.
Decision: (A) New ISectionCreateSerializationGuard/SectionCreateSerializationGuard (clio/Command/ApplicationSectionCreateSerializationGuard.cs) — DI SINGLETON (AddSingleton in BindingsModule.cs ~L290) owning a ConcurrentDictionary<string,SemaphoreSlim> keyed env+app-code (lower-cased, joined by U+241F); Run<T>(env,appCode,waitTimeout,work) does a bounded Wait, degrades to best-effort+WriteWarning on timeout, releases in finally. Injected into ApplicationSectionCreateService (extra ctor param; S107 note updated). CreateSection now wraps ONLY insert→readback in guard.Run(request.ApplicationCode, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(insertTimeoutMs), ...); prep reads stay outside. (B) New enum member ApplicationSectionCreateFailureClass.Contention + ToWireValue "contention". Replaced EnsureInsertSucceeded with ClassifyInsertResponse returning Success|Contention (throws terminal ServerError for non-JSON/empty/DETAILED rejection); IsDetailLessInsertRejection = null/empty or "InsertQuery failed"(.). New InsertWithContentionRecovery: first TryInsertAttempt → on contention, TryVerifySectionExists (existing helper, Id-matched) → true=readback(no retry), null=throw Contention(sectionCreated=null), false=Thread.Sleep(PollDelay 2s)+one more TryInsertAttempt → still contention → throw Contention(sectionCreated=false). BuildContentionFailure + ContentionRetryGuidance constant. (C) [Description] on ApplicationTool.ApplicationSectionCreate + args; AppModeling/ExistingAppMaintenance guidance error-class bullets (+sequential bullet); ToolContractGetTool.cs error-class field enum; help/en + docs/commands/create-app-section.md (Concurrency section + contention row/troubleshooting); docs/McpCapabilityMap.md. clio.mcp.e2e concurrent-create scenario (McpE2E.Sandbox, AllowDestructive+seeded-env gated, 3 parallel calls one session, asserts no error-class=contention / no "InsertQuery failed" / all succeed + cleanup).
Discovery: (1) Flipped 3 existing ApplicationSectionCreateServiceTests (detail-less body was ServerError→now Contention); the "Rejected"/detailed-message tests correctly STAY ServerError (SetUpInsertTimeoutCaptureMocks returns "Rejected" = detailed = terminal, so budget-capture tests unaffected). (2) SelectQueryHelper.ExecuteSelectQuery THROWS on null/empty response → in flipped tests the unconfigured verify readback → TryVerifySectionExists returns null → no retry, no 2s sleep (only AC-04/AC-06 tests, which configure empty-rows readback, incur the 2s PollDelay). (3) Build/test MUST use `-o <temp> -f net10.0` — clio/bin/Debug/net10.0/clio.dll is locked by the live plugin MCP server (.NET Host); from the temp dir, ReadmeChecker (AppContext.BaseDirectory/../../../../clio/Commands.md) + VisibleCommands/HelpDirectory/DocsDirectory canonical-artifact + materialization/workspace fixture tests all fail on path resolution — a PRE-EXISTING temp-dir artifact set (same before my changes), NOT real. ## 2026-07-10 - ENG-93089: session analysis — create-app-section "InsertQuery failed" under parallel/contention
Context: Analyzed two Codex Desktop rollout JSONL sessions (2026-05-27, toolkit ai-driven-app-creation) in the context of ENG-93089. Task = prevent/recover from opaque "InsertQuery failed." when create-app-section runs in parallel. No code changes yet — scoping only.
Discovery: (1) REPRO confirmed in session 019e6982 (user a.shykova): 3 create-app-section calls against ONE app (UsrClient) started within 52ms of each other (13:24:02.235/.286/.287) — all three returned `{"success":false,"error":"InsertQuery failed."}` after only 36/36/55s. (2) RECOVERY: same payloads re-run SEQUENTIALLY ~27min later (13:51:06, 13:52:46) both SUCCEEDED in 93.3s / 102.6s. So parallel→fail, sequential→success = lock/contention, not bad input; ~93-102s/section makes overlap likely. (3) Failed calls returned FASTER (36-55s) than successful (93-103s) — contention aborts insert mid-way; usable signal for retry heuristic. (4) Sibling session 019e68d6 (a.voloshchenko) created UsrCustomer but never reached parallel section creation → no repro (clean control). CODE FINDINGS (master): (a) NO serialization/lock anywhere in ApplicationSectionCreateCommand.cs; no SemaphoreSlim/mutex. (b) The async MCP tool ApplicationTool.ApplicationSectionCreate runs via McpProgressHeartbeat.RunWithProgressAndDeadlineAsync and does NOT go through BaseTool's `lock(CommandExecutionLock)` — so the global McpToolExecutionLock never serializes section creation (and couldn't: lock can't span await). (c) Even if it did, the toolkit calls clio via scripts/mcp_client.py = fresh `clio mcp-server` PROCESS per call → a static in-process lock is useless across processes. (d) MISCLASSIFICATION: detail-less `InsertQuery failed` → EnsureInsertSucceeded throws ApplicationSectionCreateException with class=ServerError + ServerErrorRetryGuidance ("retrying will most likely fail again") — the OPPOSITE of the evidence (serialized retry works). ClassifyInsertFailure never sees it (it's a success=false body, not an exception). TryVerifySectionExists helper already exists → retry-with-verify is feasible.
Files: (analysis only) sessions in ~/Downloads/rollout-2026-05-27T{08-57-14-019e6982,12-49-20-019e68d6}*.jsonl; code read: clio/Command/ApplicationSectionCreateCommand.cs, ApplicationSectionCreateFailure.cs, McpServer/Tools/{ApplicationTool.cs,BaseTool.cs,McpToolExecutionLock.cs}
Impact: Fix design fork for ENG-93089 — (A) in-process async serialization (SemaphoreSlim keyed by env+application-code) fixes the common single-server parallel-batch repro but NOT cross-process; (B) auto-retry-once-with-verify on detail-less InsertQuery failed is the robust cross-process fallback but must re-check existence to avoid duplicate/"already bound"; (C) mandatory [Description]/guidance "do not create sections in parallel" + clio.mcp.e2e scenario. Recommend A+C as primary, B as complementary. BMAD: non-trivial → ADR before code.
## 2026-07-14 – ENG-93088 odata-read masks Web API routing errors as success
Context: rollout 2026-05-27 session (a studio sandbox) showed `odata-read` on a freshly-created custom lookup (`UsrCustomerStatus`) returning `success:true, count:1, value:{Message, MessageDetail}` — Creatio served an ASP.NET Web API 404 routing body with HTTP 200, and `ParseODataResponse` fell through to the single-entity path (no `value` wrapper) and wrapped the error as data.
Decision: extend `ODataResponseError.TryDetect` (shared by odata-read + odata-create) with a THIRD branch after the OData-v4 `error` and ASP.NET `ExceptionType` branches: fire when root is `{Message(+MessageDetail)}` and has NO other member (`HasNonRoutingErrorMembers`). Append `UnregisteredEntityHint` (compile+restart guidance) ONLY when `MessageDetail` is present (the routing discriminator) — a bare `{Message}` is surfaced verbatim to avoid misattributing an unrelated error. Also added a guidance anti-pattern to `ToolContractGetTool.BuildODataRead()`.
Discovery: (1) branch is false-positive-safe because odata-read always hits the collection endpoint (`odata/{e}?$top=`), so a real body always carries `@odata.context`/`value` → `HasNonRoutingErrorMembers` true. Load-bearing assumption: default OData metadata (NOT `metadata=none`); pinned in a code comment. (2) E2E: extended `RuntimeDetectionStubServer` with `ODataRoutingErrorEntity` to serve the masked 200 body; registered env via reg-web-app (auto-detects .NET Framework → `/0/odata/` prefix) then called odata-read through the real mcp-server. Category `McpE2E.Sandbox` (needs node; not in CI).
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/ODataResponseError.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/ToolContractGetTool.cs (BuildODataRead anti-pattern), clio.tests/Command/McpServer/ODataReadToolTests.cs (+3), clio.tests/Command/McpServer/ODataCreateToolTests.cs (+1), clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Creatio/RuntimeDetectionStubServer.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/ODataReadRoutingErrorE2ETests.cs (new).
Verify: OData read+create unit = 31 pass (net8+net10); ToolContractGetTool = 103 pass; routing E2E = 1 pass (net10). No CLI docs (odata-read is MCP-only). ClioRing does not consume odata-read (grep clean).
Impact: odata-* verification failures are no longer masked as success; a freshly-created-but-uncompiled lookup now returns success:false with a compile/restart hint instead of reading as a data gap. Reuse the `RuntimeDetectionStubServer.ODataRoutingErrorEntity` pattern for future OData response-parsing E2E.

## 2026-07-24 - watch-compilation: shipped via #960, then a TeamCity-driven follow-up fix

Context: follow-up to the watch-compilation command (new experimental CLI+MCP command observing Creatio's CompilationHistory table to detect externally-triggered compiles, never triggering one itself; see prior entry if still present, or clio/Command/WatchCompilationCommand.cs / clio/Common/{CompilationSettleTracker,PollRetryPolicy,CompilationHistoryPoller}.cs for the design). This entry covers what happened after the initial PR opened: a review cycle, then a real production report, each producing a real behavior fix.

Decision (PR #960 review, all three addressed in one follow-up commit before merge): (1) Codex P1/critical - `CompilationSettleTracker.SeedFromBaseline` seeded the quiet-window clock (`_lastActivityAt`) from `baseline.CreatedOn` instead of wall-clock `now`; a baseline older than the 45s window made the very first empty poll look instantly settled, defeating detection of a compile triggered moments before the watch started. Fixed: always seed from `now`; baseline is only used for error/marker carryover and as the query cutoff. (2) Codex P2 - the command is `[FeatureToggle("watch-compilation")]`-gated off by default, but I had added it to `Commands.md`/`WikiAnchors.txt`/`docs/commands/watch-compilation.md`, violating AGENTS.md L469-473 ("omitted from generated public docs" while gated). Fixed: `Hidden = true` on the `[Verb]` (satisfies `BaseCommandTests<T>`'s README check via its own Hidden short-circuit), removed the two index entries, deleted the standalone doc page; kept `help/en/watch-compilation.txt` since it's the internal `-H` source and already correctly runtime-gated. (3) SonarCloud S3776 - `Execute` had Cognitive Complexity 26 (15 allowed); extracted `TryGetBaseline`/`RunPollLoop`/`PollOnceAndObserve`/`ReportOutcome`, no behavior change.

Discovery (live, cec, `compile-configuration --all` run concurrently with `watch-compilation`): found TWO real bugs the unit tests (fabricated data) could never have caught. (a) The poll loop lacked the same `seen.Add(record.Id)` Guid-dedup `CompilationHistoryPoller.Poll` already has - a real CompilationHistory table re-returned the same row across rounds, perpetually resetting the settle clock, so the watch never converged; fixed by adding the same dedup guard around `PollOnce`. (b) The original 8s `BaseQuietWindowSeconds` was far too small for two measured real gaps: ~18s between the HTTP trigger and the first row ever written, and ~31-33s between an ordinary package finishing and the next (slow, aggregate `Terrasoft.Configuration.Dev.csproj`) project's own row - both caused false "finished" verdicts. Unified into one 45s base window applied unconditionally (not just before the first row), still scaled up further by `DurationScaleFactor` for even slower observed projects.

Decision (production report via TeamCity, after #960 already merged): a real CI-triggered full compile on a different environment produced ONE package row (`CecDataPackage.csproj`) then 45s quiet, and watch-compilation declared "cannot confirm a full successful finish" (the old exit-1 "unconfirmed" branch) while the actual full compile was still running. User's framing: in a CI/TeamCity trigger context we already know a full compile started, so a quiet gap without the `ODataEntities` marker should read as "still compiling something slower than seen so far", not "probably done, unconfirmed". Fixed at the root: `CompilationSettleTracker.IsSettled` now NEVER reports true when activity was observed but the marker hasn't appeared, regardless of elapsed quiet time - only genuinely-zero-activity or marker-observed can settle. This removed the old exit-1 "unconfirmed" branch entirely: exit 1 now means only real (non-warning) errors; exit 2 (gave up) covers both "nothing ever happened" and "activity but marker never confirmed", with `GiveUp()`'s message now saying which.

Discovery (git/process, worth remembering for future PRs on this repo): pushing a branch update after `git fetch`-rejection can mean the PR already got AUTO-MERGED (this repo has auto-merge enabled per-PR) and GitHub auto-deleted the head branch - `git fetch origin <branch>` failing with "couldn't find remote ref" is the tell. Always check `gh`/API PR state (`state`, `merged`, `merged_at`) before assuming a stale local branch is still open; don't try to resurrect a merged PR's branch name, cherry-pick the new-only commits onto a fresh branch off current `origin/master` instead. Also: `gh` in this environment is authenticated to `creatio.ghe.com`, NOT `github.com` - `gh pr view`/`gh pr create` against this repo fail with 401; fall back to the public GitHub REST API via plain `curl` for reads (works unauthenticated on this public repo) and tell the user to open the PR themselves for writes.

Files: clio/Common/{CompilationSettleTracker,CompilationHistoryPoller,PollRetryPolicy}.cs, clio/Command/WatchCompilationCommand.cs, clio/help/en/watch-compilation.txt, clio.tests/Common/{CompilationSettleTrackerTests,PollRetryPolicyTests}.cs, clio.tests/Command/WatchCompilationCommand.Tests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/PassthroughToolClassificationRegistry.cs (NotApplicable entry), clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/WatchCompilationTool.cs.

Impact: #960 merged into master 2026-07-23 (merge commit 0553b7fb). The TeamCity-driven marker-gating fix is NOT yet merged - pushed to `fix/watch-compilation-marker-gating` (commit a0fcb0a9, based on current master), full targeted suite green on net8.0/net10.0 (6199/0/18), needs a fresh PR opened manually (compare URL: github.com/Advance-Technologies-Foundation/clio/pull/new/fix/watch-compilation-marker-gating). Old `feature/watch-compilation` local branch is stale (fully merged or superseded) and safe to delete.

## 2026-07-09 - ENG-93208 B1: bearer passthrough dropped in child-container connection sites
Context: Adversarial review of mcp-http credential-passthrough (stories 3-7) found a confirmed cross-identity/privilege-escalation bug. ToolCommandResolver.ResolvePassthrough builds an ephemeral bearer EnvironmentSettings (AccessToken set, Login/Password/ClientId null) and a child container via `new BindingsModule().Register(settings)`, but every Creatio-connection site in RegisterActiveEnvironmentServices (and the SysSettingsManager Func factory just above) read ONLY Login/Password/ClientId and defaulted null creds to "Supervisor"/"Supervisor" — so a bearer request silently authenticated as Supervisor and NoReauthExecutor was never used.
Decision: Added a bearer-first, fail-closed branch (keyed on `!string.IsNullOrEmpty(AccessToken)`) at all 4 child-container sites in BindingsModule.cs: (1) SysSettingsManager Func factory data provider (~733); (2) IDataProvider/LazyDataProvider RemoteDataProvider (~750); (3) lazyCreatioClient — covers both the CreatioClient singleton and the IApplicationClient adapter (~756); (4) IApplicationClient adapter now `sp =>` and wires `sp.GetRequiredService<IReauthExecutor>()` (the DI'd NoReauthExecutor) on the bearer leg only. Bearer ctors used: `new RemoteDataProvider(uri, accessToken, isNetCore)` and `new CreatioClient(uri, accessToken, isNetCore)`. Non-bearer login/password/OAuth branches preserved byte-for-byte; Supervisor default stays reachable only for the no-credential bootstrap case. ApplicationClientFactory (story 3) untouched — NOT redundant overall (it builds clients for explicit foreign environments passed at call time, e.g. ApplicationManager cross-env, package install); its bearer branch is bypassed only for the child-container direct-injection path.
Discovery: (1) `Creatio.Client.CreatioClient` fields for identity assertions: `_oauthToken` (bearer), `_userName`/`_userPassword` (basic). Bearer ctor is `.ctor(string,string,bool)`. (2) ATF `RemoteDataProvider` bearer ctor `.ctor(string,string,bool)` DOES wrap a reachable `Creatio.Client.CreatioClient` — a reflective type-navigated graph walk (not hardcoded ATF names) finds it, so the token is observable end-to-end. (3) CLIO005 shows as a warning building each project alone (0 errors) but the RTK-wrapped combined build once mislabeled warnings as errors — spurious.
Files: clio/BindingsModule.cs (4 sites), clio.tests/Command/McpServer/CredentialPassthroughClientIdentityTests.cs (new, 3 fail-first tests)
Impact: Multi-tenant isolation now enforced at the composition root; the fail-first test locks it (all 3 fail pre-fix reproducing Supervisor/token-drop, pass post-fix). Full Unit suite green 5080/0/35. Residual: nested-ternary sites may draw Sonar S3358 in CI.

## 2026-06-19 - Confluence "Backend designer" page: added Build & modify contract diagram
Context: Asked to add a process create/modify contract to the TER Confluence page 4752572418 ("Backend designer — architecture & delivery options"); chose a PlantUML class diagram + a routes/verbs mini-table, placed as a new section 3 after the sequence diagram (sections 3-8 renumbered to 4-9).
Decision: Render the contract as a UML class diagram in the same `plantumlcloud` (puml4cc) macro the page already uses, so it stays editable on-page and matches the existing sequence diagram's style. Contract fields sourced from clio/Command/CreateBusinessProcessCommand.cs + ModifyBusinessProcessCommand.cs (descriptor: elements/flows/parameters/mappings; modify ops: addElement/removeElement/addFlow/removeFlow/addParameter/addMapping; routes from ServiceUrlBuilder KnownRoute.BuildProcess/ModifyProcess).
Discovery: The Confluence `plantumlcloud` macro stores its diagram in `data-parameters` macroParams.data.value as **Base64( raw-DEFLATE( encodeURIComponent(plantuml-text) ) )** with `compressed:"true"` (NOT PlantUML.com's 6-bit alphabet, which uses `~1`/HUFFMAN and a different charset). Verified by decoding the page's existing sequence-diagram blob with .NET DeflateStream (raw, nowrap) -> got `%40startuml...`. To author a new one: build PlantUML, `[Uri]::EscapeDataString`, raw-deflate, `[Convert]::ToBase64String`. Validate PlantUML *syntax* separately via plantuml.com using its native 6-bit encoder on the BARE `/svg/<enc>` path (the `~1` prefix routes to the wrong decoder and errors "does not look like HUFFMAN data"). MCP `updateConfluencePage` replaces the WHOLE body and is provided inline by the model -> long base64 blobs and large prose are an easy place to slip; I duplicated a section on the first publish. Mitigation that worked: assemble body in a scratch file, decode both macro blobs from the file to confirm before publishing, then re-verify by re-fetching the live page.
Files: Confluence page 4752572418 (v13); no repo files changed. Source of truth read: clio/Command/CreateBusinessProcessCommand.cs, clio/Command/ModifyBusinessProcessCommand.cs, clio/Common/ServiceUrlBuilder.cs, clio/docs/commands/{create,modify}-business-process.md.
Impact: Recipe + validation/verification flow for embedding/editing PlantUML in Creatio Confluence pages is reusable for the other ENG-90883 research pages. Key gotcha: macro encoding is base64+deflate+urlencode, distinct from plantuml.com's encoding.

## 2026-06-30 - ENG-91555: new-container guidance in page-modification (+ PR #789 review correction)
Context: ENG-91555 asked to document the "inline items in new container" constraint in the page-modification MCP guide (root case: session 7ca711a1, runtime `Item "X" is not a container for other items` after inserting new ExpansionPanels). Delivered as PR #789. PR review (tetiana-moshon, Major/CHANGES_REQUESTED) then flagged the first cut as wrong.
Decision: Reviewer was RIGHT — corrected the block. Verified authoritatively: related-list RelatedListGuidanceResource.cs:188 + :48-54 attribute that exact runtime error to a MISSING `items: []` slot on an inserted container ("#1 detail footgun"); get-component-info crt.ExpansionPanel's canonical example inserts the container via parentName WITH `items: []` initialized. So the true root cause is the un-initialized content slot, NOT "chain-nesting", and separate parentName child inserts ARE supported when the container initializes its slot.
Discovery: Final block: heading "Inserting a NEW container — its content slot MUST be initialized"; removed the false chain-nesting mechanism and the blanket prohibition on separate parentName inserts; WRONG example = container inserted without its slot; CORRECT(inline) + CORRECT(separate) both valid; cross-ref related-list / get-component-info composite; config-node clarification (RC-1, Alexandr-Kravchuk) folded into prose. clio carries NO component descriptions — type/slot/shape deferred to get-component-info. The plugin clio MCP server is launched as bare `clio mcp-server` from .mcp.json (active plugin version 1.3.0 cache copy), which resolves via an npm shim to a different repo (C:\Projects\adaclio ... net8.0) — so a freshly-built local clio is NOT served until that .mcp.json is repointed to the absolute net10.0 dll AND Claude Code is restarted; get-guidance page-modification returning "Unknown guidance" is the tell that the wrong binary is serving.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Resources/PageModificationGuidanceResource.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/GuidanceGetToolTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/GuidanceGetToolE2ETests.cs
Impact: Validated dotnet test --filter "Category=Unit&Module=McpServer" (1460 passed). Lesson: a guide that names a runtime error MUST agree with every other guide naming the same error — cross-check the error string across GuidanceCatalog resources before asserting a root cause.

## 2026-07-08 - Investigation: Team_Atf_ClioMcpE2eTests master-branch failures
Context: Asked to investigate failures on TeamCity job Team_Atf_ClioMcpE2eTests, focus on runs where the build param BranchNameClio = master. (VCS branch column shows "trunk" for all; the clio branch under test is the BranchNameClio resulting-property, checked via /app/rest/builds/id:<id>/resulting-properties/BranchNameClio.)
Discovery: Four recent master failures split into TWO distinct modes. MODE A — test-host HANG: runs 15688937 & 15688144 (~2026-07-06) both aborted identically with "The active test run was aborted. Reason: Test host process crashed" after --blame-hang-timeout 3m. Hang-dump process tree is testhost -> cmd -> clio in BOTH: an orphaned `clio` CLI/MCP subprocess (child of a cmd child of testhost) never exits, so after 3 min inactivity the whole test host is killed and only ~247-250/408 tests run (rest never execute). The stall lands right after the PageBusinessRuleToolE2ETests `BusinessRuleCreate_Should_Bind_*_And_Report_Invalid_Environment` batch (methods themselves Passed in 3-40ms; the leaked process is what hangs) — the *_Report_Invalid_Environment tests spawn a clio process against an invalid env that apparently never times out/terminates. This is the real recurring bug. MODE B — assertion failures (flaky/env), the two MOST RECENT runs 15693316 & 15693193 (~2026-07-07): different tests fail each run -> environmental, not one regression. 15693316: ApplicationGetInfo_..._After_SchemaSync (sync-schemas success=False) + PageCreateTool_..._Dashboard_With_Optional_Properties (get-page Bundle null). 15693193: CreateWorkspace_..._Invalid_Environment_Key + _Directory_Is_Omitted (create-workspace exit code 1, both new). Each run is a different clio commit (moving master), reinforcing flaky-not-regression for Mode B.
Files: (investigation only) logs saved to scratchpad log15688937.txt / log15688144.txt
Impact: Master is currently RED (latest run 15693316 failed). Priority fix = Mode A orphaned-clio-process hang (deterministic host crash, blocks whole suite): make the *_Report_Invalid_Environment E2E paths enforce a process timeout / guaranteed kill+dispose of the spawned clio child so it can't outlive the test. Mode B needs per-test retry/quarantine or root-causing the flaky env (schema-sync / create-workspace against the shared stand).

## 2026-07-06 - ENG-92127: platform interpretation-validation pre-save gate (clioprocessbuilder)
Context: Manual designer testing of ENG-92127 found a self-referential parameter mapping (Parameter 2 = [#Parameter 2#]) is correctly rejected on the ContractProcessSchema save ("circular dependency for the parameter"); clioprocessbuilder's own build/modify path did NOT run that validation, so an AI-built process could bypass it. Work is in the ProcessBuilder repo (C:\Projects\workspace\ProcessBuilder), NOT clio.
Decision: Added a pre-save gate. New IProcessSchemaValidator/ProcessSchemaValidator (namespace ClioProcessBuilder) calls the PUBLIC platform seam ProcessSchemaManager.GetProcessValidationResult(schema, userConnection) and throws on HasErrors (joined ErrorMessages); the existing orchestrator catch surfaces it as response.ErrorMessage (build rolls back; modify releases the design session). Wired into ProcessDesigner.BuildProcess (before Save) and ModifyProcess (before SaveEdited). AUGMENTS (does not replace) the per-mapping ParameterTypeCompatibility guard: the platform type rule (ValidateParameterBindingValueTypes) is .NET-ValueType + implicit-cast based (accepts Email↔Phone, Date↔Time, Integer→Money, lookup-with-different-object) — laxer than the designer mapping-window rule the custom guard mirrors — and our-accept ⊆ platform-accept, so they layer cleanly (user chose augment after I confirmed this).
Discovery: (1) GetProcessValidationResult is NOT called by SaveSchema — the designer's ContractProcessSchema layer calls it separately, so the direct SaveSchema path must call it explicitly; the ProcessSchemaManager override short-circuits IsEmbedded → empty result. (2) For a Script source (clio's `expression`) the platform runs ValidateExpression at save (compile check), so once DEPLOYED a malformed expression fails at save, not just runtime — the ProcessModelingGuidanceResource "expression UNVALIDATED / RUNTIME-only" wording (line ~197) becomes wrong; deferred that reword to the package release (guidance describes deployed-package behavior). (3) Package sources under Files/src/cs are SDK-auto-globbed (Files/-rooted); LangVersion 7.3; ProcessDesigner is built via ActivatorUtilities (new ctor dep auto-resolved) but three TEST sites use `new ProcessDesigner(...)` and needed the arg. (4) ProcessMappingServiceTests.ApplyMapping_ShouldAssignConstantValue_WhenValueProvided is a PRE-EXISTING FLAKY test (shared/order-dependent DataValueTypeManager via ProcessParameterValueValidator.ValidateConstantValue): failed once then passed 5× on identical source and passes on master — spawned a task chip to stabilize it.
Files: packages/clioprocessbuilder/Files/src/cs/Validation/IProcessSchemaValidator.cs (new) + ProcessSchemaValidator.cs (new), packages/clioprocessbuilder/Files/src/ClioProcessBuilderApp.cs, packages/clioprocessbuilder/Files/src/cs/ProcessDesigner.cs, tests/clioprocessbuilder/{ProcessDesignerOrchestratorTests,ProcessDesignerSecurityTests,ProcessDesignerRoundTripTests,ClioProcessBuilderAppTests}.cs, spec/eng-92127-server-validation/eng-92127-server-validation-plan.md (new) — all in the ProcessBuilder repo.
Impact: clioprocessbuilder build/modify now enforces the same interpretation validation the designer runs on save. Build clean; 248/248 ProcessBuilder unit tests green. MCP reviewed: tools already relay the platform ErrorMessage (contracts unchanged) so no tool change; guidance reword deferred to package release. STILL PENDING: E2E on a stand (deploy the rebuilt package; verify a self-map/cycle is rejected and a valid process still builds).

Context: ModifyBusinessProcess_Should_EditExistingProcess (clio.mcp.e2e) hardcoded the signalStart signal entity "UsrTestRunButton" in BuildOperations(); that custom object exists on only one specific stand, so on any other environment the addElement op fails and the whole batch atomically rolls back — the test was non-portable (the describe read-back, not the weak success assertions, is what caught it).
Decision: Swap the signal entity to the base "Contact" object (present on every Creatio), keeping "on":"save". A signalStart binds to a real EntitySchema, so the referenced object must exist in the target SysSchema; Contact makes the fixture environment-independent. Left the illustrative "e.g. UsrTestRunButton" in ProcessModelingGuidanceResource as-is (it is a doc example, not an executable reference).
Discovery: (1) Runtime settings — registered environments AND the `features` map — load from %LOCALAPPDATA%\creatio\clio\appsettings.json (confirmed via `clio info --settings-file`), NOT the repo clio/appsettings.json; the repo file is only the shipped defaults/seed, so a local `features.process-designer:true` there must not be committed (it would flip the experimental default ON). (2) The E2E resolves the sibling clio\bin\<cfg>\<tfm>\clio.exe; when the live MCP-server clio locks the Debug binary, build test-only with `-p:BuildProjectReferences=false` and run `--no-build` to reuse the existing binary instead of killing the process. (3) ProcessDesignerE2EGate skips (Assert.Ignore, not fail) unless features.process-designer is enabled in the home appsettings.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/ModifyBusinessProcessToolE2ETests.cs
Impact: Live-verified passing on a reachable stand with the process-designer package in both Release and Debug/net10.0. Future process-designer E2E fixtures should use base entities (Contact) for signal/reference schemas to stay portable across stands.

## 2026-06-25 - Scope chart-widget validation to the environment platform version
Context: ChartWidgetValidation hardcoded ComponentRegistryClient.LatestVersion when loading the catalog; the registry-driven crt.ChartWidget validation should run against the target environment's component set, not always 'latest'.
Decision: Split by whether the tool has an environment. ChartWidgetValidation.ValidateAsync/ResolveTypeDefinitionsAsync now take a requestedVersion, normalise it (blank/unparseable -> latest, else 3-part Major.Minor.Patch) and pass it to catalog.LoadAsync instead of the LatestVersion constant (fail-open preserved). validate-page (no environment) gets an explicit optional `version` MCP arg — the agent passes get-component-info's resolvedTargetVersion. sync-pages and update-page (already have environment-name) do NOT get a version arg; instead they resolve the platform version FROM their environment via IPlatformVersionResolverFactory + ISettingsRepository (the same probe get-component-info uses) and feed it to the validator. NOTE (design correction mid-task): an earlier pass added the `version` arg to all three tools; the user corrected it — the save tools must derive the version from the environment they already target, not take a redundant arg. The two resolver deps were added as OPTIONAL ctor params (= null) on PageSyncTool/PageUpdateTool so DI still injects the registered services in production while ~15 existing unit-test constructions stay untouched; the resolution helper is fail-soft (null deps / bad env / probe failure -> null -> ChartWidgetValidation maps to latest). sync-pages skips the probe entirely when validate:false; update-page skips it for mobile bodies (chart validation is web-only).
Discovery: (1) "Latest fallback for a missing per-version registry" is already handled by ComponentRegistryClient.GetAsync (404 -> latest), so only the version string had to be threaded — no client change. (2) validate-page/sync-pages are MCP-only (no [Verb]); update-page is a CLI verb but the `version` arg lives on PageUpdateArgs (MCP), not PageUpdateOptions (CLI), so the CLI verb + its help/docs are unchanged. (3) ToolContractGetTool has no curated arg contract for these three tools. (4) Local build/test is blocked by the live `clio mcp-server` process holding clio\bin\Debug\net10.0 DLLs; build/test into a temp `-o` dir AND pin a single TFM (`-f net10.0`) — clio.tests/clio.mcp.e2e multi-target net8.0;net10.0 and a shared `-o` dir makes the two frameworks clobber each other (this caused 518 phantom test failures until I pinned the TFM).
Docs: deliberately NONE. sync/update version determination is deterministic + internal (the tool derives it from the environment it already targets; the agent neither chooses nor needs to know it), so it warrants no documentation — per the user's explicit call. The only new agent-facing surface, validate-page's optional `version` arg, is self-documented by its `[Description]`. An earlier pass added a sync-pages.md paragraph + a page-modification guidance bullet; both were reverted (net-zero on those files).
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/ChartWidgetValidation.cs, PageValidateTool.cs, PageSyncTool.cs, PageUpdateTool.cs; clio.tests/Command/McpServer/ChartWidgetValidationTests.cs (new), ValidatePageToolTests.cs, PageSyncToolTests.cs, PageUpdateToolBaselineTests.cs; clio.mcp.e2e/PageValidateToolE2ETests.cs, PageSyncToolE2ETests.cs, PageUpdateToolE2ETests.cs
Impact: To validate a clio change while the MCP server is running, use `dotnet test ... -f net10.0 -o <temp>` to dodge both the bin lock and the multi-TFM `-o` collision. Agents should forward get-component-info's resolvedTargetVersion to the page tools' `version` arg so pre-flight (validate-page) and save-time (update-page/sync-pages) chart validation agree on the environment's component set.

## 2026-06-16 - Feature-toggle MCP findings 3-6 + latent registration regression
Context: Fix four IMPORTANT review findings on the experimental feature-toggle system; uncovered a blocking MCP registration bug.
Decision: Did NOT add abstract/open-generic exclusion to McpFeatureToggleFilter - the ModelContextProtocol 1.4.0 SDK INCLUDES such types in its *FromAssembly scan (it iterates methods, not types), so excluding them would BREAK parity. BaseTool<T> carries [McpServerToolType] but has no [McpServerTool] method -> contributes 0 registered tools on both sides. ExperimentalCommand now reuses McpFeatureToggleFilter for all 3 markers (inherit:true) instead of forked inherit:false 2-marker helper. Wired --list (precedence: --list wins, lists and returns). Single-sourced MCP registration in McpFeatureToggleFilter.RegisterEnabledPrimitives, called by both BindingsModule and the parity test.
Discovery: BLOCKING latent bug - BindingsModule's `.WithResources(Type[])`/`.WithTools(Type[], opts)`/`.WithPrompts(Type[], opts)` all bound to the SDK's GENERIC With*<TType>(TType target,...) overload (identity conversion on a Type[] arg beats Type[]->IEnumerable<Type> reference conversion, decided before the generic-vs-nongeneric tiebreaker), registering 0 tools/0 resources/0 prompts. Probe confirmed: PROD shape 0/0/0 vs cast shape 120/86/67. Fix: type the lists as IEnumerable<Type>. The whole MCP surface was silently dead in this feature branch.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/McpFeatureToggleFilter.cs, clio/BindingsModule.cs (~632-645), clio/Command/ExperimentalCommand.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/McpFeatureToggleFilterTests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/ExperimentalToolTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/ExperimentalToolE2ETests.cs, clio/help/en/experimental.txt, clio/docs/commands/experimental.md
Impact: Future MCP registration must pass IEnumerable<Type> (never Type[]) to With*; the parity test now drives the real production seam so the cast cannot be dropped again. The IEnumerable<Type>-overload-binding hazard is the #1 gotcha when touching MCP type-list registration.

## 2026-03-19 00:00 – Push workspace backup investigation

Impact: Future fixes should make backup behavior explicit/configurable and should not rely on `--Safe` for install-time backup control.

Decision: Advised that Docker already caches lines 1-19 as stable layers when the daemon cache is preserved, and recommended either a named base stage / separately tagged intermediate image or BuildKit cache export/import for environments with ephemeral caches.
Discovery: `BuildDockerImageService.CreateBuildContext` always copies the template and `source/` into a temporary context, so repository-root `.dockerignore` rules do not control that staged context; the main invalidation point in the template is `COPY source/ ./`, not the apt/entrypoint layers.

Impact: Future Docker build-performance questions can start from the correct cache boundary in the prod template and distinguish between local layer reuse versus exported remote/intermediate cache strategies.

## 2026-04-08 15:02 – Add existing-section metadata update flow
Context: Needed a broader follow-up to ENG-88149 so existing installed application sections can be updated after creation, including repairing broken JSON-style headings with a new plain-text caption.

## 2026-04-10 11:48 – Fix entity caption loss during column mutations
Context: User session analysis (copilot-session-b197a4a1) showed entity caption "Об'єкт" (uk-UA) was reset after clio-schema-sync update-entity on .NET Framework environment.
Decision: In LoadSchema, removed Cultures=[GetCurrentCultureName()] from GetSchemaDesignItemRequestDto. Sending only the current system culture (en-US) caused Creatio to return Caption filtered to that culture. When SaveSchema sent the filtered Caption back, the original uk-UA caption was overwritten. Empty Cultures=[] (default) tells Creatio to return all localizations, preserving the full round-trip.
Discovery: GetSchemaDesignItem with Cultures=["en-US"] returns entity Caption mapped to the requested culture key only. SaveSchema then replaces ALL caption entries with the sent subset, wiping other-locale captions. Same pattern in RemoteEntitySchemaCreator is verification-only (not saved back), so no fix needed there.
Files: clio/Command/EntitySchemaDesigner/RemoteEntitySchemaColumnManager.cs
Impact: Column mutations (add/modify/remove) now preserve entity caption in all cultures, not just the machine current locale.

## 2026-04-14 16:05 – MCP URL fallback vs registered environments
Context: Investigated why an agent used direct `uri/login/password` instead of registering a new clio environment before operating on a page.
Decision: Keep the finding at analysis level for now: URL-based MCP execution is an intentional fallback in `ToolCommandResolver`, but it creates ambiguous agent behavior when working tools expose both `environment-name` and direct connection args.

## 2026-04-17 11:55 – E2E pushed packages need hotfix to become editable
Context: Debugged MCP E2E failures where tests created a temp workspace/package, used push-workspace to install it on remote stands, then immediately tried package mutations such as create-lookup, create-data-binding-db, and sync-schemas update flows.
Decision: Keep push-workspace for package deployment but enable `pkg-hotfix <package> true` immediately after push inside mutation-oriented E2E arrange flows so the remote package becomes editable before designer/schema-data writes.
Discovery: Core computes package read-only state from `InstallType`, not `InstallBehavior`. `push-workspace` installs `CreatioPackages.zip` through archive/package-installer flow, which leaves packages as `InstallType=Repository` and therefore `IsReadOnly=true`. `PackageService.StartPackageHotfix` flips package editability by setting maintainer/install-type to editable state. Verified that EntitySchema, DataBindingDb, and SchemaSync mutation E2Es pass after hotfixing.

Impact: Future destructive E2E tests that push a workspace and then mutate remote package contents should hotfix the package after push unless a true SourceControl-mode push flow is introduced.

## 2026-05-05 – ENG-88747 Added converter format validation and AI guidance hooks
Context: Freedom UI converters registered without a `VendorPrefix.Name` key fail at runtime in Creatio with `"Error when register X. Type property should have format VendorPrefix.ConverterTypeName"`. The AI agent could ship pages that pass save and only break at runtime.
Decision: Added `SchemaValidationService.ValidateConverterDeclarations` that parses `SCHEMA_CONVERTERS` and flags any top-level key without a dot. Wired it into `validate-page`, `update-page`, and `sync-pages`, and updated their tool descriptions to instruct the agent to call `get-guidance page-schema-converters` whenever `SCHEMA_CONVERTERS` is edited.
Discovery: The converter object accepts both quoted (`"usr.X"`) and unquoted identifier (`BadConverter`) keys; identifier keys cannot contain a dot by JS grammar so they always violate the rule. The first implementation only handled quoted keys — fixed by splitting `TryReadConverterEntry` into `TryReadQuotedConverterKey` (returns `bool`) and `ReadIdentifierConverterKey` (no failure path, mirrors `TryReadIdentifierPropertyName` at `SchemaValidationService.cs:1235`). Method-shorthand (`key(arg) { ... }`) is supported via the `(` delimiter branch. Cognitive complexity in `PageValidateTool.Validate` was reduced from 16 to 13 by extracting `RunContentValidation`, mirroring the helper in `PageSyncTool`.
Files: clio/Command/SchemaValidationService.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageValidateTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageUpdateTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageSyncTool.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/SchemaValidationServiceTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageValidateToolE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageUpdateToolE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageSyncToolE2ETests.cs, .codex/workspace-diary.md
Impact: Bad converter keys are caught client-side before save across all three page-mutation tools, with E2E coverage on each. The `RunContentValidation` helper is now duplicated in `PageValidateTool` and `PageSyncTool`; if a third caller appears, lift it to a shared static class.

## 2026-05-05 – ENG-88747 Code-review follow-ups: deduplication, regex tightening, handler-shape correctness, E2E and doc gaps
Context: Self-review on the ENG-88747 branch surfaced ~130 lines of byte-equivalent parser duplication (`*Converter*` vs `*Declaration*` helpers in `SchemaValidationService.cs`), missing handler/validator E2E coverage in all three page tools, an unupdated `sync-pages.md`, the `sync-pages` MCP description still claiming converter-only enforcement, a generic error message that always pointed handlers/validators at "page-schema-handlers or page-schema-validators", and a `key.Contains('.')` check that accepted malformed prefixes like `".X"`, `"X."`, and `"X..Y"`. The user then pointed out that real Freedom UI handlers use array form `[{ request: "vendor.Name", handler: async (req, next) => {...} }]`, not object form — making the entire `ValidateHandlerDeclarations` validator dead code on canonical bodies (it only fires on `{...}` shape, which itself is already rejected by `ValidateHandlerStructure`). Three existing handler unit tests were also latently broken because they did `Replace("/**SCHEMA_HANDLERS*/{}", ...)` against `ValidListPageBody`, which actually contains `/**SCHEMA_HANDLERS*/[]`, so the replace was a no-op.
Decision: Removed the duplicated `*Converter*` helpers; `ValidateConverterDeclarations` and `ValidateValidatorDeclarations` now delegate to the unified `ValidatePrefixedDeclarations(jsBody, marker, elementType, guidanceName)` (those two ARE keyed by VendorPrefix.Name). Deleted `ValidateHandlerDeclarations` entirely and instead extended `SchemaHandlerValidationService.ValidateHandlerEntry` to validate the `request` field value against the shared `SchemaValidationService.VendorPrefixedNamePattern` regex (compiled, `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`). The handler-array walker already existed and extracts the unquoted `request` string — piggybacked on it. Replaced `ValidateHandlerDeclarations` calls in `PageValidateTool` and `PageUpdateTool` with `ValidateHandlerStructure` so the new request-format check is enforced consistently across all three page tools (`PageSyncTool` already called `ValidateHandlerStructure`). Updated `sync-pages` and `validate-page` MCP descriptions, `sync-pages.md`, `update-page.md`, and `update-page.txt` to clarify that handlers is an array with `request` values (not an object keyed by VendorPrefix.Name). Added a `guidanceName` parameter to `ValidatePrefixedDeclarations` so converter and validator errors point the agent at their own guidance pages.
Discovery: Validator surface dropped from ~310 lines to ~60. The handler request check reuses `VendorPrefixedNamePattern` made `internal` — kept the regex in one place. New unit tests on `ValidateHandlerStructure` (request without dot, request starting with dot, mixed array, empty array, well-formed `crt.*` request) cover the new path. The user's example handler (`request.$context.set(...)`) passes because only `.get(`, `.viewModel`, `.sender`, `.$get(`, `.$set(` are forbidden — `set` on `$context` is fine.
Files: clio/Command/SchemaValidationService.cs, clio/Command/SchemaHandlerValidationService.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageSyncTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageValidateTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageUpdateTool.cs, clio/docs/commands/sync-pages.md, clio/docs/commands/update-page.md, clio/help/en/update-page.txt, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/SchemaValidationServiceTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageValidateToolE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageUpdateToolE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageSyncToolE2ETests.cs, .codex/workspace-diary.md
Impact: All 596 McpServer unit tests pass. Validation now matches real Freedom UI shapes: object-keyed for converters/validators, array-with-`request`-values for handlers. The new request-format check fires on canonical handler bodies (which the previous implementation never touched) and routes the agent to the correct guidance page per element type.

## 2026-05-06 – Validator factory shape and converter function shape checks
Context: Copilot agent run `creatio-adaclio-testing/runs/run_20260506_122524` produced a Freedom UI page where the custom validator used `validate: function(value, config){...}` instead of the canonical `validator: function(config){return function(control){...};}`. Existing `ValidateCustomValidatorParamCompleteness`, `ValidateValidatorBindingPlacement`, etc. all passed because they check params/bindings, not the factory signature. The runtime then ignored the entry (`validate` is not the recognised key) and the validator never executed. Same blind spot applied to converters whose value can silently be an object/string instead of a function.
Decision: Added two new public methods on `SchemaValidationService`: `ValidateCustomValidatorFactoryShape` rejects (a) wrong outer key — `validate`, `validateFn`, `validation`, `validatorFn`, `fn`, `check`, `rule`, `test`, `isValid`; (b) missing `validator` key; (c) non-function value; (d) flat `function(value, config)` instead of factory; and `ValidateConverterFunctionShape` rejects converters whose value is not a function (object literal, string, array). Wired both into `PageUpdateTool.CollectValidatorErrors`, `PageSyncTool.Validate` (with `RunContentValidation` and merge into `CollectErrors`/`IsContentValidationSuccessful`), and `PageValidateTool.Validate`. Error messages name the offending element + wrong-key/issue + point at `get-guidance page-schema-validators` or `page-schema-converters`; per user preference no canonical mini-template is embedded.
Discovery: The factory regex `return\s+(?:async\s+)?function\b|return\s+(?:async\s+)?\([^)]*\)\s*=>|return\s+(?:async\s+)?[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\s*=>` produced false-positives when a flat function body contained the literal string `"return function"`; added `StripStringsAndComments` (mirrors `SchemaHandlerValidationService.SanitizeForHandlerApiScan`) to blank out string and comment regions before regex match. Method-shorthand entries like `validator(config){...}` were initially missed because `ExtractTopLevelObjectPropertyNames` doesn't recognise shorthand keys; replaced that call with the new shorthand-aware `EnumerateTopLevelObjectEntries`. `TryReadKeyValueRange` accepts both `:` and `(` delimiters so shorthand values are captured the same way `TryReadDeclarationEntry` (line 1592) handles them.
Files: clio/Command/SchemaValidationService.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageUpdateTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageSyncTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/PageValidateTool.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/SchemaValidationServiceTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageValidateToolE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageSyncToolE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/PageUpdateToolE2ETests.cs, .codex/workspace-diary.md
Impact: 28 new unit tests + 6 new e2e tests (2 per page tool) covering wrong-key aliases, missing validator key, non-function values, flat-function rejection, method-shorthand factory acceptance, async/arrow factory acceptance, and string-literal-in-body false-positive guard. All 200 schema-validation/handler/page-tool unit tests pass; net8.0 + net10.0 build clean. The two new validators close the gap that allowed the run_20260506_122524 page body to be saved with a never-executing validator.

## 2026-05-06 – ENG-88747 Sonar cleanup: extracted shared lexer helpers
Context: After committing the validator factory shape and converter function shape checks, Sonar Quality Gate reported `Duplicated Lines on New Code` at 14.6% (threshold 3%). The bulk of dup lived in `SchemaValidationService.cs`: a local `TryReadKeyValueRange` byte-equivalent to the existing `TryReadDeclarationEntry`, a local `StripStringsAndComments` near-equivalent to `SchemaHandlerValidationService.SanitizeForHandlerApiScan`, a local `FindFirstTopLevelArrow` near-equivalent to `SchemaHandlerValidationService.ContainsTopLevelArrowToken`, and `EnumerateTopLevelDeclarationKeys` walker repeating the same loop as the new `EnumerateTopLevelObjectEntries`.
Decision: Promoted `StripStringsAndComments` and `FindFirstTopLevelArrow` to `JsParserHelper` as `internal static` shared utilities. Collapsed `EnumerateTopLevelDeclarationKeys` to a one-line `EnumerateTopLevelObjectEntries(...).Select(e => e.Key).ToList()` delegation. Extracted `TrimAndStripAsync(expression)` to remove the triple `.Trim().TrimEnd(',').Trim()` + async-keyword-strip pattern from `IsCallableFunctionExpression` and `LooksLikeFactoryShape`.

Net effect: SchemaValidationService.cs new-code shrank by ~85 lines; JsParserHelper.cs gained ~84 lines that are not duplicates of any existing block. `SchemaHandlerValidationService` was intentionally left alone — its `SanitizeForHandlerApiScan` and `ContainsTopLevelArrowToken` retain regex-literal handling that the validator-side helpers don't need, so consolidating them risks behaviour drift in handler scans.
Files: clio/Command/JsParserHelper.cs, clio/Command/SchemaValidationService.cs, .codex/workspace-diary.md
Impact: 200 schema-validation/handler/page-tool unit tests still pass with no test changes. Sonar duplication metric should drop below the 3% gate after the commit lands. Future similar checks can reuse `JsParserHelper.StripStringsAndComments` and `JsParserHelper.FindFirstTopLevelArrow` directly instead of cloning the walker.

## 2026-05-07 – fix(unlock-package): route lock/unlock through ClioGate
Context: Issue #585 — `clio unlock-package` silently reported "Done" but left packages locked (InstallType=1). Application logs showed `SecurityException: Current user does not have permissions for the "SysPackage" object` from DataService ESQ permission layer.
Decision: Replaced DataService ESQ calls in `PackageLockManager` with ClioGate endpoints (`/rest/CreatioApiGateway/UnlockPackages`, `/rest/CreatioApiGateway/LockPackages`) which use `Terrasoft.Core.DB.Update` — bypassing the NUI permission check entirely. Also removed silent error swallowing: the gate returns `bool`; now throws `InvalidOperationException` on `false`.
Discovery: (1) ClioGate URL base is `/rest/CreatioApiGateway/` — NOT `/rest/CreatioApiGatewayService/`. Using the wrong suffix returns an HTML 404 page; `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<bool>` then throws `'<' is an invalid start of a value`. (2) `CheckCanManageSolution()` was already present on both `LockPackages` and `UnlockPackages` in cliogate — always grep before adding. (3) `PackageLockManager` is auto-registered via `RegisterAssemblyInterfaceTypes` — no explicit DI entry needed when removing/adding constructor parameters. (4) On macOS without `pwsh`, build cliogate with `dotnet build … -f net472 --source ~/.nuget/packages`; ATF.Repository version from `cliogate/obj/project.assets.json`. (5) Package push command is `push-pkg`, not `push-package`.
Files: clio/Package/PackageUnlocker.cs, clio/Common/ServiceUrlBuilder.cs, clio/cliogate/cliogate.gz, cliogate/descriptor.json, AGENTS.md, .codex/workspace-diary.md
Impact: Documented ClioGate URL pattern, macOS build steps, and deploy/verify workflow in AGENTS.md so future agents don't repeat the wrong-URL mistake or fumble the build. Branch: fix/unlock-package-use-cliogate.

## 2026-05-14 13:30 - Mobile Freedom UI pages reference document
Context: Research task to produce a single verified source-of-truth for AI agents working with mobile Freedom UI page schemas via clio MCP.
Decision: Verified all claims against clio C# source, creatio-ui TypeScript source, CrtUIPlatform package schemas, Creatio Academy, and a live Creatio 8.x environment via MCP calls.
Discovery: (1) update-page and sync-pages both reject mobile JSON bodies -- SchemaValidationService.ValidateMarkerIntegrity inside PageUpdateCommand.TryUpdatePage always runs and requires AMD section markers that mobile bodies do not have; validate=false in sync-pages bypasses only the outer MCP-level check, not this inner call.
