Discovery: the type WAS persisted (process metadata had DataValueType for the param) — so it was never a persistence bug. The value was wrong: ProcessDesigner.ResolveDataValueTypeUId did _userConnection.DataValueTypeManager.GetInstanceByName("Text"), and "Text" resolves to the ABSTRACT base TextDataValueTypeUId = 8b3f29bb-ea14-4ce5-a5c5-293a929b6ba2 (see Terrasoft.Core/DataValueType.cs:129). The designer's "Data type" picker only lists CONCRETE types (ShortText 325A73B8-0F47-44A0-8412-7606F78003AC, MediumText, LongText, Integer 6b6b74e2…, Boolean 90b65bf8…, Lookup b295071f…, Guid 23018567…), so the abstract base renders blank.
Decision: in ProcessDesigner, NormalizeParameterTypeName maps "Text"/"String" → "ShortText" (concrete), keep DataValueTypeUId (NOT the DataValueType object — assigning a shared manager instance is non-idiomatic and was an unrelated dead-end). CORRECTION — mistakes I made this session, do NOT repeat: the describe `type` field I first added read parameter.DataValueType?.Name, which is NULL on a read-back schema (only DataValueTypeUId is populated) → the field was always omitted. I then wrongly treated that always-empty field as "proof the old assembly is still loaded" and chased a phantom deploy problem (even tried compile-all, which is wrong for an assembly package). Reality on this stand: a pool restart DOES reload the package assembly — the user's FS-link + restart workflow is correct; the rebuilt assembly was loaded after the restart, and after the user compiled the package the Text→ShortText fix worked (designer showed "Text (50 characters)" = ShortText). Fixed the describe field to resolve the name via _userConnection.DataValueTypeManager.GetInstanceByUId(uid) (Manager.cs:354). The earlier modify-by-name "not found" / by-uid DesignSchema NPE were specific to certain processes' state, NOT a general "cold ProcessSchemaManager" rule. Lesson: verify deployed server behavior by the actual designer/metadata, not by a freshly-added describe field whose own correctness is unproven.

CLI get-page gained kebab-case --output-directory. Backward-compat: an explicit --expected-checksum disarms on-disk arming (guard returns not-armed) so it is never overwritten.

(3) sync-pages has no CLI verb (MCP-only) → out of CLI scope. (4) CLI update-page with no on-disk baseline arms nothing → zero extra SysSchema queries (no perf regression for plain CLI users).

## 2026-06-16 – [RequiresPackage] attribute replaces inline cliogate checks
Context: Generalize the cliogate-only version gate (inline `IClioGateway.CheckCompatibleVersion` + implicit `ServicePath.Contains("rest/CreatioApiGateway")` trigger + `RemoteCommand.ClioGateMinVersion`) into a package-agnostic declarative attribute, ahead of a second required package.
Decision: New `[RequiresPackage("name","version",Hint=...)]` on the OPTIONS class (mirrors `[FeatureToggle]`). Enforced at the two dispatch chokepoints — `Program.ExecuteCommandWithOption` (CLI + scenario runner) and MCP `BaseTool.InternalExecute<TCommand>` — NOT in a base-class hook (the 4 target commands override Execute / aren't RemoteCommand, so a `RemoteCommand.Execute` hook would never fire). `IClioGateway` kept as the queryable API for graceful/conditional callers (get-info, ApplicationDownloader) and refactored to delegate to the new `IRequiredPackageChecker`.
Discovery: MCP enforcement MUST resolve `IRequiredPackageChecker` from the per-call env-keyed container (`ToolCommandResolver.Resolve<T>(options)`), NOT via constructor injection — a ctor-injected checker binds to the MCP startup/bootstrap container (placeholder http://localhost) and validates the WRONG environment; and an optional ctor param `=null` is never forwarded by derived tools, silently disabling the gate (same false-confidence class as the old `WithTools(Type[])` bug). `EnsureRequirements` early-returns with NO `GetPackages()` HTTP call when the type has no attribute (zero-cost path). Use a static `RequiresPackageAttribute.IsDefinedOn(Type)` pre-check before resolving the env checker so ungated tools touch no environment.
Files: clio/Common/RequiresPackageAttribute.cs, clio/Common/RequiredPackageChecker.cs, clio/Common/PackageRequirementException.cs, clio/Program.cs (TryGetPackageRequirementError), clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/BaseTool.cs (ResolveFromCallContainer<T>), clio/Common/ClioGateway.cs, clio/Command/RemoteCommand.cs, Lock/Unlock/RestoreWorkspace/SqlScript/ShowPackageFileContent + GetCreatioInfo commands.
Impact: To require any Creatio package for a command, decorate its options class — no inline plumbing. Graceful-degradation commands (get-info) stay imperative on IClioGateway; the attribute is hard-fail only.

## 2026-06-16 00:00 – [RequiresPackage] property-level (bool-true) triggers
Context: Extend class-only [RequiresPackage] to gate on a bool option flag (required only when true) and apply to the conditional cliogate commands.
Decision: AttributeUsage now Class|Property. `IRequiredPackageChecker.EnsureRequirements(Type)` → `EnsureRequirements(object instance)` (needs the value). Collect-then-enforce: class attrs always + property attrs where the bool value is true; if triggered list empty, return before any GetPackages() (zero-cost preserved). Non-bool decorated property → InvalidOperationException naming the property (fail-fast during the metadata scan, no HTTP). Read value off the CANONICAL property only (Async / UseFeatureWebService), never the hidden alias.
Discovery: `RequiresPackageAttribute.IsDefinedOn(Type)` had to also scan properties — a property-only decorated type was otherwise silently skipped by the MCP pre-check in BaseTool.EnforcePackageRequirements (same silent-no-op class as the WithTools(Type[]) bug). Guarded by IsDefinedOn_ShouldReturnTrue_WhenOnlyAPropertyIsDecorated. NSubstitute landmine: after the signature change, `typeof(X)` / `Arg.Any<Type>()` still compile as `object` but match a Type, so stubs silently miss — switched matchers to the instance / `Arg.Any<object>()`.
Applied: PullPkgOptions.Async (pull-pkg --async → cliogate PackagesGateway), FeatureOptions.UseFeatureWebService (set-feature --use-feature-web-service → FeatureStateService), ListenOptions class-level (listen → ATFLogService). All presence-only. Default paths (core GetZipPackages / ATF.Repository FeatureService) stay usable without cliogate.
Files: clio/Common/RequiresPackageAttribute.cs, clio/Common/RequiredPackageChecker.cs, clio/Program.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/BaseTool.cs, clio/Command/PackageCommand/DownloadPackageCommand.cs, clio/Command/FeatureCommand.cs, clio/Command/ListenCommand.cs, clio.tests/Common/RequiredPackageCheckerTests.cs, clio.tests/Common/RequiresPackageAttributeTests.cs (new), clio.tests/Command/ProgramPackageRequirementGateTests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/BaseToolTests.cs
Impact: New user-facing refusal — `pull-pkg --async` / `set-feature --use-feature-web-service` / `listen` now fail early with an install-gate hint when cliogate is absent. No MCP tool exists for these three (gate is automatic via BaseTool if one is added later). No CLI arg/help change.

## 2026-06-16 – [RequiresPackage] part 2: full cliogate ServiceContract audit + property-level gating
Context: Review revealed the first pass only covered the CreatioApiGateway route. The cliogate package exposes FOUR [ServiceContract] classes (cliogate/Files/cs): CreatioApiGateway, PackagesGateway, FeatureStateService, ATFLogService — each at /rest/<ClassName>/. Commands hitting any of them need cliogate.
Decision: Extended [RequiresPackage] to bool PROPERTY-level (required only when flag is true): EnsureRequirements(Type)->(object instance); class attr = always, bool prop attr = when-true; non-bool decorated prop throws fast. Gated: listen (class, ATFLogService unconditional), push-workspace (class 2.0.0.0, WorkspaceInstaller.Install ResetSchemaChangeState unconditional), pull-pkg (prop Async, PackagesGateway only on --async), set-feature (prop UseFeatureWebService, FeatureStateService only on --use-feature-web-service deprecated). Decorate the CANONICAL property, not the hidden kebab/camel alias.
Discovery: Audit's "unconditional" claims must be VERIFIED — pull-pkg default path uses core PackageInstallerService (only --async hits cliogate); publish-app (alias publish-workspace) uses WorkspaceInstaller.PublishToFolder where the reset call is COMMENTED OUT (:212) so it is NOT cliogate-dependent — left ungated. Deliberately NOT gated (graceful/conditional, gating would regress): the SetFileDesignMode family (pkg-to-db/-to-file-system/set-fsm-config/turn-fsm/create-user-task/modify-user-task-parameters/link-from-repo all 404-degrade), download-configuration/add-item (inverse/combination), get-info (graceful). LANDMINE fixed: RequiresPackageAttribute.IsDefinedOn(Type) must scan PROPERTIES too, else a property-only-decorated command silently bypasses the MCP pre-check.
Files: clio/Common/RequiresPackageAttribute.cs, clio/Common/RequiredPackageChecker.cs, clio/Command/{ListenCommand,PushWorkspaceCommand,FeatureCommand,PackageCommand/DownloadPackageCommand}.cs, clio/Program.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/BaseTool.cs, docs help/en + docs/commands for listen/pull-pkg/set-feature/push-workspace.
Impact: To gate a command on a package conditionally, put [RequiresPackage] on the bool option that triggers the remote call. Always verify the default (flag-off) path is package-free before gating, and never gate a command that already degrades gracefully.

## 2026-06-17 – Docs-cache freshness: sync-revalidate stale component docs (ENG-91135 reopen)
Context: ENG-91135 reopened — an agent repairing an already-added crt.QuickFilter acted on a STALE cached component doc. clio docs-cache used stale-while-revalidate, so get-component-info served the pre-fix `.component.md` instantly (cached 9-11 Jun, before the doc fix landed on the CDN) while the background refresh arrived too late; the agent never saw §2.2 and tried wrong-path / wire-onto-DataTable repairs. Session export confirmed: CDN `latest` already had the fixed doc — the failure was clio-side cache delivery + the doc lacking a repair (not just add) recipe.
Decision: For DOCS only (not the registry payload), `ComponentRegistryDocsClient.GetDocAsync` now revalidates a stale hit SYNCHRONOUSLY against the CDN, bounded by `StaleRevalidateBudget = 5s`, and serves the stale bytes only as a fallback (stale-if-error). Removed the docs background refresh (`ScheduleBackgroundRefresh` / `_inFlightRefreshes`). `ComponentRegistryClient` (registry payload) intentionally keeps stale-while-revalidate — Alex scoped this to docs.
Discovery: the docs background refresh had no `DrainAsync` hook (unlike the registry's `PendingRefreshTasks`), so deleting it is safe. Budget cancellation relies on `TryFetchOnceAsync`'s `when (!cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested)` guard: a budget-CTS timeout surfaces as `OperationCanceledException` and is caught in `TryRevalidateWithinBudgetAsync` (distinguished from a real caller-cancel) → returns null → stale fallback. A 4xx revalidation is permanent (no retry) → immediate stale fallback. Cold-cache miss keeps the unbounded fetch (no stale copy to fall back to).
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/ComponentRegistryDocsClient.cs, ComponentRegistryDocsCacheStore.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/AGENTS.md, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/ComponentRegistryDocsClientTests.cs. (The repair guidance — §2.3 — lives in creatio-ui `quick-filter.component.md`; CDN publish is the nightly Jenkins generator job, see memory `cdn-component-registry-nightly-deploy`.)
Impact: get-component-info now trades a few seconds on a stale doc for the CURRENT guide; an outdated cached doc no longer silently misleads agents. MCP tool contract unchanged (MCP reviewed, no update required). To extend the same policy to the registry payload, mirror the bounded revalidate in `ComponentRegistryClient.GetAsync`.

## 2026-06-17 – ENG-91317 PR #723 review follow-up (tetiana-moshon) — explicit --expected-checksum stale baseline
Context: tetiana-moshon Major thread on PageBaselineGuard.cs:64 — an explicit `--expected-checksum` made TryArm return `(null,false)`, so PageUpdateCommand.Execute skipped RefreshOrDrop and `.clio-pages/{schema}/meta.json` kept the PRE-save checksum. The next unpinned `update-page` auto-armed from that stale baseline and raised a false `checksum-mismatch` conflict against a value the user's own prior save had already superseded (regresses AC6).
Decision: TryArm no longer short-circuits on a pinned checksum. It now always resolves metaFilePath + reads the on-disk baseline. When a baseline matches the environment AND a checksum was pinned, it reports `(metaFilePath, true)` WITHOUT overwriting options.ExpectedChecksum — so the explicit checksum still wins the comparison, but RefreshOrDrop moves the on-disk baseline forward to response.NewChecksum after a successful non-dry-run save. No matching baseline (pinned) → still `(_, false)`, nothing to refresh. Execute's `baselineArmed && success && !DryRun → RefreshOrDrop` is unchanged.
Discovery: The behavior change is CLI-only — MCP callers (PageUpdateTool/PageSyncTool) always have ExpectedChecksum==null at TryArm, so callerPinnedChecksum is false and the path is identical to before. No MCP/doc change required. Updated the existing TryArm_ShouldRespectExplicitChecksum test to assert armed=true + untouched checksum, added TryArm_ShouldNotArm_WhenExplicitChecksumSetAndNoBaseline and an end-to-end TryArm→RefreshOrDrop test (pin checksum, save, assert meta.json == post-save checksum) per the reviewer's requested coverage.
Files: clio/Command/PageBaselineGuard.cs, clio.tests/Command/PageBaselineGuardTests.cs
Impact: Mixing pinned/unpinned page saves against the same `.clio-pages` baseline dir no longer leaves the on-disk baseline pointing at an overwritten checksum, so a legitimate follow-up save is not blocked by a false conflict.

## 2026-06-17 – ENG-91317 PR #723 review follow-up (tetiana-moshon, 5-lens) — path-traversal hardening
Context: New reviewer tetiana-moshon CHANGES_REQUESTED with 1 Major + 5 Minor. Major (explicit --expected-checksum stale baseline) already fixed in 703bd2a5; Minor 4 (optional-nullable services) fixed in ba4c4b19. Addressing Minor 3 (security): PageFileWriter.WritePageFiles does `Directory.Delete(Path.Combine(rootDir, schemaName), recursive:true)` with no charset/containment check on schemaName — a defense-in-depth gap in a destructive shared service (repo mandates containment elsewhere, e.g. ComponentRegistryDocsPath).
Decision: Validate schemaName against `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` (compiled regex) at the top of WritePageFiles → fail-fast PageGetResponse before any FS mutation; PLUS a belt-and-suspenders GetFullPath containment assertion that the resolved schemaDir stays under `.clio-pages/`. Added a 6-case `[TestCase]` (../escape, a/b, a\b, .., "with space", "") asserting Success=false + no files written. Minors 2 (no get-page write opt-out) and 5 (asymmetric heavy-payload stripping) judged intentional design — answered with rationale in the PR reply, not changed. Minor 6 (CLI conflict round-trip coverage) already satisfied by Execute_ShouldReturnFailure_WhenArmedChecksumDiffers (exit 1 + no SaveSchema) + PageBaselineGuardTests + PageFileWriterTests.
Files: clio/Command/PageFileWriter.cs, clio.tests/Command/PageFileWriterTests.cs
Impact: A path-separator or `..` in a future non-platform schema name can no longer make the recursive delete escape the workspace. Validated: build 0/0 (no new warnings in page files); dotnet test --filter "Category=Unit&Module=Command" → 1685 passed/0 failed/25 skip.
Follow-up (same day): the first cut ALSO added a GetFullPath containment assertion using `_fileSystem.Path.DirectorySeparatorChar`. That broke `PageGetTool_WhenDirectoryCreationFails_ReturnsError` — its bare `Substitute.For<IFileSystem>()` returns `'\0'` for the unstubbed DirectorySeparatorChar, so `StartsWith(fullRoot + '\0')` was always false and the guard fired before the test's CreateDirectory-throw path. Removed the containment assertion: the `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` regex is already airtight against traversal (a matching name has no separator/`..`/drive marker), so the assertion was redundant defense that only added a stubbed-fs false-negative. LESSON: production code that consumes `IFileSystem.Path.*` beyond Combine/GetFullPath can be falsified by partial NSubstitute fs mocks — prefer charset validation over separator-arithmetic for containment.

Context: The event name was stored 3x per event (OTLP body, attributes["event_name"], and the dedicated event_name field) and persisted into 3 ClickHouse columns (Body, LogAttributes['event_name'], EventName). TelemetryService.BuildLogEvent drops the event_name attribute and the body; OpenTelemetryLogEvent replaces its body field with a dedicated EventName field (and OtlpLogRecord drops its body field too); SchemaVersion deliberately kept at 1 (pre-release - no old-shape rows exist to discriminate, so the relocation ships as the initial shape). The two ends MUST move together: drop the attribute client-side without moving the collector filter and every event is dropped server-side (event_name==nil). The local probe suite (deploy-caadt-local.ps1 TEST 1/2/3) is the verification gate for the bare-path filter and now asserts the EventName column + empty Body.

## 2026-06-19 10:07 – Confluence PlantUML macro edit (ENG-90883 research page)
Context: asked to restack the "Build modify contract" class diagram on Confluence page 4752572418 (TER space) so MODIFY sits below BUILD.
Decision: PlantUML layout fix — added hidden directional link `BuildProcessResult -[hidden]down-> ModifyRequest` and switched the 3 cross-package `Operation ..> X` links to `.up.>` so they reinforce vertical stacking.
Discovery: the "PlantUML Diagrams for Confluence" (puml4cc/stratus) macro stores its source in the ADF extension node `data-parameters` JSON, key `data.value`, with `compressed:true`. Encoding chain (NOT PlantUML's own ~1 codec): PlantUML text -> percent-encode (urllib quote safe='') -> raw DEFLATE (zlib wbits=-15) -> STANDARD base64 (has +,/,= ). Decode is the inverse. Round-trip with a tiny py script; edit only the one `data.value` substring and re-send the whole body via mcp atlassian updateConfluencePage (whole-body replace; verified live by re-decoding both diagram blobs). Macro also supports `compressed:false` (uncompressed) per stratus docs, but base64 is what the editor produces.
Files: (no repo files) scratchpad puml.py/encode2.py/assemble.py; Confluence page 4752572418 now v14.
Impact: reusable recipe for programmatically editing puml4cc diagrams on Confluence without the native editor; avoids hand-corrupting the compressed payload by always round-trip-verifying via decode.

(3) Signal start uses the SAME wrapper on ProcessSchemaStartSignalEvent.EntityFilters (meta key DZ13), via the same FilterModuleMixin. (4) Lookup column equality → InFilter(filterType 4, rightExpressions[]); scalar → CompareFilter(1, rightExpression). Param ref → dataValueType 26 (Mapping), value={value:GetMetaPath() token, displayValue, Id:fresh GUID}; constant → dataValueType=column type + scalar. Enums: FilterType Compare1/IsNull2/Between3/In4/Group6; ComparisonType Equal3/NE4/Less5/LE6/Gt7/GE8/StartWith9/Contain11/EndWith13/IsNull1/IsNotNull2; Logical And0/Or1; Expr Column0/Param2; DVT Text1/Int4/Float5/Money6/DateTime7/Date8/Time9/Lookup10/Bool12/Mapping26. ## 2026-06-19 – ENG-91842 BUG fixed: signal-start filter ignored (HasEntityFilters)
Context: live verify (share developer-9a2ab65a) — clio-built signal-start process showed the filter in the designer but fired on EVERY modify; user redid the filter by hand and it worked. Compared both schemas' ProcessSchemaStartSignalEvent.
Discovery: the ONLY signal-relevant difference was HasEntityFilters. Confirmed in Terrasoft.Core/Process/ProcessSchemaStartSignalEvent.cs: HasEntityFilters is a [MetaTypeProperty] bool, meta key DZ8, default false; WriteMetaData omits it when false (hence absent in the clio build). The runtime evaluates EntityFilters ONLY when HasEntityFilters==true → without it the stored filter is ignored. Escaping diff (" vs \") and extra Perform-task params in the designer version were red herrings.
Fix: ProcessFilterService.ApplyFilter sets signal.HasEntityFilters=true (ClearFilter resets false). Tests assert both. Package commit 532997f (dev-nf ProcessFilterServiceTests 13 passed). Capture doc updated with the HasEntityFilters rule. USER MUST REDEPLOY the package (rebuild + compile clioprocessbuilder in Creatio) for the fix to take effect.
Impact: signal-start filters now actually restrict the trigger. Lesson: a designer-faithful serialized value is necessary but NOT sufficient — gate flags like HasEntityFilters/HasEntityColumnChange must be set too; verify against a working designer capture, not just "filter renders".

Context: Validated the theming dev flow end-to-end with two live coding-agent runs (create a dark/blue theme → deploy → verify) and pressure-tested the `theming` MCP guide for an AGENT (not human) reader.
Decision: (1) Reworked ThemingGuidanceResource into an agent-lean article — Scope as a dispatch map (Which flow / List themes / Get-set default); Source-of-truth fetch made workspace-agnostic (`npm pack @creatio-devkit/theming` OR `npm i` in a Node project — a Creatio package is NOT a Node project); delete-default made actionable (inform+confirm); removed the "What a theme is" block + the "Common mistakes" section (folded the one real gotcha into the steps). (3) Get/set-default now requires confirmation before changing the system-wide `DefaultTheme` (applies to all users). (4) Guidance-discovery fix: the theming tools' [Description] (list-themes/clear-themes-cache, both variants) and the get-guidance [Description] now point to / list `theming`, mirroring how esq/page/business-rule tools route to their guidance.

A normal push deploys by CONTENT-DIFF (real-install marker = `Files saved in package "<pkg>"`; `0 editable primary packages` prints on EVERY push and is NOT a skip) and refreshes BOTH the theme registry (GetAvailableThemes) AND the `cssFilePath` MD5 hash (browser cache-bust) on its own; a version bump is NOT required for a content change. The earlier "plain push doesn't refresh / version-bump required" belief was an artifact of a BROKEN package (no descriptor.json). DefaultTheme value = theme `id`; empty/unresolved → stock theme (deleting the default reverts gracefully). Agent run #1 reverse-engineered "theme = CSS file in package" (list-themes + a find-entity-schema dead-end) BEFORE reading get-guidance; run #2 (after the discovery-pointer fix) read `get-guidance theming` FIRST and confirmed before setting the system-wide default — both fixes validated live.

## 2026-06-22 23:26 – IdentityService direct DB seeding feasibility
Context: Visualizer message `45e50935` asked whether OAuth/IdentityService configuration can be seeded directly in the database for Docker-style deployments.
Decision: Investigated read-only against the `bank` Postgres DB using the local Creatio connection string with secrets suppressed from summaries.
Discovery: Runtime token validation is backed by IdentityServer EF tables (`Clients`, `ClientSecrets`, `ClientGrantTypes`, `ClientScopes`, `ApiResources`, `ApiScopes`, `ApiResourceScopes`). Creatio UI/client-management also writes `OAuthClientApp`, `OAuthGrantTypeInClient`, and `OAuthResourceInClient`; secret fields in Creatio tables/sys-settings are encrypted, while `ClientSecrets.Value` is a 44-character shared-secret hash. Direct seeding is feasible for runtime clients if we generate the hash and insert the IdentityServer rows, but a full UI-equivalent seed must also reproduce Creatio metadata/encrypted fields or accept that the client is not fully manageable/displayable through the OAuth UI.
Files: F:\inetpub\wwwroot\clio\bank\ConnectionStrings.config, F:\inetpub\wwwroot\clio\bank-identity\appsettings.json
Impact: Future clio/docker design can choose between a minimal runtime seed and a full Creatio-metadata seed; a write-test should be explicitly approved because it creates OAuth credentials directly in the database.

## 2026-06-23 – Second merge: catch up to origin/master 7d595594 (+16 commits, PR #715 mergeability)
Context: PR #715 showed a GitHub merge conflict. Root cause: the earlier merge brought in master@6cec3e65, but origin/master advanced to 7d595594 (+16, incl. PR #753 OAuth MCP tools + deploy-identity). 3 files re-conflicted.
Decision: (ServiceUrlBuilder.cs) SAME KnownRoute enum-append collision as before — master's commit eaea278c took 46/47/48 for OAuthConfig{GetIdentityServerClientSecret,CreateTechnicalUser,AddClient}; RENUMBERED the branch's process routes from 46–49 to 49–52 (BuildProcess=49…ModifyProcess=52) so master's OAuth keeps 46–48; both KnownRoutes dict sets kept. (GuidanceGetToolE2ETests.cs) master's GuidanceGet_Should_Return_Server_To_Server_OAuth_Guide and the branch's GuidanceGet_Should_Hide_ProcessDesigner_Guides_When_Feature_Disabled were inserted at the SAME location and tangled across two hunks (signature + body, sharing the [Test]/[AllureTag] + Arrange scaffolding); split into two complete methods (union). (workspace-diary.md) append-only union. GuidanceCatalog.cs / BindingsModule.cs / Program.cs / Commands.md auto-merged clean.
Discovery: The KnownRoute enum is a recurring merge hotspot — any two branches that append routes after the same base value collide. Renumbering the LATER-merged side above master's max is the stable pattern. GitHub computes PR mergeability against the CURRENT base tip, so a branch can be green locally yet show "conflicting" the moment master gains an overlapping commit.
Files: clio/Common/ServiceUrlBuilder.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/GuidanceGetToolE2ETests.cs, .codex/workspace-diary.md
Impact: PR #715 mergeable against origin/master 7d595594. ## 2026-06-26 – PR #715 review: AI-surface fixes + full naming alignment (describe-business-process)
Context: a-serhiichyk-creatio left 5 standalone PR comments beyond the main REQUEST CHANGES review (verb naming, B2-followup, docs hygiene, AI-surface prompt drift, naming/contract) + a server-side deprecated-EndEvent note. First reply covered only the main review; these were unanswered. User: "fix valid items" then "change everything".
Decision: Fixed in two commits. (1) 3192256f — prompt drift A/B/C (validate prompt dropped abandoned process-add-element/.djs-validate-outline → ends at create/modify+describe; describe prompt field list → real DescribedElement fields; create prompt += signalStart/signal), rule-id F (missing-node R2→R15; softened "R1–R17 pre-checked" to enforced subset), describe uid (DescribedElement.Uid added, Id doc fixed — server sends id=Name + uid=UId, clio was dropping uid), docs hygiene (removed 3 scratch handoff/state docs w/ creds+paths). (2) 2f900f15 — full naming alignment: kebab MCP args via args-records (create/modify/list: environmentName→environment-name, packageName→package-name, processName/Uid→process-name/process-uid) + verb/MCP-tool/prompt rename describe-process→describe-business-process (aliases dp, describe-process).
Discovery: (1) MCP arg casing mechanism — bare method params expose the C# param name verbatim (camel); to get kebab you MUST use an args-record with [property: JsonPropertyName] (describe/validate already did). SDK flattens the record → flat arg schema, so refactoring create/modify/list to records changes only the wire key names, not the schema shape. (2) ReadmeChecker (clio.tests/Command/ReadmeChecker.cs) gates EVERY non-hidden [Verb]: canonical name must have a Commands.md "(docs/commands/<verb>.md)" link + a help/en/<verb>.txt + docs/commands/<verb>.md file + a WikiAnchors.txt line starting "<verb>:". Renaming a verb => rename both files (git mv) + update Commands.md/WikiAnchors or the test fails. (3) Verb back-compat = add old name to [Verb] Aliases (no per-alias Hidden); CommandLineParser supports the alias. (4) e2e tests call tools over the MCP protocol with arg dicts (not method calls) so the arg-record refactor doesn't break e2e compile — but the hardcoded dict KEYS (["environmentName"]) had to be kebab-ed for the gated runs; tool NAMES use the ToolName consts so they auto-followed. (5) "describe-business-process" does NOT contain substring "describe-process" → safe to mechanical-replace describe-process→describe-business-process (only the alias spots needed preserving).
Files: ~32. Code: CreateBusinessProcessTool/ModifyBusinessProcessTool/ListUserTasksTool (+ args records), DescribeProcessCommand ([Verb]), DescribeProcessTool (ToolName), 3 prompts, ProcessModelingGuidanceResource, IProcessDescriber, ProcessGraphValidator. Validated full Unit 4556 passed.

## 2026-06-24 – ENG-92146 PR #757 review fixes (cliogate HTTP readiness probe)
Context: Three Major review threads (tetiana-moshon ×3, m-dymytrova robustness note) on the cliogate HTTP readiness probe.
Decision: (1) Readiness predicate now treats only 2xx/401/403 as "serving" and retries 404/3xx/5xx (IsServingStatus helper) — a transient warm-up 5xx/3xx no longer counts as ready, which was reintroducing the ENG-92146 false-positive cascade. (2) Caller sets AllowAutoRedirect=false so a 302 is observed as a redirect, not followed to a login 200. (3) Per-request HttpClient.Timeout 30s->10s plus an optional overall deadline (CliogateHttpReadinessProbe overallTimeout ctor arg, linked CTS) wired from ClioCliCommandRunner (3 min) so an accept-then-hang host can't stack 12×30s into a ~7-8 min arrange stall. (4) Rewrote CliogateHttpReadinessProbeTests from a real HttpListener (real I/O in a [Category("Unit")] test) to a stub HttpMessageHandler — true unit test, no sockets, parallelizable; added 503-then-serving, persistent-5xx, persistent-3xx, 403-serving and overall-deadline cases.
Discovery: BuildMessage preferred lastStatusCode and dropped lastError, hiding the deadline reason when a status had been observed — now appends lastError alongside the status. clio.mcp.e2e is still not in CI (project-context), so moving the unit test into clio.tests for the unit gate would need a cross-project ProjectReference + InternalsVisibleTo (architectural change) — deferred for human decision.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Configuration/CliogateHttpReadinessProbe.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Configuration/ClioCliCommandRunner.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/CliogateHttpReadinessProbeTests.cs
Impact: probe no longer accepts transient warm-up responses as readiness, worst-case arrange time is bounded, and the contract is covered by fast true-unit tests.

## 2026-06-24 – ENG-90640: login-readiness gate + WebException status in readable error
Context: cliogate install-gate fails at CreatioClient.Login on a freshly-deployed e2e stand (~30 fixtures cascade); clio logged only a bare stacktrace so 401-auth vs connect/warm-up was indistinguishable.
Decision (TASK 1, harness-only): added WaitForLoginReadinessAsync(ping-app -e env, 12×5s) BEFORE the install-gate loop in ClioCliCommandRunner.EnsureCliogateInstalledAsync. Chose ping-app because on .NET-Core stands clio routes it through CreatioClient.ExecuteGetRequest, which forces CreatioClient.Login via the lazy AuthCookie (InitAuthCookie → Login) — the SAME login codepath install-gate's UploadFile uses (verified by ilspycmd-decompiling Creatio.Client 1.0.38). So a 401 fails the gate (isolates ENG-91829 creds), a warm-up connect/timeout is retried away. On exhaustion: full stdout/stderr to TestContext.Out + descriptive "did not become loginable within Ns" assertion.
Decision (TASK 2, production): enhanced ExceptionReadableMessageExtension.GetReadableMessageException so any WebException (direct, ConnectFailure-friendly arm, or nested in a wrapper) appends "(WebException: <Status>[ (HTTP <code> <reason>)])". Non-debug only-path benefits (CI runs non-debug). ConnectFailure keeps its friendly text + hint; nested via TryGetWebException inner-chain walk.
Discovery: on .NET 10 HttpWebResponse.StatusCode delegates to a private _httpResponseMessage (HttpResponseMessage) — there is NO m_StatusCode/_statusCode int field. To fabricate one in a unit test: RuntimeHelpers.GetUninitializedObject(typeof(HttpWebResponse)) then set _httpResponseMessage = new HttpResponseMessage(statusCode). The public ctor is [Obsolete(error:true)] and the serialization ctor throws PlatformNotSupportedException.
Discovery: GetPkgListCommandTests + RestartCommand.Tests assert the connect-failure message via StartsWith(...)+Contains("Make sure the site is running") — both survive the appended status (no exact .Be match), verified green.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Configuration/ClioCliCommandRunner.cs, clio/ExceptionReadableMessageExtension.cs, clio.tests/ExceptionReadableMessageExtension.Tests.cs
Impact: next TeamCity run on this branch reveals 401-vs-connect at the login boundary and absorbs the stand warm-up window before install-gate; the WebException-status helper benefits every clio HTTP failure path, not just install-gate.

## 2026-06-25 15:55 – ENG-90640: make ClearRedis e2e hang-proof (WaitAsync wall-clock guard)
Context: Run 15638941 (EnvironmentPath set, from fixed HEAD d764b8a9 with the resolver fix) STILL hung >15min at the same spot. The floor config (EnvironmentUrl-only, run 15638935) does NOT hang because ClearRedis fast-fails on the empty EnvironmentPath before any Redis op.

Connect/seed/exists use the existing 2-min arrange CTS; teardown gets a dedicated 30s budget and swallows OCE (best-effort; seeded key is test-prefixed). ## 2026-06-24 – PR #759 bound the background success readback (tetiana review)
Context: drive-pr-green pass. CI green + Sonar 0 + MERGEABLE; the only blocker was tetiana-moshon's CHANGES_REQUESTED with two Major threads. Thread 4 (McpToolExecutionLock "false premise" in the fan-out rationale) was already fixed by 69f5935f — the doc now rests solely on the single-session stdio invariant, exactly as asked — so it only needed a reply + the 9-min-stale timing noted. Discovery: `IApplicationClient.ExecutePostRequest(..., int requestTimeout = Timeout.Infinite, ...)` is ONE method with an optional arg, so a 3-arg NSubstitute stub silently binds the 4th param to its default — adding a 4th real param (readback override = 30_000) made every `CreateSection(..., Arg.Any<int?>())` stub stop matching the MCP call. Had to widen the stubs/Received to 4 args (ApplicationToolTests heartbeat-contract + CaptionCultureArgMappingToolTests were the two that broke). CLI tests use a 2-arg form → both overrides default to null → unaffected. The 4 Deploy_Should_* failures in the targeted run are pre-existing (fail identically on a stashed baseline; need a real PostgreSQL/identity stand).

## 2026-06-25 00:00 – Stop teaching scoped UserConnection (lifetime defect)
Context: Code-review blocker B1 — package template registered the platform-owned per-request UserConnection as a container-managed disposable (`AddScoped<UserConnection>(sp => UserConnection)`); MS.DI disposes any IDisposable resolved from a scoped/transient factory at scope close, tearing down the platform connection's DB executors + clearing UserConnection.Current mid-request. Verified end-to-end against core (C:\bare\Forest\core\trunk): ThreadContextInitializer.cs:61 sets Current; ClassFactory.Bind(CoreApiContainer.Resolve<UserConnection>) (AppConnection.cs:396) → GetService<UserConnection> → ApplicationModule.cs:238 GetUserConnection → FindOrCreateUserConnection(false) returns the SAME cached request connection; UserConnection.cs:1533 Dispose → DisposeExecutors()+ResetCurrent(); platform's own dispose at request end (HttpOperationUserConnectionFactory.HandleHttpRequestCompleted) becomes a guarded no-op.
Decision: Fix = `Func<UserConnection>` accessor (advisor-endorsed). MS.DI has NO ExternallyOwned concept; the only non-disposing overload takes a fixed instance (can't vary per request). Registering `AddTransient<Func<UserConnection>>(sp => () => UserConnection)` keeps the connection out of container tracking AND avoids the latent root-caching bug. Transient (not singleton/scoped) on the Func is deliberate — lets a singleton consumer depend on it without a captive-dependency error.
Discovery: The "skills" that teach this are MCP guidance resources surfaced via get-guidance and copied into workspace .codex/skills/creatio-config-webservice. Two carried the defect: ConfigurationWebServiceGuidanceResource.cs (CompositionRootPattern) and ComposableAppSkillGuidanceResources.cs ("Register UserConnection as scoped"). Guidance tests assert only marker substrings, so C# inside the string literals is unverified by tests — must read rendered guidance to catch contradictions (initial edit accidentally double-defined CalculatorEngine; reconciled to a separate ContactRepository example).
Files: clio/tpl/package/Files/src/cs/MainApp.cs (registration + CreateScope doc-comment); clio/Command/McpServer/Resources/ConfigurationWebServiceGuidanceResource.cs; clio/Command/McpServer/Resources/ComposableAppSkillGuidanceResources.cs
Impact: New generated packages + AI-authored WebServices no longer dispose the platform connection. Stale examples still carrying the old pattern (regenerate or leave): packages/ManualPkg, packages/Pkg1426397c7ffe44b, spec/data-binding/DataBindingPkg. Fix: make Arrange() private protected (restricted to same-assembly derived classes) + ArrangeContext internal (same-assembly). The two domains match, no compiler error.
Fixtures converted: 15 NoEnvironment fixtures with standard ArrangeContext (GuidanceGet/18, ToolContractGet/17, PageValidate/14, ComponentInfo/13+2special, McpGuidanceResource/7, EntityBusinessRule/~11, PageBusinessRule, PageCreate, ODataRead, ODataWrite, SchemaCreate, GetUserCulture, ExecuteEsq, ExperimentalTool/2, FindEmptyIisPort). ComponentInfo has 2 special tests (composite-wire) that set CLIO_COMPONENT_REGISTRY_LOCAL_FILE env var — they call McpServerSession.StartAsync directly and are correctly NOT sharing the fixture server.
Expected saving: ~160+ NoEnvironment test-level server startups → fixture-level startups (~15 total). Savings ~1,450 s (24 min) of pure startup overhead on the full NoEnvironment run.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/McpContractFixtureBase.cs (new), 15 fixture .cs files (modified)
Impact: ENG-92462 AC2 fulfilled — shared-server/env bootstrap for contract test groups; mutating tests remain isolated. Follow-up candidates: ApplicationSectionToolE2ETests (12 tests, direct McpServerSession.StartAsync pattern, mixed-category fixture), OAuthConfigurationToolsE2ETests (3 tests, direct pattern).

## 2026-06-26 — min-Creatio-version gate: third error code (version-check-failed)
Context: Team ratified splitting the gate failure space into THREE machine-readable codes (all exit 78). Distinction is "response received but no usable version" vs "no response at all" — NOT auth-vs-transport (untellable from the exception).
Decision: Introduced CreatioVersionResolution record (Version, CreatioVersionResolutionStatus {Resolved, ReachableWithoutVersion, ProbeFailed}) with static factories. ICreatioVersionProvider.GetCoreVersion()->Resolve(). Provider tracks per-source ProbeOutcome (Responded bool + RawVersion) — a returned HTTP call (even empty/garbage) = Responded; soft-degradable throw = Failed. Aggregation: first parseable version=>Resolved (secondary short-circuits); else any Responded=>ReachableWithoutVersion; else=>ProbeFailed. Checker: ProbeFailed=>version-check-failed (connectivity/access message, NOT "update Creatio"); ReachableWithoutVersion=>version-undeterminable (existing msg). IsCompatible: non-Resolved=>false. Memoize the resolution (null _resolution = not probed).
Discovery: ProgramCreatioVersionGateTests + BaseToolTests build CreatioVersionRequirementException directly and mock the checker — code-agnostic plumbing, NO real provider, so no edits needed there. CLI/MCP gates surface "{Message} [{ErrorCode}]" exit 78 for ANY code, so the new code flows through with zero Program.cs/BaseTool.cs change.
Caveat: ProbeFailed message appends strictest.Hint as usual — a command whose Hint literally says "Update Creatio…" would reintroduce that wording into a connectivity failure. Spec-consistent; flagged to architect.
Files: clio/Common/CreatioVersionResolution.cs (new), CreatioVersionRequirementException.cs, ICreatioVersionProvider.cs, CreatioVersionProvider.cs, ICreatioVersionChecker.cs, CreatioVersionChecker.cs, clio.tests/Common/CreatioVersion{Provider,Checker}Tests.cs
Impact: Automation can now distinguish unreachable/access-denied from reachable-but-no-version; commit 01d1b95.

## 2026-06-26 12:00 – ENG-91830 infra-tool MCP InternalError: real root cause = FakeKubernetes.Dispose throws
Context: ENG-90640 sub-task ENG-91830 (Reopened). assert-infrastructure / show-passing-infrastructure / deploy-creatio / restore-db e2e fixtures failed with `McpProtocolException: InternalError (-32603)` and were [Ignore]d. Prior notes blamed (a) MCP SDK typed-POCO structured-content conversion and (b) "requires reachable Kubernetes" — BOTH WRONG.
Decision: verify-root-cause before fixing. Reproduced locally (net10.0, no k8s, no Creatio) — both Assert/ShowPassing fail. String-return change did NOT fix; a try/catch around the call-tool filter's next() did NOT catch it. Added a temporary stderr ILoggerProvider to the MCP server (BindingsModule) → captured the real server exception: `System.NotImplementedException at Clio.FakeKubernetes.Dispose() (FakeKubernetes.cs:17)` thrown by `ServiceProviderEngineScope.DisposeAsync()` inside `McpServerImpl.InvokeScopedAsync`.
Discovery: MCP SDK 1.4.0 runs every tool call in a per-request DI scope and disposes it AFTER the handler returns. `IKubernetes` is a transient that falls back to `FakeKubernetes` when no kubeconfig (BindingsModule.cs:165-178); `FakeKubernetes : IKubernetes` is IDisposable and its Dispose() threw NotImplementedException → scope teardown threw → opaque -32603 OUTSIDE the tool method and OUTSIDE the call-tool filter (so string-return and filter-catch were both blind to it). FindEmptyIisPort works because it has no k8s dependency. The throw masked everything — once fixed, the original typed-POCO returns work fine (the SDK serialization was never the problem).
Fix: `FakeKubernetes.Dispose()` → no-op (clio/FakeKubernetes.cs). All 4 fixtures now pass env-free; un-ignored them and re-tiered Sandbox→NoEnvironment (the "requires reachable k8s" reasons were misdiagnoses; the failure-path Deploy/Restore tests use invalid inputs and never reach real infra). Reverted all diagnostic scaffolding (string-return, filter try/catch, DiagLogger, AddLogging). Added FakeKubernetesTests (Dispose no-throw + idempotent).
Files: clio/FakeKubernetes.cs, clio.tests/Common/Kubernetes/FakeKubernetesTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/{AssertInfrastructure,ShowPassingInfrastructure,DeployCreatio,RestoreDb}ToolE2ETests.cs

Verified: 6 infra e2e pass net10.0; clio.tests Category=Unit 2098 passed 0 failed; analyzer build clean (2 pre-existing CLIO005 in BindingsModule, not mine). Lesson reinforced ([[verify-root-cause-before-asserting]]): capture the actual server-side exception via a logger before theorising about SDK serialization — both prior write-ups were wrong because the -32603 hid the real Dispose throw.

## ## 2026-06-30 — ENG-92127: element→process parameter mapping direction & type-compat (analysis, no code)
Context: Verifying the mental model for "Implement element's parameters mapping to the process parameters" before implementing. Reference = a real UsrConcatProcess ProcessSchema (ConcatTask UserTask + ShowTask + process-level params).
Discovery (mapping direction / storage model — confirmed against the real schema):
 - The binding ALWAYS lives on the *consumer/target* parameter, pointing at the source. Two distinct storage shapes:
   * Element INPUT ← process input / another element output: stored both as a `ProcessSchemaMapping` (TargetMetaPath=`[Element:{el}].[Parameter:{p}]`, Source=`[#...[Parameter:{procParam}]#]`) AND mirrored on the element param's own `SourceValue`. Flow = process→element (IN).
   * Process OUTPUT ← element output: stored on the *process* parameter's `SourceValue` (Source:3 formula referencing `[#...[Element:{el}].[Parameter:{outParam}]#]`). Flow = element→process (OUT). The element's output param keeps `SourceValue:{}` (it is produced by the element, a source, never a sink).
 - So "map user-task OUTPUT → process OUTPUT, not the reverse" is CORRECT: a user-task output is a source (IsResult=true, Direction=1), a process output is a sink populated at process end; you configure it from the process-param side selecting the element output as source. SourceValue `Source` enum seen: 1=constant, 3=formula/reference (incl. `[#SysVariable.X#]`).
 - `Direction` ints: 0=Input, 1=Output, 2=Bidirectional/Variable, 3=Internal (see ProcessModel/Schema.cs ProcessParameterDirection).
Discovery (AC#3 "types must be the same" is KIND-level, NOT exact UId): the reference schema maps across DIFFERENT DataValueType UIds — process params are ShortText `{325A73B8-…}` (Text50) while ConcatTask params are Text `{8B3F29BB-…}`, and the platform accepts it. Academy: source list "only displays parameters whose type **corresponds to** the target". So type-compat must be matched on `CreatioDataValueKind` (Text↔Text, Numeric↔Numeric, …), which clio already models in `clio/Common/CreatioDataValueType.cs` (GetKind/IsText/IsNumeric/…). Implementing AC#3 as strict UId equality would wrongly reject this exact working process.
Files: clio/Command/ProcessModel/Schema.cs (ProcessParameterDirection, *DataValueTypeUId consts ~526-566), clio/Common/CreatioDataValueType.cs (kind table + helpers), clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/ProcessDesigner/CreateBusinessProcessTool.cs (mappings[] contract: elementName/elementParameter + processParameter|expression|value).
Impact: when wiring element→process param mapping, store the binding on the target (process-output SourceValue for OUT, element-param mapping for IN) and gate validity by CreatioDataValueKind equality, not DataValueType UId equality.

## 2026-06-29 — ENG-92563 Lever 1: gate MCP-host registration behind an explicit bool
Context: Parent ENG-90640 perf. `BindingsModule.Register(...)` registered the MCP stdio host (AddMcpServer + WithStdioServerTransport + WithRequestFilters + McpFeatureToggleFilter.RegisterEnabledPrimitives — 128 primitives with eager per-tool JSON-schema gen) UNCONDITIONALLY, so every CLI command and every per-env DI build in a live MCP session paid ~11–15ms (Debug) for a host they never use. The genuine payoff is the per-env agent-session containers (ToolCommandResolver), not the CLI.
Decision: Added an explicit `bool registerMcpHost = false` parameter to Register and wrapped the host block in `if (registerMcpHost)`. The flag is threaded EXPLICITLY (never read the static Program.IsMcpServerMode inside BindingsModule — in a live MCP session it is process-wide true, so per-env builds would still register the host). Only Program.cs Resolve<T>'s Container build passes `registerMcpHost: IsMcpServerMode`; the bootstrap bm build, ToolCommandResolver per-env builds, and all other call-sites use the default false.
Discovery (the ValidateOnBuild trap): Register ends with BuildServiceProvider(ValidateOnBuild:true). McpServerCommand's ctor depends on the McpServer singleton, so it MUST move inside the gate too — otherwise non-mcp builds fail validation (McpServerCommand→McpServer unresolvable). The ticket text said "leave AddTransient<McpServerCommand>() untouched"; that premise is WRONG (ValidateOnBuild eagerly validates every registered descriptor), so I gated McpServerCommand with the host. Crucially, the MCP tool TYPE registrations (AddTransient<XTool> at ~349-427) stay UNCONDITIONAL and that is SAFE: only StartTool/StopTool take McpServer in their PRIMARY ctor and they are NOT DI-registered (SDK-only via ActivatorUtilities, never validated); PageUpdateTool/PageSyncTool take McpServer as a METHOD parameter (SDK injects per-call), which DI validation never inspects. So among DI-registered services only McpServerCommand needed gating. Changed Program.IsMcpServerMode setter private→internal so the Program test could reproduce mcp mode.
Files: clio/BindingsModule.cs, clio/Program.cs, clio.tests/Command/Program.Tests.cs, clio.tests/Command/BindingsModuleMcpHostGateTests.cs (new)
Impact: every non-mcp CLI command and every per-env agent-session container skip AddMcpServer + 128-primitive eager schema gen. No command/output/exit-code change. ValidateOnBuild + ValidateScopes kept true (acceptance criterion). Validated: Debug build 0 errors / 0 new CLIO warnings (the 2 CLIO005 on business-rule commands pre-exist on master); plain CLI --version + help OK; mcp-server stdio probe initialize + tools/list = 128 (unchanged); full Category=Unit 4499 passed / 0 failed / 34 skipped; 2 new gate tests + the McpServerCommand-resolve test green. MCP reviewed, no update required (DI-internal perf change, tool set unchanged); docs reviewed, no update required. Base = master.

## 2026-07-01 – ENG-90636 build-theme MCP workspace-write mode (D2-A, uncommitted)
Context: analyzing the theming MCP surface surfaced that the `build-theme` MCP tool was pure-compute (returns css) while the guide's workspace/dev flow told MCP agents to use CLI `build-theme --output` — which the MCP tool cannot do (Finding F2). D2-A decision: give the MCP tool a workspace-write mode. Chosen over keeping it pure because in compute mode the full theme.css round-trips through the model twice (tool response + follow-up file-write arg = expensive output tokens); writing inside the tool and returning only the path keeps the large CSS out of the agent context.
Decision: input shape is `workspaceDirectory` (absolute) + `packageName` (NOT a raw output path), mirroring `new-ui-project` — the agent supplies workspace+package identity, clio resolves `<ws>/packages/<pkg>/Files/themes/<cssClassName>/`. Revised ADR D1 from "pure read-only compute" (flags now ReadOnly=false/Destructive=false/Idempotent=true/OpenWorld=false); OQ-03/consequences/checklist + story-4 + tp + sprint-status realigned in place.
Discovery: setting `IWorkspacePathBuilder.RootPath` then using `IsWorkspace`/`BuildPackagePath` is the canonical layout-resolve pattern (~7 commands do it: CreateUserTask/DeleteSchema/CreateWorkspace/Workspace.cs/...), so do NOT hand-roll the .clio/packages/Files constants (first pass did; refactored to reuse). FS checks + resolution live in `BuildThemeCommand` (owns IFileSystem) so the flat tool stays thin and the mode is unit-testable with substitutes — no reliance on the singleton path builder's CWD walk-up. Build/write logic is shared: private `WriteArtifacts` + `TryBuildTheme(options,outputDir,...)` overload serve CLI `--output`, and `TryBuildTheme(options,workspaceDirectory,packageName,...)` layers workspace/package validation on top. MCP tool stays flat (R-02): inline params + `[Description]`, no args-record; two new params at BuildThemeTool.cs:58-59. `BuildThemeResult` gained `path` (output-only; css/descriptor omitted in write mode). BuildThemeCommand gained an `IWorkspacePathBuilder` ctor dep — resolves via existing AddTransient<BuildThemeCommand> (no BindingsModule change, no full-suite trigger).
Files: clio/Command/Theming/BuildThemeCommand.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/BuildThemeTool.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/BuildThemeToolTests.cs (+4 cases), clio.mcp.e2e/BuildThemeToolE2ETests.cs (ReadOnly=false + workspace-write E2E), spec/{adr/adr-theming-native-build,stories/story-theming-native-build-4,test-plans/tp-theming-native-build,sprint-status}.
Impact: workspace/dev flow is now MCP-native (was CLI-only). Validated: clio + clio.tests + clio.mcp.e2e build clean net10.0, no CLIO warnings on theming files; targeted unit run Category=Unit&(Module=McpServer|Command|Theming) = 3604 passed/0 failed/11 skipped. STILL OPEN: uncommitted (needs consent); manual MCP E2E not run; F1 = rewrite ThemingGuidanceResource workspace step to route MCP agents to workspaceDirectory+packageName (still shows CLI `--output`) — until then agents aren't guided to the new capability.


## 2026-07-01 – check-theming-access MCP tool + reusable Creatio rights/license clients (uncommitted)
Context: precheck whether a caller may manage themes on an environment — operation right `CanManageThemes` + license `CanCustomizeBranding` — grounded in creatio-ui `ThemePermissionsService` (RightsService.getCanExecuteOperation + LicenseService.getLicenseOperationStatuses). clio had NO client-side rights/license check before this (only cliogate SERVER-side `DBSecurityEngine.GetCanExecuteOperation`).
Decision: two reusable Common-layer clients over a shared abstract base, plus one MCP-only tool (no CLI verb) that composes them.
- `Clio.Common`: `ICreatioRightsClient`/`CreatioRightsClient` -> `RightsService.svc/GetCanExecuteOperation` ({"operation":name} -> {"GetCanExecuteOperationResult":bool}); `ICreatioLicenseClient`/`CreatioLicenseClient` -> `LicenseService.svc/GetLicOperationStatuses` ({"licOperationCodes":[...]} -> {"GetLicOperationStatusesResult":{success,licOperationStatuses:[{Key,Value}]}}). Both derive `abstract CreatioServiceClient` (shared JsonOptions + build-url→serialize→POST→empty/non-JSON→InvalidOperationException). Naming follows the `CreatioVersionChecker`/`ICreatioVersionChecker` convention.
- Method shape mirrors the Angular reference: plain return (bool / IReadOnlyDictionary<string,bool>), NOT Try+out; transport/parse failure THROWS, caught at the edge (MCP tool -> failure result). A license success=false payload -> empty map -> not granted.
- Request settings are a Common-level `CreatioRequestOptions` (record; TimeOut/MaxAttempts/RetryDelay, defaults 100000/3/1) so the Common clients never depend on the Command layer; the tool builds a bare `new CreatioRequestOptions()` and does NOT set a timeout — it relies on the 100s default (the underlying `ExecutePostRequest` default is `Timeout.Infinite`, so a bounded default is what matters). In the same pass the whole theme family (list/create/update/delete/clear-themes-cache tools) had its hardcoded MCP `TimeOut = 30_000` removed for the same reason — a named timeout const is used elsewhere only when there is a caller-overridable range (execute-esq) or multiple distinct timeouts (ApplicationTool), neither of which applies here.
- MCP: `CheckThemingAccessTool` — a plain `[McpServerToolType]` + `[FeatureToggle("theming")]` tool injecting ONLY `IToolCommandResolver` (NOT `BaseTool`, since it wraps no command — same shape as `ExecuteEsqTool`/`ODataReadTool`/`ClearBrowserSessionTool`, which resolve services + compose). ReadOnly; `check-theming-access-by-environment` / `-by-credentials`; builds a bare `EnvironmentOptions` (the exact type `IToolCommandResolver.Resolve<T>(EnvironmentOptions)` consumes) to resolve BOTH clients per-call from the env-scoped container, then composes -> `{success,canManageThemes,canCustomizeBranding,hasThemingAccess}`.
- ServiceUrlBuilder KnownRoute ids 58/59 (RightsGetCanExecuteOperation/LicenseGetLicOperationStatuses). Guidance: ThemingGuidanceResource no-code prereq points to check-theming-access; McpCapabilityMap updated.
Discovery: clio has no base "Creatio service client" — inline `IApplicationClient.ExecutePostRequest` + per-class parse is the norm; the generic `ExecutePostRequest<T> where T:BaseResponse` is bound to the `{success,errorInfo}` envelope and does NOT fit RightsService's `{GetCanExecuteOperationResult}`. `ServiceUrlBuilder.Build(KnownRoute)` returns a FULL absolute URL (FW `/0/` baked in). `IToolCommandResolver.Resolve<T>(EnvironmentOptions)` is UNCONSTRAINED, so an MCP tool can resolve non-command env-scoped services (clients) from the per-call container — no wrapping command needed. `RemoteEntitySchemaDesignerClient` is the client prior-art but takes RemoteCommandOptions because it is Command-layer; Common-layer clients must not.
Files: clio/Common/{CreatioRequestOptions,CreatioServiceClient,CreatioRightsClient,CreatioLicenseClient}.cs, clio/Common/ServiceUrlBuilder.cs (58/59), clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/CheckThemingAccessTool.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Resources/ThemingGuidanceResource.cs, clio/BindingsModule.cs, docs/McpCapabilityMap.md, clio.tests/Common/{CreatioRightsClient,CreatioLicenseClient}Tests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/CheckThemingAccessToolTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/CheckThemingAccessToolE2ETests.cs.
Impact: reusable rights/license plumbing for any future precheck; theming server-flow has a one-call guided precheck (MCP-only). Validated: full Category=Unit 4962 passed/0 failed on net8.0 AND net10.0; clio + clio.tests + clio.mcp.e2e build clean (0 errors, no new CLIO warnings). STILL OPEN: uncommitted (needs consent); no CLI verb by design; hermetic e2e only asserts the two tool names are advertised (gated on `theming`); manual MCP E2E not run.
## ## 2026-06-30 — ENG-91314 reopened: HTML-error diagnostic + remove-package-dependency + guidance
Context: ENG-91314 (add-package-dependency, PR #698) was REOPENED after two ADAC sessions (Kateryna). ## ## 2026-06-30 — ENG-92127 E2E VERIFIED on a live stand + clio describe DTO gap fixed
Context: Verifying the element-parameter mapping on the test-stand stand (local IIS "Creatio" :1026, physical path C:\Projects\Creatio\TSBpm\..., clioprocessbuilder Pkg folder is a JUNCTION to C:\Projects\workspace\ProcessBuilder\packages\clioprocessbuilder — FS shared, FSM on).
Discovery (deploy saga root cause): the runtime kept serving OLD clioprocessbuilder behavior through ~8 deploy attempts (build+restart, pkg-to-db, push-pkg×N, clear-redis, compile-creatio). TWO independent causes, both finally understood:
 1. REAL blocker: the package UID was mismatched — workspace descriptor.json UId f100e6d2-... vs the stand DB SysPackage.UId 8219c8e1-... So Creatio saw same-name-different-UID and never replaced the runtime assembly ("The package already exists with a different UID" on FS-update). FIXED by the user unlocking the package + me aligning the workspace descriptor UId to 8219c8e1 (working-tree only, NOT committed — canonical git UId stays f100e6d2) + the user loading from file system. push-pkg also kept failing its post-install cliogate Unlock step (UnlockPackages returns non-JSON → broken on the stand) — the FS-load path bypasses it.
 2. FALSE NEGATIVE that masked success: clio's DescribeProcessCommand DESERIALIZES the server response into Clio.Command.ProcessModel.DescribedParameter and re-serializes it — and that DTO had no `direction`/`isResult`, so the new server fields were STRIPPED from describe output. My chosen deploy indicator (direction/isResult in describe) was therefore invisible regardless of stand state. source/value are NOT stripped — used those to verify instead.

A type-mismatch addMapping (Integer Duration → Guid ProcResult) was rejected with "Cannot map 'Duration' to 'ProcResult': ... incompatible data value types ..." (AC#3 ✓). The new mapping fields being honored at all proves the stand runs my code.
Fix this session: added `Direction` (string) + `IsResult` (bool?) to DescribedParameter (clio/Command/ProcessModel/IProcessDescriber.cs) so describe surfaces what the server returns (omitted vs older servers via WhenWritingNull). Validated: Category=Unit&(Module=ProcessModel|Module=McpServer) 1624/1624 green (net8+net10); clio.csproj clean.

## 2026-07-01 22:30 – ENG-92541 (ext): hard-gate custom CSS `styles`
Context: Follow-up to the guidance-only ENG-92541 change — user asked that when the agent writes a `styles` field into viewConfigDiff, the tool require explicit approval (guidance alone is skippable). Confirmed decisions: gate ONLY `styles` (not `classes`); validate-page REPORTS (warning, no block); implement as extension of ENG-92541.
Decision: Deterministic hard-reject mirroring the ENG-89871 localizable-literal pattern. New `SchemaValidationService.ValidateCustomCssStyles` (web) / `ValidateMobileCustomCssStyles` (mobile) detect a `styles` JSON object with >=1 property anywhere in a viewConfigDiff insert/merge `values` subtree (empty `{}`/null/non-object ignored; does not recurse into the styles object). New kebab `--allow-custom-css` flag on PageUpdateOptions + PageUpdateArgs (MCP) + per-page on PageSyncPageInput. Gate lives in PageUpdateCommand.ValidateWebInput/ValidateMobileInput (`if(!AllowCustomCss)` → reject); sync-pages inherits it (traced SyncPages→...→BuildUpdateRequest→UpdateCommand.TryUpdatePage, so command-level gate covers sync — only threaded the per-page flag). MCP PageUpdateTool.ValidateWebPageBody also Collects the styles check (early specific error, intentional duplicate like the literal check). validate-page folds ValidateCustomCssStyles errors into Warnings (never affects contentOk). Guidance STOP block + GATE "Why" now state the hard-reject + flag.
Discovery: `styles` is a universal Freedom UI base input (every component inherits it) — the single correct lever; `classes` deliberately left ungated (can reference platform classes → false-positive risk). Two-phase confirmation-token pattern (like `force`) is the only way an MCP tool can "ask for approval": reject → agent AskUserQuestion → resubmit with allow-custom-css=true; decline → don't resubmit.
Files: SchemaValidationService.cs, PageUpdateOptions.cs, PageUpdateTool.cs, PageSyncTool.cs, PageValidateTool.cs, PageModificationGuidanceResource.cs; tests SchemaValidationServiceTests.cs, PageUpdateCommandCustomCssTests.cs (new), ValidatePageToolTests.cs; e2e PageUpdateToolE2ETests.cs + PageValidateToolE2ETests.cs; docs update-page.(txt|md), sync-pages.md.
Impact: Verified via coder subagent + independent re-run — dotnet build clio.csproj 0 errors (only pre-existing CS9113/CLIO005), `Category=Unit&(Module=Command|Module=McpServer)` = 3430 passed / 0 failed (net8+net10). E2E not run (needs live env). Commit still pending user approval. Both ENG-92541 increments (guidance + hard-gate) now on branch feature/ENG-92541_css-warning-guidance.

## 2026-07-01 22:55 – ENG-92541: "don't ask ≠ don't warn" guidance clause
Context: Adversarial live test (session 759fd1e2) showed the agent, told "don't ask/don't warn — just apply", self-set allow-custom-css=true on the FIRST update-page call with NO warning. Added 2 assertions to GuidanceGetTool page-modification test.

## 2026-07-01 16:00 – LoadSchema: gate enriched re-issue on schema availability (ENG-91314)
Context: PR #802 review (b-horodyskyi, Major/correctness) — enriched-error re-issue was gated on `response == null`, but `TryGetSchemaDesignItem` returns a non-null envelope whenever `Success == true`, so a `Success == true` response with a null `Schema` skipped the `GetSchemaDesignItem` re-issue and emitted the generic "returned no schema" message, losing the missing-dependency diagnostic.

## 2026-07-01 17:30 - ENG-92558 PR #804 review fix: pre-migrate shared clio home once (Major #2)
Context: PR #804 review (m-dymytrova) Major — vetted parallel NoEnvironment fixtures that do not override ConfigureMcpServerSettings share the runner's global CLIO_HOME; under 2 workers two [OneTimeSetUp]s start two clio mcp-server processes whose SettingsBootstrapService.Load(applyRepairs=true) WRITES appsettings.json on a missing/legacy home, a cross-process race with only an in-process lock.
Decision: Added assembly-wide [SetUpFixture] McpSharedHomeSetUpFixture (namespace Clio.Mcp.E2E) whose [OneTimeSetUp] starts one shared MCP server with default (non-overridden) settings and disposes it, so the create/migrate write happens once, serially, before any parallel fixture; later loads on that home are read-only and the race window never opens. Isolated-home fixtures (OAuth/canary) are unaffected.
Discovery: In-process priming would be wrong — with CLIO_HOME unset, AppSettingsFolderPath keys off the entry assembly's Company/Product, so the testhost process resolves a different home than the clio.dll child. Starting a real child server is the only way to migrate the same home the parallel children read. Verified: e2e builds clean; McpFixturePolicyTests + FindApp/AddItemModel contract fixtures pass (4/4) with ~11s one-time server start proving the SetUpFixture runs.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/McpSharedHomeSetUpFixture.cs, .codex/workspace-diary.md
Impact: The shared-global-home write race for the vetted parallel NoEnvironment cohort is closed; full cohort timing/behaviour proof remains a CI/TeamCity concern (needs a stand).
