## 2026-07-07 – ENG-91842 data-source filters (Option B): live-verified dates + macros + date-parts
Context: continuation of the 2026-07-06 entry. With a live stand (test-stand) the deferred vocabulary was verified against real saved schemas and finished: date/time constants, relative-date/system macros, and left-hand date-parts. User deploys the package + restarts the stand; I create+describe via MCP and inspect the raw metadata.json on disk.
Decision: (1) Date/DateTime/Time CONSTANT is stored as a quote-wrapped LOCAL ISO string literal ("\"yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fff\"") in BOTH reps, plus a UTC `dateValue` (...Z) in the edit rep only; TZ from `_userConnection.CurrentUser.TimeZone` (try/catch → UTC). A bare string renders as `<?>` in the designer — the quote-wrapping is mandatory. (2) A MACRO is a right-hand `FunctionExpression{functionType:1, macrosType, functionArgument?(Integer)}`, always a Compare (never lookup-In); a date macro on a date column sets `trimDateTimeParameterToDate=true`. Argument macros (NextNDays) require `macroArgument` or throw. (3) A DATE-PART is a LEFT-hand `FunctionExpression{functionType:3, datePartType, functionArgument:ColumnExpression{columnPath}}` compared to an Integer value; column recovered from functionArgument on read-back. New `DatePartCatalog` (Day/Week/Month/Year/Weekday/Hour; HourMinute/Time deferred — needs the time carrier).
Discovery: THE recurring trap — every filter field needs a property on BOTH the package `FilterConditionDescriptor` AND clio's `DescribedFilterCondition`. Macro read-back silently DROPPED live even with green unit tests because clio's DTO lacked `macro`/`macroArgument` and System.Text.Json discards unknown JSON on re-serialize; same fix applied pre-emptively for `datePart`. clio must be rebuilt+restarted to pick up a DTO change (a stale MCP-server process serves the old DTO). Confirmed we CANNOT reuse core `EntitySchemaQueryFilter`/DataContract wholesale: the platform serializes PascalCase, lacks the client-only edit fields (className/dateValue/displayValue), and there is no server-side wrapper producer — the metadata is exactly what the visual designer used to build only on the client. Hand-rolled encoder kept; core read as SPEC only.
Files: package — Filters/DatePartCatalog.cs (new), Filters/ProcessFilterService.cs (BuildLeftExpression + datePart/Integer typing in BuildCondition), Filters/FilterDescriptorReader.cs (ReadColumnPath digs into functionArgument + TryReadDatePart), Contracts/FilterContracts.cs (DatePart), ProcessDesignConstants.cs (datePartType/functionType=3/Integer=4 + date value types), tests/FilterDescriptorReaderTests.cs (+3 date-part tests). clio — Command/ProcessModel/IProcessDescriber.cs (DescribedFilterCondition.DatePart), Resources/ProcessDesigner/ProcessModelingGuidanceResource.cs (datePart bullet), Tools/ProcessDesigner/{CreateBusinessProcessTool,ModifyBusinessProcessTool}.cs (macro+datePart in [Description]), clio.tests/Command/ProcessModel/ServerProcessDescriberTests.cs (+datePart read test).
Verify: package FilterDescriptorReaderTests 16 pass (dev-nf); clio ProcessModel 92 + McpServer 1549 pass (net8). Dates + macros live-verified on test-stand; date-parts pending redeploy for live-verify (Year(CreatedOn)=2026). CLI docs reviewed, no update required (process-designer commands are feature-toggled → omitted from committed Commands.md/help/docs); MCP guidance + tool descriptions updated.

## 2026-07-07 – ENG-91842 filters: signal-start param-ref guard + serializer/applier split
Context: user observed in the designer that a signalStart filter cannot map a column's right side to a parameter, while Read data can — asked to confirm in the client code and then enforce it. Then asked to do it "architecturally correct".
Decision: (1) CONFIRMED in the platform client — `FilterModuleMixin.getFilterModuleConfig` defaults `filterEditConfig` to `ProcessDesignerFilterEditFilter`, whose `applyMenuItems` adds the `SELECT_PARAMETER` menu item (maps the right side to a process/element param, dataValueType=MAPPING). `BaseSignalEventPropertiesPage.getFilterModuleConfig` OVERRIDES it to `filterEditConfig:null`, so a signal filter falls back to the base `Terrasoft.FilterEdit.Filter` (`applyMenuItems: Terrasoft.emptyFn`) — no parameter option. Read/Add/Modify/Delete data pages do NOT override, so they keep it. Semantic reason: a signal is evaluated to decide which records START the process, before any instance exists → no parameter has a value yet. (2) Enforced it server-side: reject a `processParameter`/`elementParameter`/`expression` right-hand source anywhere in a signal-start filter tree (constants/macros/date-parts/isNull only). (3) REFACTOR (architecturally-correct placement): split the old `ProcessFilterService` — it now knew about element kinds via ApplyFilter/ClearFilter — into a PURE serializer `ProcessFilterService` (`BuildFilterValue` + descriptor→JSON only, zero element knowledge) and a new element-aware `ProcessFilterApplier` (`ApplyFilter`/`ClearFilter`: EntityFilters-vs-DataSourceFilters storage routing, the signal param-ref guard, root-schema resolution). Applier depends on `IProcessFilterService`. Rationale: keep all "knows about signal/data element" logic cohesive in one class; the serializer stays reusable and testable in isolation.
Discovery: `ApplyFilter` was ALREADY element-type-aware before this task (it must be — signal stores the filter in `EntityFilters`+`HasEntityFilters`, a data node in a `DataSourceFilters` parameter), so the guard rode on existing knowledge; the refactor just moved that whole seam out of the serializer. Blast radius of the split: `ProcessDesigner` + `ProcessOperationExecutor` (ctor dep `IProcessFilterService`→`IProcessFilterApplier`), DI in `ClioProcessBuilderApp`, and 6 test fixtures (ApplyFilter/ClearFilter tests migrated `ProcessFilterServiceTests`→new `ProcessFilterApplierTests`; 4 ctor call sites now pass an applier).
Files: package — Filters/IProcessFilterApplier.cs (new), Filters/ProcessFilterApplier.cs (new), Filters/ProcessFilterService.cs (slimmed to serializer), Filters/IProcessFilterService.cs, ClioProcessBuilderApp.cs (DI), cs/ProcessDesigner.cs, Operations/ProcessOperationExecutor.cs; tests — ProcessFilterApplierTests.cs (new, 8 tests incl. 3 guard tests), ProcessFilterServiceTests.cs (apply/clear tests removed), ProcessDesigner{Orchestrator,RoundTrip,Security}Tests.cs + ProcessOperationExecutor{,GraphOps}Tests.cs (ctor arg). clio — Resources/ProcessDesigner/ProcessModelingGuidanceResource.cs (SIGNAL-START RESTRICTION bullet), Tools/ProcessDesigner/{CreateBusinessProcessTool,ModifyBusinessProcessTool}.cs ([Description]).
Verify: package 273 pass / 1 known-unrelated pre-existing fail (ProcessMappingServiceTests DataValueTypeManager harness gap); clio McpServer 1549 + ProcessModel 92 pass (net8). CLI docs reviewed, no update required (process-designer feature-toggled → omitted from committed docs). Live-verify of date-parts + this guard still pending a redeploy.

## 2026-07-07 – ENG-91842 filters: code-review pass (4 dimensions) + fixes + coverage
Context: /creatio-code-review over all commits on both feature/ENG-91842-data-source-filters branches (clio 18 commits, ProcessBuilder 10). Ran 4 parallel dimension reviewers (correctness, security, clarity/conventions, tests).
Decision: fixed the one real defect + the cheap correctness/clarity wins; added coverage for the top gaps.
Discovery + fixes:
- **[Major, real latent bug] Nested filter group broke describe.** FilterDescriptorReader returned a `FilterDescriptor` for EVERY group incl. nested ones; nested groups live in the declared `List<FilterGroupDescriptor>`, and the WCF describe endpoint serializes with the default `DataContractJsonSerializer` (WebMessageFormat.Json, BodyStyle=Wrapped, no custom formatter) → a derived instance in a base-typed list throws without `[KnownType]`. So `describe-business-process` would throw for any process with an AND/(B OR C) filter. Flat filters were fine (root `Filter` is declared `FilterDescriptor`), which is why live tests passed — no test/e2e described a nested-group filter through WCF. Fix: `ReadRootGroup` (FilterDescriptor, root only) + `ReadNestedGroup` (base FilterGroupDescriptor) + shared `PopulateGroupMembers`. Guard test asserts `Groups[0]` is exactly `FilterGroupDescriptor`.
- **[Minor] Get vs Find.** ResolveColumn (`GetInstanceByUId` ×2) and ProcessFilterApplier.ResolveRootSchema (`GetInstanceByName`) used the throwing Get*, making the friendly "not found" messages dead code (raw ItemNotFoundException surfaced). Switched to FindInstanceByUId/FindInstanceByName (see [[creatio-manager-get-vs-find-semantics]]).
- **[Major, clarity] Magic value-type literals** 4/5/6/12 in ConvertConstant → added Float/Money/Boolean constants and switched on named constants; removed a stale date comment.
- **[Minor, defensive] New guards:** reject datePart+macro on one condition; reject isNull/isNotNull carrying a right-hand source (was silently dropped).
- Security review: CLEAN (auth gate reused = the stronger CheckCanManageProcessDesign; no string-built JSON — all via dictionaries + JsonSerializer; fail-closed JsonDocument parse; no secret leakage). Not fixed / deferred: bare `catch(Exception)` in ResolveUserTimeZone (kept — intentional UTC fallback; narrowing risks an unknown platform exception type in prod); read-back of an un-catalogued macro/datePart code yields a partial condition (narrow, tied to deferred HourMinute).
- Coverage added (+18 package cases, +1 clio): nested-group type guard, date UTC/offset branch, bare-group input, full comparison vocabulary, valid-JSON-not-filter→null, column-not-found, expression encoder input, unknown process-parameter, datePart+macro & isNull+value rejection, ClearFilter(data element), signal object-derivation, signal expression rejection; clio DTO expression/elementParameter deserialization.
Files: package src FilterDescriptorReader.cs, ProcessFilterService.cs, ProcessFilterApplier.cs, ProcessDesignConstants.cs; tests FilterDescriptorReaderTests.cs, ProcessFilterServiceTests.cs, ProcessFilterApplierTests.cs; clio ServerProcessDescriberTests.cs.
Verify: package 291 pass / 1 known-unrelated pre-existing fail; clio ProcessModel 93 pass (net8). Live-verify of date-parts + signal guard still pending a redeploy.

## 2026-07-07 – ENG-91842 filters: date offset-detection via DateTime.Kind (drop HasExplicitOffset)
Context: reuse question — does HasExplicitOffset (our manual Z/+/- scan deciding instant-vs-naive for a caller ISO string) duplicate client or core logic?
Discovery: NO reusable analog. Client (`core/…/data/filters/parameter.js` setValue/getSerializableObject) works from a JS `Date` object — stores `dateValue` = Date, emits `dateValue`(UTC …Z) + `value` = `Terrasoft.encodeDate(dateValue)`; it never parses an arbitrary string, so the "has offset?" question can't arise. Core (`Terrasoft.Core/Entities/EntitySchemaColumnDef.cs:527`) parses a date const via `DateTime.TryParseExact(value, DateTimeColumnConstFormat, Invariant, DateTimeStyles.None)` — one fixed format, naive, no offset sniffing. Our helper is a legit artifact of the string-based MCP contract (accepts 2026-05-01 / …T12:00:00 / …Z / …+02:00).
Decision: replaced the manual scan with framework-native detection — `DateTime.TryParse(raw, Invariant, DateTimeStyles.RoundtripKind, out probe)`; `probe.Kind == Unspecified` ⇒ naive (interpret in user zone), `Utc`/`Local` ⇒ absolute instant (re-read via `DateTimeOffset` for a host-TZ-independent UtcDateTime). Deleted `HasExplicitOffset`. More robust on edges (fractional seconds, +00:00, space vs T) than the `Z`/`+`/`-` scan; behavior on well-formed ISO unchanged.
Files: packages/clioprocessbuilder/Files/src/cs/Filters/ProcessFilterService.cs (BuildDateConstant rewrite, HasExplicitOffset removed); tests/clioprocessbuilder/FilterDescriptorReaderTests.cs (+numeric-offset +02:00, +date-only midnight).
Verify: package 293 pass / 1 known-unrelated pre-existing fail. +02:00→10:00Z conversion confirms Kind-detection live.

## 2026-07-07 – ENG-91842: split ProcessDesigner (10-dep facade) into per-use-case handlers + guard
Context: ProcessDesigner's ctor had grown to 10 params (UserConnection + 9 services) and kept accreting one per new capability. Question: architecturally OK?
Discovery: real cohesion smell (constructor over-injection). Dependency-usage map showed deps partition by METHOD, not shared: BuildProcess used {repository, layout, graphBuilder, parameterService, mappingService, filterApplier}; ModifyProcess {repository, layout, graphBuilder, operationExecutor}; ListUserTasks {userTaskCatalog}; DescribeProcess {describer}. Describe/List were pure pass-throughs (auth-check + delegate) to already-existing services. So the class was 4 separable jobs sharing only the CanManageProcessDesign gate.
Decision: option 1 (full split). New `IProcessDesignGuard`/`ProcessDesignGuard` (UserConnection) = the shared gate in one place. `IProcessBuildHandler`/`ProcessBuildHandler` (guard + 6 create collaborators) owns BuildProcess + its rollback. `IProcessModifyHandler`/`ProcessModifyHandler` (guard + 4) owns ModifyProcess + its session-release. `ProcessDesigner` is now a thin facade (buildHandler, modifyHandler, guard, userTaskCatalog, describer = 5): delegates build/modify, runs list/describe as guarded pass-throughs. Guard is called inside each handler's try (build/modify) and the facade's try (list/describe) so "unauthorized → error response" behavior is preserved. DI in ClioProcessBuilderApp: register guard (needs Connection) + both handlers + facade (all compose from registered services → plain AddScoped, no ActivatorUtilities/Connection). New capability now lands in a focused handler, not the shared ctor.
Tests: moved BuildProcess tests → new ProcessBuildHandlerTests (7), ModifyProcess → ProcessModifyHandlerTests (5), both substituting the guard (no user-gate setup needed). Real gate → new ProcessDesignGuardTests (authorized-passes, missing-op-throws; the non-General branch is NOT unit-testable — TestFramework's mocked SysUserInfo.ConnectionType can't be driven off General, and the old ProcessDesignerSecurityTests never covered it either). ProcessDesignerOrchestratorTests rewritten to facade-level (delegation + list/describe guard wiring). Deleted ProcessDesignerSecurityTests (coverage split into guard + facade tests).
Files: package src IProcessDesignGuard.cs, ProcessDesignGuard.cs, IProcessBuildHandler.cs, ProcessBuildHandler.cs, IProcessModifyHandler.cs, ProcessModifyHandler.cs (new); ProcessDesigner.cs, ClioProcessBuilderApp.cs (mod). Tests: ProcessBuildHandlerTests.cs, ProcessModifyHandlerTests.cs, ProcessDesignGuardTests.cs (new); ProcessDesignerOrchestratorTests.cs, ProcessDesignerRoundTripTests.cs (mod); ProcessDesignerSecurityTests.cs (deleted).
Verify: package 298 pass / 1 known-unrelated pre-existing fail. Optional further step (not done): group {parameterService, mappingService, filterApplier} into an IProcessContentApplier to drop the build handler from 7→5.

## 2026-07-07 – ENG-91842: architecture-review batch (core reuse + DRY + edit-rep guard)
Context: user asked for a critical architecture pass + "could core be reused?" Ran 3 parallel analysts (enum reuse, serialization/column reuse, architecture critique), then "делай все".
Decision + changes (all package unless noted):
- **Core enum reuse (ProcessDesignConstants.Filters):** replaced ~37 magic wire codes with (int)core-enum values, kept const (enum members are compile-time constants) and FULLY-QUALIFIED to dodge the nested `Filters` name clash. FilterType/DataValueType/FunctionType/DatePart → Terrasoft.Core.Entities.Filters.*; ComparisonType → Terrasoft.Core.Entities.FilterComparisonType; ExpressionType → EntitySchemaQueryExpressionType (member SchemaColumn=0); Logical → Terrasoft.Common.LogicalOperationStrict (NOT LogicalOperation — And=1 trap). Macros stays hand-coded (client-only primary-column values 34/35/36/41 absent from the reachable C# enum + IsDateKind/RequiresArgument metadata). Compiler now re-binds the codes on upgrade.
- **Column-path reuse:** ResolveColumn now calls EntitySchema.FindSchemaColumnByPath (splits, hops lookups via ReferenceSchema, caches) instead of hand-walking split + FindInstanceByUId; ~30 lines → ~8, drops the 2nd manager lookup. VERIFIED the test mock (TestEntitySchemaManager) supports the real method incl. Account.Code lookup-hop (59 filter tests green).
- **DRY:** ResolveReference reuses ProcessSchemaElementLocator.ResolveElement (killed the 4th inline copy); one shared FilterConditionDescriptor.HasReference predicate now used by BOTH serializer + signal guard (was two divergent definitions); deleted dead AddSingleton<ILog> + now-unused Common.Logging using + LoggerName const; aligned clio DescribedSignal.On doc (single event, not "combination").

## 2026-07-06 11:10 – Release 8.1.0.71: CI smoke-test broke on packageSourceMapping (--add-source)
Context: Merged PR #811 (BL-1 --json envelope) to master and cut release 8.1.0.71. The GitHub tag+release published fine but the release-to-nuget workflow FAILED at the "Verify packaged tool version" smoke step, so "Publish to NuGet" was skipped — the package never reached NuGet.
Decision: Root-caused to CI infra, not the release content: the smoke step ran `dotnet tool install clio --add-source ./output`, and newer NuGet SDKs hard-reject `--add-source` when the repo nuget.config has <packageSourceMapping> active ("The --add-source option cannot be combined with package source mapping"). The identical step + identical nuget.config passed on 8.1.0.70 (02.07) under the older SDK — only the self-hosted runner's SDK changed. Fix (PR #819): the smoke step now writes a dedicated temp nuget.config at step time (clio -> local ./output source; * (+ creatio.client) -> nuget.org; Terrasoft.*/Creatio.* -> mirror, mirroring the repo config) and installs with `--configfile` instead of `--add-source`. Then re-cut the release: deleted tag+release 8.1.0.71 and recreated it on the fixed master HEAD (2e5890b1) so the `release: published` event re-ran the workflow with the fixed file — Test/Pack/Verify/Publish all green, clio.8.1.0.71.nupkg pushed to nuget.org.
Discovery: (1) A `release: [published]` workflow checks out the TAG's commit, so a fix committed to master after tagging does NOT apply to a re-run — the tag must be moved to a commit that already contains the fix (delete+recreate release with `gh release create <tag> --target <full-sha>`; short SHA / stale tag errors with "Release.target_commitish is invalid"). (2) PowerShell here-strings inside a YAML `run: |` block: the closing `"@` must land at column 0 AFTER YAML strips the block's base indent — align `@"`/`"@` to the run block's own indent (10 spaces here), verified by parsing the YAML and checking the delimiter columns. (3) The workflow filename is misspelled `.github/workflows/reliase-to-nuget.yml` — grep by content, not by expected name.
Files: .github/workflows/reliase-to-nuget.yml (PR #819)
Impact: Release publishing is resilient to the runner's NuGet source-mapping enforcement; future X.Y.Z.W releases no longer need `--add-source`. If a release's NuGet publish fails after the tag is cut, fix on master then delete+recreate the release targeting the fixed full SHA rather than re-running the old workflow.

## 2026-07-07 – CORRECTION to the discovery-regression p.4 "wrapper friction" (it was a harness artifact)
Context: User pushed back on the prior entry's finding #4 (every fresh agent's FIRST MCP call fails on the {"args":{...}} envelope), noting ENG-92653 / ENG-92761 / ENG-92462 were supposed to address this. Investigated the three tickets + the live inputSchemas.
Decision/finding: My p.4 was a FALSE POSITIVE caused by MY bridge, not a clio regression. Root cause: mcp_bridge.py `list` printed only name+description and HID each tool's inputSchema, so the sandboxed subagents hand-built JSON blind and guessed top-level fields → hit the McpToolErrorFilter wrapper hint → self-corrected. A real MCP client (Claude Code) injects the full inputSchema, which correctly advertises the envelope. Verified against the live net10 build:
  - ENG-92653 fix IS present: clio-run.args inputSchema = {"type":["object","null"]} (the untyped-args bug that made Claude Code drop the object is fixed).
  - Resident tools (get-guidance/list-packages/get-tool-contract) expose args typed as object with inner props and required:["args"] — the envelope is fully self-describing.
  - ENG-92761 (resident flag + core-rules line) present; ENG-92462 is an e2e-runtime perf task, unrelated to wrapping.
Proof: added inputSchema to the bridge `list` output (faithful-client parity) and re-ran the same two tasks. Ground-truth logs: env-profile retest = 3 calls, 0 wrapper failures (get-tool-contract{}, get-tool-contract{tool-names}, clio-run{command,args}); inventory retest = list-packages/list-apps, 0 wrapper failures. First-attempt correct wrapping in BOTH the resident {"args":{...}} shape and the clio-run {"command","args"} envelope. Prior run (schema hidden) had a 1st-call wrapper failure on 4/4 agents; with schema shown it is 0/N.
Files: scratchpad/mcp_bridge.py (list now emits inputSchema), t1/t2 retest logs; no repo changes.
Impact: The three tickets hold — do NOT reopen on the strength of the earlier p.4. Lesson for this discovery-regression recipe: the bridge MUST surface each tool's inputSchema in `list`, else you measure the harness's blind-spot, not the server. The real (schema-typed) client wraps correctly first try. Any future "wrapper friction" claim must be reproduced with schema exposed before it counts.

## 2026-07-09 – Enumerate the full macro vocabulary in process-modeling guidance
Context: During manual testing a second agent doubted whether `CurrentHalfYear` is supported and nearly rolled it back. Root cause: the process-modeling guidance listed macros as `Today | Yesterday | CurrentUser | CurrentYear | NextNDays | …` — a truncated example list that never named the HalfYear (or Hour, or recurring "every year") families, so an agent reading the guide couldn't confirm them and (wrongly) assumed the designer/platform lacked them.
Decision: Replaced the truncated example with a dedicated bullet listing the COMPLETE macro set grouped by family — relative periods (Yesterday/Today/Tomorrow + Previous/Current/Next × Week/Month/Quarter/HalfYear/Year/Hour), argument macros (NextNDays/PreviousNDays/NextNHours/PreviousNHours + macroArgument), recurring "every year" (DayOfYearToday/DayOfYearTodayPlusDaysOffset/NextNDaysOfYear/PreviousNDaysOfYear), and system/lookup (CurrentUser/CurrentUserContact). Also stated explicitly that an unknown macro is REJECTED at build (validated against the platform catalog via MacrosCatalog.Resolve), NOT silently accepted — closing the "the API just took the string" misconception (that caution is true for the `expression`/formula path, not for `macro`).
Discovery: `CurrentHalfYear` IS fully supported — MacrosCatalog binds it to `(int)Terrasoft.Core.Entities.EntitySchemaQueryMacrosType.CurrentHalfYear` (server enum; the package compiles against it, so the member exists and resolves at runtime). The designer has the Half-Year submenu (user screenshots this session). Only the 4 primary-column macros are genuinely client-only.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Resources/ProcessDesigner/ProcessModelingGuidanceResource.cs
Impact: clio compiles clean (net10.0); no test asserts the process-modeling macro text (safe). Future agents can confirm HalfYear/Hour/every-year macros from the guide instead of guessing.

## 2026-07-09 00:00 – Port `register-sso-provider` command from creatio-identity-platform-cli
Context: User asked to replicate the identity-platform-cli `sso register-provider` command in clio.
Decision: Added `register-sso-provider` (alias `sso-register-provider`) as a `RemoteCommand<RegisterSsoProviderOptions>` extending `IdentityCommandOptions` (gives `--format text|json`). The source CLI trial-and-errors both routes because it only has a URL; clio knows IsNetCore, so a deterministic route is cleaner. `BaseCommandTests<T>` enforces 4 doc artifacts via ReadmeChecker: Commands.md index entry, help/en/<verb>.txt, docs/commands/<verb>.md, and a Wiki/WikiAnchors.txt line.

## 2026-07-09 00:30 – register-sso-provider: two runtime fixes found via live run
Context: User's F5 run exited 0 with NO output (VS swallowed the parser exception). Ran the built clio.exe directly to surface the real error.
Discovery: (1) Option-name collision — `EnvironmentOptions` (CommandLineOptions.cs:13) already declares a hidden `--url` alias for `--uri`, so my `--url` made CommandLineParser throw "Sequence contains more than one matching element" during verb matching → renamed the option to `--issuer-url` (C# property stays `Url`). Lesson: check the base option long-names in clio/Command/CommandLineOptions.cs before naming a new [Option]; hidden aliases count. (2) `--IsNetCore` is `bool?` not `bool`, so CommandLineParser requires an explicit value — `--IsNetCore true`, a bare `--IsNetCore` errors "has no value". Also hardened ProceedResponse to fail on non-JSON responses (was reporting false success on HTML/404 bodies). Verified end-to-end against a live net8 stand: server returned {Id,Code,Name} (PascalCase) and exit 0.
Files: clio/Command/RegisterSsoProviderCommand.cs, clio/help/en/register-sso-provider.txt, clio/docs/commands/register-sso-provider.md, clio.tests/Command/RegisterSsoProviderCommandTests.cs
Impact: register-sso-provider confirmed working. Two reusable gotchas recorded: base hidden `--url` alias, and `bool?` options needing explicit values.

## 2026-07-09 01:15 – register-sso-provider: routing corrected to standard convention
Context: My initial route logic was inverted (netcore→/0, framework→no /0), copied from the source identity-platform-cli comment. User confirmed the target stand is .NET Framework and it needs /0, i.e. the standard clio convention: NetCore→no /0, Framework→/0.
Decision: Dropped the custom absolute-URL ServicePath and its IsNetCore branch; ServicePath is now the relative "/api/SsoProvider/Register" and RemoteCommand.RootPath (IsNetCore ? Uri : Uri+"/0") supplies the /0 prefix — same rule as every other clio RemoteCommand. Flipped the two routing unit tests accordingly. Also improved ProceedResponse: a bare JSON-string body (e.g. "SsoProvider with Code 'x' already exists.") is now surfaced verbatim as the failure message instead of the generic "non-JSON response" text (added TryGetJsonStringMessage).
Discovery: Verified live against the Framework stand — calling WITHOUT --IsNetCore routes to /0/api/SsoProvider/Register and succeeds (Test3code created). On this stand a POST to /api/SsoProvider/Register (no /0) returns an empty body (route not matched). Empirical platform check: POST /ServiceModel/AuthService.svc/Login → 200 at root. Note: earlier "success" runs used --IsNetCore true against a framework stand, which under the OLD inverted code produced /0 by accident — masking the bug. Lesson: don't trust a cross-repo routing comment over clio's own RootPath convention.
Files: clio/Command/RegisterSsoProviderCommand.cs, clio.tests/Command/RegisterSsoProviderCommandTests.cs, clio/docs/commands/register-sso-provider.md

Discovery: the live run immediately surfaced that Story 15's own E2E fixtures called long-tail MCP tools (11 of the 15 touched tools — everything except list-apps/get-app-info/list-app-sections/get-component-info, the 4 resident in lazy-mode tools/list per ENG-90312/92761) DIRECTLY by name via tools/call, which only resolves resident tools and returns "Unknown tool: '<name>'" for the rest. A real client MUST reach the long tail via `clio-run` (`{"command":"<tool>","args":{...}}`) — `clio-run` forwards its own "args" field verbatim to the target's SDK-native binding, so wrapping is purely mechanical and preserves each tool's existing wrapped-record vs. flat-parameter shape. The AC-03 registered-env no-regression leg's identical direct-by-name bug was MASKED by its own deliberately narrow assertion (checks only for the ABSENCE of the passthrough-rejection text, which "Unknown tool" also satisfies) — a false green. Separately, the two pre-existing ENG-93208 describe-environment two-tenant tests assumed the response echoes the target host; it doesn't (coreVersion + seed-data GUIDs only) — both live tenants shared identical seed-data GUIDs (same base image) but differed on coreVersion, so the fix uses a response-level "not byte-identical + both carry real metadata" proof instead of a specific field value.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/McpHttpMultiTenantE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/McpHttpConcurrencyIsolationE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/McpHttpNoRegressionE2ETests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/McpHttpPassthroughStand.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/McpHttpServerSession.cs, spec/stories/story-mcp-passthrough-tool-parity-15.md
Impact: Final live result 55/55 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, across two real tenants. Any FUTURE MCP E2E fixture that calls a tool NOT in the lazy-mode resident set (get-tool-contract / tools/list) must route through clio-run — direct tools/call by name silently produces "Unknown tool", and assertions that only check for a specific rejection substring can mask that failure as a false pass. Worth a general callout for anyone authoring new MCP E2E coverage, not just this feature.

Context: continuing sequential Story 2->8 implementation; Story 7 reconciles the ENG-93208 legacy platform-api-key gate with the new OAuth front door now that Stories 5/6 protect the whole endpoint and gate credential-capture on the authenticated principal.
Decision: ADR D-6 already resolved OQ-D (retire as default, keep as opt-in dev/offline fallback) -- implemented literally: EnforcePlatformApiKeyGate takes a new `authorizationEnabled` param; when true it bypasses the legacy key check entirely and derives PassthroughEnabledItemKey from `context.User.Identity.IsAuthenticated` alone (RequireAuthorization from Story 5 already guaranteed it); when false, byte-for-byte unchanged pre-ENG-93386 behavior. Context: Alex asked to open the PR, then to run a codex-CLI review on it.
Decision: pushed feature/ENG-93386-mcp-http-standard-authorization and opened PR #846, stacked on the still-open PR #830 (base=claude/clio-mcp-multi-tenant-73a807, not master) -- matches the ENG-93208 stacking precedent. Codex found 2 real P2 issues in the Story-8 final-review fixes themselves (a second-pass catch on code written just hours earlier):
1. `IsPublicBind` reused the narrow `IsLoopbackAlias` (4-literal set) instead of a full loopback-range parser, so `127.0.0.2` would have been misclassified as public and refused a harmless local bind -- fixed by promoting `TargetUrlValidator.IsLoopbackIpOrLocalhost` (private->internal) and reusing it.
2. The e2e `OAuthClientCredentialsTokenFetcher` sent the documented comma-separated scope list verbatim as the OAuth `scope` form field; RFC 6749 requires space-delimited -- fixed with a `ToSpaceDelimitedScope` normalizer.
Discovery: even a feature that just passed a 3-reviewer adversarial gate can have a follow-up review (different tool, different angle) catch something real -- codex caught a regression I introduced IN the fix for the adversarial review's own finding (IsPublicBind). Worth running an independent second-opinion review after fixing first-pass findings, not just after the original implementation.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/McpHttpServerCommand.cs (IsPublicBind), clio/Command/McpServer/TargetUrlValidator.cs (IsLoopbackIpOrLocalhost visibility), clio.tests/Command/McpServer/PublicBindGuardTests.cs (+2 tests), clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/OAuthClientCredentialsTokenFetcher.cs (ToSpaceDelimitedScope).

## 2026-07-10 – Fix get-syssetting alias writing empty value (data-loss footgun)
Context: Ticket — `clio get-syssetting <code>` (alias of set-syssetting) read mode was gated solely by --get, so a value-less get fell through to the write path and POSTed {"<code>":""} via PostSysSettingsValues, silently clearing the setting. Value-less `set-syssetting <code>` did the same.
Decision: Two-layer fix. (1) Program.NormalizeGetSysSettingArgs — when args[0]=="get-syssetting" (case-insensitive) and no --get present, append --get so the get alias resolves to the read path; wired into NormalizeCommandLineArgs (runs for dispatch/help/version, harmless for the latter two). (2) SysSettingsCommand.Execute — write path now returns 1 with a user-facing error when opts.Value is null (defense in depth; also covers the scenario/YAML runner which builds options directly via Activator and bypasses arg normalization). Also added a WriteWarning when a value is supplied on the get path (value ignored, read-only) — from review Finding 1.
Discovery: CommandLineParser does NOT surface which alias invoked a verb, so alias→read intent must be handled at the arg-normalization layer (same pattern as create-data-binding --environment→-e and the --json bare-flag injection). Cut line is `opts.Value is null` (omitted positional) NOT IsNullOrEmpty — an explicit `set-syssetting code ""` stays a legitimate "set empty" write, consistent between CLI and YAML. Scenario runner (YAML/Step.cs) constructs SysSettingsOptions directly, which is exactly why the Execute-level guard (not just normalization) is load-bearing. Base BaseClioModuleTests.TearDown is [TearDown] virtual — override it (call base) to avoid CS0114; several sibling fixtures still hide it (pre-existing warnings).
Files: clio/Program.cs, clio/Command/SysSettingsCommand.cs, clio.tests/Command/SysSettings.cs (refactored fixture to DI-container SUT resolution per convention), clio.tests/Command/SysSettingArgsNormalizationTests.cs (new), clio/help/en/set-syssetting.txt, clio/docs/commands/set-syssetting.md. MCP reviewed, no update required (get/set/list/create-sys-setting tools are separate and already read/write-correct; TryUpdateSysSetting already rejects null value).
Impact: get-syssetting now reads; a value-less write can never clear a setting. Validated: dotnet test --filter "Category=Unit" (full suite, 5418 passed / 0 failed on net8.0; Program.cs change = full-suite trigger).

## 2026-07-10 - ENG-93370 Story 1 implemented (compatibility catalog + registry fail-fast)
Context: started implementation. Story 1 = the durable core (IMcpToolCompatibilityCatalog) + registry collision fail-fast.
Decision/Discovery: (1) CLIO005 only tracks EXPLICIT Add*<T>()/typeof registrations - clio's reflection-loop RegisterAssemblyInterfaceTypes (AddTransient(ifaceVar, typeVar)) is INVISIBLE to it, so a new I*-interface auto-registers as transient and is NOT flagged even while unconsumed (Story 2 consumes it). So the catalog needs no clio-run wiring in Story 1. (2) ValidateOnBuild=true constructs every transient at container build across the whole suite -> the catalog's ctor validation runs eagerly for free (satisfies H9 "eager"). (3) restart-by-environmentName legacy [McpServerTool] method removal MOVED to Story 2 (atomic with the handler that reads the catalog) to avoid a regression window where nothing serves the alias. (4) Registry silent-first-duplicate (McpToolInvokerRegistry.cs:112) -> throw InvalidOperationException; zero dup names today so it only fires on authoring mistakes, surfaced at ValidateOnBuild startup. nameof(IMcpToolCompatibilityCatalog) resolves cross-namespace (Tools nested under McpServer). (5) Nullable disabled project-wide (no <Nullable>), LangVersion 12; internal ctor for tests (IVT clio.tests) - DI uses only public ctors so no ambiguity.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/McpToolCompatibilityCatalog.cs (new: interface + record + 2 enums + validated impl + seed), clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/McpToolInvokerRegistry.cs (fail-fast), clio.tests/Command/McpServer/McpToolCompatibilityCatalogTests.cs (9 tests).
Validated: dotnet build clio.csproj net8.0 clean (0 err, 0 new CLIO warnings); dotnet test --filter "Category=Unit&Module=McpServer" net8.0 = 1868 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip.
Impact: catalog ready for Story 2 handler to consume; alias map + fail-fast validation proven.

## 2026-07-11 – `clio config` deploy-creatio defaults for Explorer right-click
Context: The Windows Explorer "clio: deploy Creatio" action runs `clio deploy-creatio --zip-file "%1"` with no other args, so it falls through to Kubernetes/Rancher. Users had no way to make it deploy to a local DB + Redis.
Decision: New `config` verb (General group) persists a `deploy-creatio-defaults` block in appsettings.json (db-server-name, redis-server-name, site-name, site-port, deployment). A new `IDeployCreatioDefaultsResolver` fills options omitted on the CLI from those defaults and derives a site name from the zip file name when none is set; it runs at the very start of `InstallerCommand.Execute` BEFORE the `_kubernetes is FakeKubernetes && DbServerName empty` guard, so a configured default db-server-name routes the plain Explorer deploy to local. Explicit CLI flags always win.
Discovery: The K8s-vs-local branch keys solely off `options.DbServerName`, so injecting defaults pre-guard is the single lever needed. The interactive STEP-1 site-name loop in CreatioInstallerService only runs `while (SiteName is empty)`, so any explicit --site-name (and now a derived one) already bypasses the existing-site collision prompt — derivation is consistent with existing --site-name behavior, not a new regression. `SanitizeSiteName` restricts to ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_] and prefixes a leading digit with `_` because real Creatio build zips start with a version (10.1.257_...), which is otherwise an invalid unquoted DB identifier.
Files: clio/Command/ConfigCommand.cs, clio/Command/CreatioInstallCommand/DeployCreatioDefaultsResolver.cs, clio/Command/CreatioInstallCommand/InstallerCommand.cs (ctor + ApplyDefaults call + shared AllowedDeploymentMethods/AutoDeploymentMethod consts), clio/Environment/ConfigurationOptions.cs + ISettingsRepository.cs (DeployCreatioDefaults + get/set), clio/BindingsModule.cs, clio/Program.cs, clio/HelpSystem/CommandHelpCatalog.cs, docs (help/en/config.txt, docs/commands/config.md, Commands.md, Wiki/WikiAnchors.txt), tests (ConfigCommandTests, DeployCreatioDefaultsResolverTests, SettingsRepositoryDeployDefaultsTests + 2 updated InstallerCommand ctor call sites).
MCP: reviewed — not applicable. `config` is a local-workstation config command with no agent value (writes appsettings.json). deploy-creatio's existing MCP tool contract is unchanged: defaults are applied inside InstallerCommand, the tool's arguments/descriptions/destructive flags are untouched.
Impact: `clio config --deploy-db-server-name my-local-postgres --deploy-site-port 40018 --deploy-deployment iis` makes the right-click deploy target local DB+Redis with zero further args. Validated: full Unit tier 5475 passed (both net8.0/net10.0); Command+Core 2416 passed after 3-lens pre-PR review fixes (leading-digit/ASCII sanitization, explicit --show, site-port range validation, shared deployment-method constants).

## 2026-07-14 14:08 – Make MCP progress waits timeout-safe
Context: TeamCity build 15725495 failed unrelated PR #866 because the corrupt-archive deploy progress test received a stale partial snapshot after its terminal-event wait timed out.
Decision: Replace polling with notification-driven wakeups, recheck one final snapshot at the timeout boundary, and throw a secret-safe diagnostic timeout rather than returning unsatisfied data.
Discovery: The old cancellation path broke out of its delay without refreshing the queue, so a boundary-arriving terminal event could be present while the caller still received the previous stage-only snapshot.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/McpServerSession.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/DeployUninstallProgressTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/AGENTS.md, spec/mcp-progress-wait-timeout/
Impact: Shared MCP E2E runs no longer convert a timeout race into misleading event-order failures, while genuine missing terminal events fail explicitly with safe diagnostics.

## 2026-07-14 15:02 – Isolate and order MCP progress assertions
Context: The first comprehensive review of issue #876 found that the fixture-wide capture queue could leak terminal events across invocations, accumulate wakeups, and format an unbounded diagnostic history; repeated validation then reproduced concurrent callback ordering as a separate flake.
Decision: Scope every wait to an explicit progress token, coalesce notification wakeups, cap diagnostics to the latest 20 matching notifications, and replay typed events by their protocol sequence before asserting order.
Discovery: MCP notification handlers can complete out of arrival order even within one request, so queue insertion order is not the protocol order; the versioned sequence field is authoritative and matches ClioRing's ordered-buffering contract.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/McpServerSession.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/DeployUninstallProgressTests.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/AGENTS.md, spec/mcp-progress-wait-timeout/
Impact: Ten fresh-process fixture runs passed on each of net8.0 and net10.0 without installing or uninstalling Creatio, while unrelated streams can no longer satisfy a wait.

## 2026-07-14 15:18 – Keep opaque progress tokens out of diagnostics
Context: Final security review found that timeout text echoed the caller-supplied progress token even though opaque correlation values may contain sensitive identifiers and failures are written to CI logs.
Decision: Use the token only for in-memory stream filtering, omit it from exception text, and cover the rule with a secret-shaped unrelated token.
Discovery: Secret-safe typed-event summaries do not require exposing the correlation key used to select the stream.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/McpServerSession.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/DeployUninstallProgressTests.cs, spec/mcp-progress-wait-timeout/mcp-progress-wait-timeout-qa.md
Impact: Timeout diagnostics retain event, sequence, stage, status, and outcome evidence without leaking opaque caller input.

## 2026-07-14 15:36 – Require complete progress streams and broadcast wakeups
Context: Final quality and testing reviews found that a terminal callback could arrive before lower sequences and that one shared consuming semaphore could wake the wrong token waiter.
Decision: Broadcast each notification through a versioned task-completion signal, compare typed progress-token values, and require a distinct contiguous sequence from zero through terminal before completing a wait.
Discovery: Sorting a partial snapshot cannot recover callbacks that have not arrived; terminal presence proves completeness only when every preceding sequence is already captured. This supersedes the earlier coalescing-semaphore decision.
Files: clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Mcp/McpServerSession.cs, clio.mcp.e2e/DeployUninstallProgressTests.cs, spec/mcp-progress-wait-timeout/
Impact: Deterministic terminal-first and typed-token regressions pass, and the five-test fixture passed ten fresh-process runs on each of net8.0 and net10.0 without real Creatio lifecycle operations.

## 2026-07-14 - ENG-93208 PR #830: systemic fix for the WorkspaceSyncTool CwdLock Major (tetiana-moshon)
Context: PR #830's last remaining blocker was a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` Major from tetiana-moshon on `WorkspaceCommandToolBase.ExecuteInWorkspace`: it pinned process-wide cwd (`SetCurrentDirectory`) around the ENTIRE network-bound `push-workspace`/`restore-workspace` install/restore under the single global `McpToolExecutionLock.CwdLock` — the same lock `PageSyncTool.WriteVerifiedBodyFile` takes to anchor page output to cwd, so any tenant's push/restore head-of-line-blocked every OTHER tenant's page-sync for the whole network call. A narrow lock-scoping fix was rejected up front: the workspace/package machinery reads process cwd transitively in multiple places (`WorkingDirectoriesProvider.CurrentDirectory`, `PackageArchiver`/`PackageDownloader`/`BasePackageInstaller`/`CreatioPackage` cwd fallbacks), so shrinking the lock without removing the cwd dependency would reintroduce the exact cross-tenant race the lock existed to prevent.
Decision: Two Explore-agent audits (dispatched before touching code) found (1) the ENTIRE push/restore call graph (`Workspace.Install`/`Restore` → `WorkspaceInstaller`/`WorkspaceRestorer` → `PackageArchiver.Pack`/`ZipPackages`, `BasePackageInstaller`, `PackageBuilder`, `ComposableApplicationManager`) resolves every path through `IWorkspacePathBuilder.PackagesFolderPath`/etc — EVERY raw `Environment.CurrentDirectory`/`GetCurrentDirectoryIfEmpty` site in that graph is a dead branch already guarded by a non-empty explicit argument; the only real seam is `IWorkspacePathBuilder.RootPath` (already settable — `Workspace.PublishToFile`/`PublishToFolder` already use it); (2) `IWorkspacePathBuilder` is registered `AddSingleton` in `BindingsModule.cs`, but `BindingsModule.Register` builds a BRAND-NEW `ServiceProvider` per call, cached PER-TENANT by `SessionContainerCache` (keyed off credentials) — so "Singleton" means per-tenant-container, not process-global; two different tenants already get two different `IWorkspacePathBuilder` instances. This made a PLAIN mutable field (no `AsyncLocal`) provably safe — advisor flagged this exact fork before implementation ("storage and lock structure are coupled": AsyncLocal needs no lock, a plain field on a per-tenant singleton needs the existing per-tenant lock to stay wrapped, NOT dropped). Implementation: `WorkspaceCommandToolBase.ExecuteInWorkspace` now resolves `IWorkspacePathBuilder` via a newly-`private protected` `BaseTool.ResolveFromCallContainer<TService>` (was `private`) — the SAME per-tenant container `execute()`'s `InternalExecute<TCommand>` resolves the command from — sets `.RootPath = workspacePath` for the duration of `execute()` inside the KEPT `ExecuteUnderTenantLock` wrapper (guards the SAME tenant's own concurrent calls), and resets it to `null` in `finally`. The `SetCurrentDirectory`/`CwdLock` pin is gone entirely for this tool; zero changes to `Workspace.cs`/`WorkspaceInstaller.cs`/`WorkspaceRestorer.cs`/`PushWorkspaceCommand.cs`/`RestoreWorkspaceCommand.cs`/`BindingsModule.cs` — the fix is confined to `Command/McpServer/Tools/{BaseTool,WorkspaceSyncTool,McpToolExecutionLock}.cs`.
Discovery: the extra `ResolveFromCallContainer<IWorkspacePathBuilder>(options)` call happens BEFORE `execute()`'s own `ResolveCommand<TCommand>` gate, so an unknown/unreachable environment now throws `EnvironmentResolutionException` a step earlier than before — without a matching catch this would have regressed `WorkspaceSyncContractToolE2ETests.PushWorkspace_Should_Report_Invalid_Environment`/`RestoreWorkspace_Should_Report_Invalid_Environment` (expect graceful exit code 1, not an unhandled exception). Added a `catch (EnvironmentResolutionException) → FromResolverError` / `catch (Exception) → FromException` mirroring `InternalExecute<TCommand>`'s own resolve-catch exactly, plus a new unit test reproducing it (`PushWorkspace_Should_Report_Unresolvable_Environment_Gracefully`). `ResolveFromCallContainer<TService>(options)` (single-arg, no gates) does NOT invoke `EnforcePackageRequirements`/`EnforceCreatioVersionRequirements` — those live only in `ResolveCommand<TCommand>` — so no double-gate risk.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/{BaseTool,WorkspaceSyncTool,McpToolExecutionLock}.cs; clio.tests/Command/McpServer/WorkspaceSyncToolTests.cs (rewrote the two "executes from requested workspace" tests to assert `IWorkspacePathBuilder.RootPath` instead of `Directory.GetCurrentDirectory()`, since asserting cwd literally tested the OLD pin mechanism; added a deterministic CwdLock-non-blocking test using a background-thread lock holder + Stopwatch, and the unresolvable-environment regression test).
Verify: full Unit suite green both net8.0 and net10.0 (6213/0/39 each) after the exception-handling fix; McpServer module alone 2340/0/1 on net8.0. Existing `WorkspaceSyncToolE2ETests`/`WorkspaceSyncContractToolE2ETests` (push/restore against a real sandbox + invalid-environment contract) already exercise the changed root-resolution path end-to-end — no new e2e test added; TeamCity MCP e2e run recommended before merge. ClioRing reviewed: grepped `clio-ring/ClioRing.Ipc`, `clio-ring/ClioRing`, `clio-ring/ClioRing.Desktop/actions.json` for `push-workspace`/`restore-workspace`/`PushWorkspace`/`RestoreWorkspace`/`WorkspaceSyncTool` — zero matches, Ring does not consume this tool surface. MCP contract (tool names, args, destructive flags, error message text) unchanged — prompts/resources/docs need no update.
Impact: push-workspace/restore-workspace no longer contend for `McpToolExecutionLock.CwdLock` at all, closing the cross-tenant head-of-line-blocking Major from tetiana-moshon without weakening isolation — resolves the last CHANGES_REQUESTED item on PR #830.

Context: A follow-up agent-assisted review (b-horodyskyi) on PR #830 flagged one Major security finding, one Major (explicitly non-blocking) performance finding, and one Minor doc-drift finding.
Decision: (1) `BaseTool.ExecuteResolved`'s two catch blocks handed `ex.Message`/`$"{ex.Message} [{ex.ErrorCode}]"` straight to the tool's `onFailure` factory unredacted — every other MCP error path (`CommandExecutionResult.FromException`, `McpToolErrorFilter`, the per-tool `SensitiveErrorTextRedactor.Redact(ex.Message)` pattern used by ~40 other tools) redacts before crossing the MCP boundary. Impact: closes the FR-11-style redaction gap on the one typed-response path (`ExecuteResolved`) that had bypassed the PR's own secret-hygiene sweep, and corrects security-relevant precedence documentation that could mislead a future gateway integrator. ## 2026-07-15 10:30 – Clean IIS application-pool profiles during uninstall
Context: Issue #881 required uninstall-creatio to remove the actual IIS virtual-account profile when possible and complete successfully with one warning when Windows keeps it locked.

## 2026-07-17 — ENG-93373 review-gate fixes
Context: 3 parallel reviewers (correctness/concurrency, security/contract, test-coverage) on the working diff.
Decision: (1) SECURITY HIGH — gate `readOnly||idempotent` wrongly bounded idempotent SERVER writes (install-gate/generate-source-code/add-package-dependency) with "safe to retry" → concurrent-duplicate-write risk. Narrowed gate to `!destructive && (readOnly || toolName=="get-page")`; Idempotent hint dropped; get-page admitted by explicit one-tool allowlist (Creatio read + local-only write). (2) M2 — reordered ObserveAndDispose before ThrowIfCancellationRequested. (3) M3 — separate delayCts cancels the deadline timer on fast completion (no lingering 120s timer). (4) L5 — workCts disposed in the observe-continuation after work completes, not synchronously (avoids ObjectDisposedException on a cooperative tool). (5) Test HIGH — added clio-run e2e (execute-esq via clio-run, the primary long-tail vector) proving inner-dispatch bounding.
Discovery: execute-esq is NON-resident + ReadOnly → clio-run is the PRIMARY long-tail read vector (agents reach non-resident tools via clio-run per core-rules), durable handler is the raw-name fallback. execute-esq expects a SelectQuery OBJECT (rootSchemaName), not SQL; its internal timeout 30s > 1s read-deadline. H1 (abandoned read holds per-tenant Monitor / parks pool thread) and M4 (abandoned DispatchAsync restores shared RequestContext late) accepted+documented as the same single-session detach trade-off as the write path (benign: fresh context per request; agent-paced ~1 abandon/timeout). L6 (get-page cross-identity double-write) = narrow pre-existing PageFileWriter edge, same-tenant serialized, documented not fixed.
Files: same as prior entry + updated gate signature (toolName param) across McpToolErrorFilter/McpToolInvokerRegistry; ADR + AGENTS.md gate section corrected.
Impact: gate is now reads-only (never server writes); all 3 dispatch vectors (filter/clio-run/durable) bounded; 2 e2e (filter + clio-run) pass locally. 2420 McpServer unit tests green.

Decision: Require v1 library-bound validation before publication, validate one bounded local P-256 public-key PEM with no network/device/reparse path, and include effective key fingerprint plus configured library ID in activation identity. MCP source add/remove are destructive; add also requires explicit confirmation. info-knowledge stays local unless checkUpdates=true.
Discovery: Hot trust revocation must hash SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes rather than the path so same-path key replacement or deletion forces runtime revalidation. Synthetic v1 E2E commits must be valid full hexadecimal object IDs.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeBundleContracts.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeBundleRuntime.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeMultiSourceActivator.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeSourceManagementService.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/KnowledgeManagementTools.cs
Impact: Configured-source publication and activation can no longer fall back to legacy environment trust, and trust changes are observed without restarting MCP.

## 2026-07-19 13:20 – Isolate Git transport process environment
Context: Final security review found that inherited Git variables could redirect helpers or inject command-valued configuration during knowledge retrieval.
Decision: Added opt-in process environment clearing with an inherited-variable allowlist and absolute executable resolution; Git now inherits only OS, locale, proxy, and CA variables plus its explicit disabled configuration.
Discovery: Clearing `GIT_*` variables is insufficient if the executable remains a bare name resolved from the child working directory; resolution must occur before launch and ignore relative PATH entries.
Files: clio/Common/ProcessExecutor.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeGitTransport.cs, clio.tests/Common/ProcessExecutorTests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/KnowledgeGitTransportTests.cs
Impact: Knowledge retrieval cannot inherit `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, injected configuration, askpass, or helper settings, and launches a pinned absolute Git executable.

## 2026-07-19 13:25 – Distinguish NuGet outages from current catalogs
Context: Final correctness review found NuGet feed and package failures were reported as successful up-to-date checks when a generation was already installed.
Decision: Added an explicit failed retrieval status with a bounded diagnostic; update fails and info reports unknown, while a successfully checked catalog with no newer revision remains no-candidate.
Discovery: Transport failure must not blacklist an immutable version, but it also cannot be treated as evidence that no update exists.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeBundleContracts.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeTransportContracts.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeBundleNuGetClient.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeSourceManagementService.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/KnowledgeBundleNuGetClientTests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/KnowledgeSourceManagementServiceTests.cs
Impact: Operators no longer receive false up-to-date results during NuGet outages, timeouts, or invalid remote responses.

## 2026-07-19 14:05 – Bound Git retrieval across subprocesses
Context: Final performance review found each sequential Git command received a fresh transport timeout, allowing one retrieval to exceed its advertised operation deadline.
Decision: Start one stopwatch per retrieval, pass only the remaining budget to every Git subprocess, and classify shared-deadline exhaustion as a failed retrieval. Explicit info update checks now pass the same bounded deadline.
Discovery: Per-process timeouts do not establish an operation-wide bound when branch discovery, initialization, fetch, inspection, and archive commands run sequentially.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeGitTransport.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeSourceManagementService.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/KnowledgeGitTransportTests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/KnowledgeSourceManagementServiceTests.cs
Impact: Git-backed install, update, repair, and update-info checks cannot multiply the configured timeout by the number of Git subprocesses.

## 2026-07-19 14:10 – Complete multi-source knowledge POC hardening
Context: Final parallel review of the coordinated Clio and clio-knowledge POC found package-version, interrupted-publication, transport-failure, process-environment, and MCP mutation-classification gaps.
Decision: Bind NuGet package and signed library versions, fail closed on transport outages, reconcile only exact high-water orphan generations under both locks, use one Git operation deadline, isolate Git process state, and require destructive confirmation for install/update tools.
Discovery: A replay ledger written before an activation marker needs autonomous exact-orphan reconciliation; otherwise the correct cold-start high-water guard can make an interrupted update unrecoverable. A transport outage is not evidence that a source is up to date.

## 2026-07-18 12:00 – Redis auto-detect bounded retry (#883)
Context: deploy-creatio (--redis-db -1) hard-failed on a single transient Redis connect blip (Rancher Desktop port-forward hiccup) since ENG-90640 made FindEmptyLocalDatabase fail-fast (AbortOnConnectFail=true, ConnectRetry=1, 12s).
Decision: Added a bounded retry (MaxConnectAttempts=3) with exponential backoff (500ms→1000ms) around the connect in RedisDatabaseSelector.FindEmptyDatabase, keeping the per-attempt 12s fail-fast timeout. Extracted SelectEmptyDatabase (uses `using` to dispose the multiplexer). Retry only on transient failures; a definitive error is surfaced immediately.
Discovery: StackExchange.Redis surfaces bad credentials as RedisConnectionException with FailureType=AuthenticationFailure (not a distinct type). Naive `ex is RedisConnectionException` over-matches and would retry auth misconfig 3x (~37.5s). IsTransientConnectFailure must exclude AuthenticationFailure and ProtocolFailure. Connect+probe seam made testable via internal ctor taking Func<ConfigurationOptions,IConnectionMultiplexer> + Action<TimeSpan> (public parameterless ctor wires ConnectionMultiplexer.Connect + Thread.Sleep); DI binds the public ctor. Worst-case unreachable Redis stays bounded ~37.5s (seconds, not minutes).
Files: clio/Common/Database/RedisDatabaseSelector.cs, clio.tests/Common/Database/RedisDatabaseSelectorTests.cs, clio/docs/commands/deploy-creatio.md
Impact: A momentary blip no longer aborts deploy-creatio and leaves a half-configured ConnectionStrings.config; genuinely unreachable/auth-misconfigured Redis still fails fast. Shared selector so LocalRedisAssertion/K8RedisAssertion (assert flows) also benefit.

## 2026-07-18 12:35 – ENG-91315 restart --wait-ready + async compile-status contract
Context: Compile→restart→warm-up cycle had no first-class contract (source: ENG-91312 session atomization); agents hand-rolled ~10min of healthcheck polling after restart, and compile-creatio's fully-synchronous call hard-failed clients with a ~180s ceiling (Copilot CLI) on a 3-15min full compile.
Decision: New shared `IServerReadinessWaiter` (clio/Common) drives HealthCheckCommand for both `restart-web-app --wait-ready --ready-timeout` and CreatioInstallerService's deploy wait-ready stage (timing preserved exactly: 15s initial/45s budget for installer). MCP `restart-by-environment-name` defaults `waitReady=true` (Alex's explicit call — agents almost always want to wait, false-negative debugging in ENG-91312 outweighs latency risk) wrapped in McpProgressHeartbeat.RunWithProgressAndDeadlineAsync; on deadline returns a NEW `CommandExecutionResult.FromInfo` (exit 0 + InfoMessage) in-progress envelope pointing at `clio-run healthcheck`. `compile-creatio` gets the same deadline wrap plus a new in-memory `ICompileOperationRegistry` (singleton — explicitly skip-listed out of BindingsModule's auto-transient-scan) and a new read-only `compile-status` tool to poll it.
Discovery: `CompileCreatioTool.ExecuteFullCompile/ExecutePackageCompile` call `commandResolver.Resolve<TCommand>(options)` OUTSIDE `Execute<TOptions>`'s own try/catch — an unregistered-environment `EnvironmentResolutionException` there propagated straight out of the heartbeat work delegate, meaning `registry.Finish` never ran and the tracked operation stayed "Running" forever for the single most common failure. Caught only by the NEW e2e test chaining compile-creatio(invalid env)→compile-status(same env); no unit test had a resolver that could throw. Fixed with an explicit try/catch mirroring BaseTool's own EnvironmentResolutionException→FromResolverError / Exception→FromException handling (RestartTool didn't need this fix — it already goes through BaseTool.InternalExecute<TCommand>, which already handles it). Also: NSubstitute can proxy a concrete non-sealed class like HealthCheckCommand directly (`Substitute.For<HealthCheckCommand>(ctorArgs...)`) for waiter tests. Also: ClioRing's ClioWorkflowViewModel hardcodes `Tool = "restart-by-environment-name"` with only `environmentName` — verified compatible (no client-side call timeout, CancellationTokenSource only cancels on explicit user action, progress notifications already rendered to the output log), with one accepted UX nuance: an in-progress envelope on a slow restart still shows Ring's green "Success" badge since IsError=false, even though the app is still warming up — descriptive text remains visible in the log regardless.

## 2026-07-21 – ENG-93886: create-data-binding --help dispatch fix (Default=0 hypothesis DISCONFIRMED)
Context: `clio create-data-binding --help` returned 0 bytes (exit 0); the ticket's own suspected root cause was `Default = 0` on `CreateDataBindingOptions.InstallType`. An earlier code-analysis pass (this session's own understand-and-plan workflow) proposed removing that Default as the fix.
Decision: Did NOT touch `InstallType`/`Default=0` — empirically disconfirmed by building clio.dll and reproducing: `create-app` (`ApplicationCreateCommand.cs`, no int Option at all) is independently broken the same way (0 bytes), so a single attribute value cannot be the trigger. Instead widened `Program.TryHandleBuiltInHelp` (clio/Program.cs) with a new branch: `<verb> --help`/`-h` (verb not literally "help", not `--WEB`/`-W` mode) now short-circuits to `renderer.TryRenderCommandHelp(verb)` — the SAME call the working `clio help <verb>` branch already uses — BEFORE CommandLineSDK's own parser ever runs. Falls through unchanged when the renderer returns null (typo verbs, feature-toggled-off commands).
Discovery: (1) Confirmed root cause shape empirically, not just by inspection: a verb breaks `--help` when its name is a case-insensitive prefix of another registered verb's name AND it has no `[Verb] Aliases` AND its options class inherits `EnvironmentOptions` (create-data-binding vs. -db, create-app vs. -section both break this way; add-package/update-cli/upload-license have Aliases and work; register/remove-data-binding-row don't inherit EnvironmentOptions and work). Tested and DISCONFIRMED that adding an `Aliases` entry alone fixes it (tried on create-data-binding, temporarily, reverted) — even invoking through the newly-added alias itself still returned 0 bytes, so the trigger is deeper than the Aliases attribute; a closed-source CommandLineSDK dispatch fragility, not a single flag. (2) Proved the fix is low-risk via direct execution, not just review: `create-data-binding-db --help` and `help create-data-binding-db` were already byte-identical BEFORE this fix — meaning a working verb's `--help` already renders through this exact same `CommandHelpRenderer.TryRenderCommandHelp` path today (via `LocalHelpViewer.CheckHelp` inside CommandLineSDK's `CustomHelpViewer` hook, see `clio/WikiHelpViewer.cs`), so the new intercept changes nothing for already-working verbs (confirmed via before/after diff on create-data-binding-db, add-package, list-pages, a typo verb, and the feature-toggled-off `ring` verb — all byte-identical). (3) The fix repairs `create-app`/`create-app-section` as a free side effect (same mechanism) — deliberately left as an incidental PR callout, not a new acceptance criterion. (4) `--WEB`/`-W` mode is unaffected (explicitly excluded by the new branch, matching the exact pre-existing `args[1]` position check) — verified `_webBrowser.Enabled` is Windows-only (`WebBrowser.cs`) so this is safe to test on macOS without hitting real network/browser. (5) `CommonProgramTest.cs` (Module=Core) already has an established pattern for driving `Program.ExecuteCommands([verb, "--help"])` in-process (`add-item`, `ping`, `set-pkg-version` cases already existed) — a later code-analysis pass had wrongly claimed no such pattern existed; extended that file rather than inventing a new one. (6) Running the hidden `__generate-help-artifacts` exporter to regenerate `create-data-binding.md` also touched ~140 unrelated files (Commands.md 417 lines, WikiAnchors.txt 99 lines, help.txt 342 lines, several docs/commands/*.md deleted for now-feature-toggled/removed commands) — the committed docs have drifted badly from what the generator currently produces, unrelated to this ticket; reverted everything except the one clean `create-data-binding.md` diff and flagged the drift separately rather than bundling a ~140-file unrelated diff into a Minor help-text fix.
Files: clio/Program.cs, clio/help/en/create-data-binding.txt, clio/HelpSystem/CommandHelpCatalog.cs, clio/docs/commands/create-data-binding.md, clio.tests/CommonProgramTest.cs
Impact: `create-data-binding --help` (and `create-app`/`create-app-section --help` as a bonus) now render real help instead of silently succeeding with empty output; zero regressions (full `Category=Unit` suite: same pre-existing 19 failures before and after, all unrelated DbHub/Windows-profile/.NET-Framework environment tests, confirmed via git-stash A/B diff). Future agents: do not re-propose the `Default=0` narrow fix, and do not assume `docs/commands/*.md`/`Commands.md`/`WikiAnchors.txt` are in sync with the live exporter — check the actual diff size before committing a regeneration.

## 2026-07-21 (same day, follow-up) – ENG-93886: adversarial self-review caught a BLOCKER in the first fix version
Context: ran an independent self-review agent against the diff above before presenting it. It found that the first version's help-token scan (`normalizedArgs.Any(IsHelpFlagToken)`, matching bare `-h`/`--help` ANYWHERE in the args) hijacked any verb that already binds `-h` to its own option — `healthcheck -h <host>` (`[Option('h',"web-host")]`) and `publish-app -h <url>` (`[Option('h',"app-hub")]`, aliases ph/publish-hub/publish-workspace/publishw) silently showed help (exit 0) instead of running, with no error. Reproduced live before trusting the finding: `dotnet clio.dll healthcheck -h 192.168.1.1` printed the help screen instead of pinging the host.
Decision: replaced the blind token scan with `Program.IsUnclaimedHelpFlagToken(token, optionsType)` (now `internal static`, clio/Program.cs) - reflects over the TARGET VERB's own `[Option]` attributes (reusing the same `OptionAttribute.ShortName`/`LongName` shape `CommandHelpRenderer.BuildOptionDisplay` already reads) and only treats `-h`/`--help` as a help request when that verb has not already claimed the name for itself. `--help` (long form) collisions are not currently possible in this codebase (grepped: only 2 verbs anywhere claim short `-h`, none claim long `--help`), but the check covers both directions symmetrically rather than assuming long-form is permanently safe.
Discovery: my first regression test for this (driving `healthcheck`/`publish-app` through the full `Program.ExecuteCommands` pipeline and asserting on output/exit code or on a thrown "no environment registered" exception) passed in isolation but FAILED when the full `Category=Unit` suite ran end-to-end - some other test in the full run leaves a registered environment behind (shared static/on-disk settings state across fixtures), so "no environment registered" no longer held. `CommonProgramTest.cs` has zero precedent for driving a non-`--help` verb through `ExecuteCommands` (every existing case short-circuits on help before touching environment resolution), which is exactly why this gap wasn't already covered. Fix: test `IsUnclaimedHelpFlagToken` directly and hermetically (`typeof(PublishWorkspaceCommandOptions)` -> false, `typeof(CreateDataBindingOptions)` -> true) instead of through the full pipeline - no DI, no environment, no shared state, deterministic in isolation AND inside the full suite (re-verified: same pre-existing 19 failures, this test not among them).
Files: clio/Program.cs, clio.tests/CommonProgramTest.cs
Impact: the shared help-dispatch chokepoint (~207 verbs) no longer risks silently replacing a real command run with a help screen for any verb that owns its own `-h`/`--help`-named option, present or future. Lesson for future agents: when a fix widens a shared dispatch chokepoint, a token-presence scan over the whole args array is not enough - check whether the specific verb has already claimed that token for itself. And when a new test needs to prove "real execution happened" for a verb that requires environment/DI setup, prefer testing the underlying decision function directly over relying on incidental full-pipeline side effects (they can depend on cross-test global state and pass in isolation while flaking in the full suite).

## 2026-07-22 - Fix upload-image "File is not an image" (quoted filename)
Context: User reported upload-image broken on ts1-infr-web01/web02. Prior sessions blamed a "broken dev stand" rejecting all uploads with 200 {"error":"File is not an image."}.
Discovery: NOT the stand and NOT clio's transport. Root cause = Content-Disposition filename was QUOTED (filename="x.png"). The image API derives the image type from the filename extension with a naive parse that does not strip quotes, so it reads extension 'png"' and rejects. Proven by curl matrix: quoted=reject, unquoted=success (empty {} body) on both .NET Core (web01) and .NET Framework (web02). The earlier "broken stand + raw curl repro" was a phantom — that curl copied clio's quoted shape.
Decision: Send Content-Disposition as a raw UNQUOTED header via TryAddWithoutValidation("Content-Disposition", $"attachment; filename={Uri.EscapeDataString(fileName)}"); percent-encoding keeps non-ASCII a valid unquoted token. Ground truth: user-captured platform UI request sends `content-disposition: attachment; filename=rule_unlocks_field.png` (unquoted).
Files: clio/Common/SysImageUploader.cs, clio.tests/Command/SysImageUploaderTests.cs
Impact: upload-image + set-background-image now verified live on web01 (ASCII + Cyrillic логотип.png) and web02. Closes the long-pending Cyrillic live-verification. Test now asserts on the raw header string (no quotes) — TFM-independent, unlike the old FileName getter assertion.

## 2026-07-27 18:05 – ENG-93985: no Google Fonts @import for operating-system font families
Context: Branding agent asked build-theme for a system font (Verdana); the generated theme.css carried a Google Fonts @import for it. Reported as "theme styles are not applied".
Decision: Added Clio.Theming.SystemFontFamilies (25 curated OS-bundled names, OrdinalIgnoreCase) and filtered those families out in ThemeCssBuilder.ApplyFonts BEFORE they reach FontImportBuilder, so the family lands in --crt-font-family-* with no @import. Guarded the now-reachable empty-family case: FontImportBuilder.BuildUrl([]) would emit a malformed "css2?&display=swap". Deliberately did NOT derive the list by probing Google, and deliberately excluded Roboto/Open Sans/Lato/Montserrat/Inter plus CSS generics. Added a CollectWarnings advisory when --font-weights is passed with only system families.
Discovery: The ticket's stated cause (system fonts "are not present on Google fonts, therefore an error") is wrong for its own repro font. Google Fonts answers HTTP 200 for Verdana, Tahoma, Georgia, Times New Roman, Courier New, Trebuchet MS, Consolas, Garamond, Impact and Comic Sans MS, serving a metric-compatible substitute UNDER THE REQUESTED FAMILY NAME - so the download shadows the installed OS font instead of failing. It rejects only Arial, Segoe UI, Monaco and Lucida Sans Unicode (400). A weight-count heuristic cannot separate the two: Lato is a genuine Google family that returns only weight 400 because it ships 100/300/400/700/900. Verified in Chrome that a FAILED @import does not break sibling rules in the same sheet, so the reported "styles not applied" is NOT stylesheet death - most likely a render-blocking hang where fonts.googleapis.com is unreachable, which would equally affect a valid Google font (spring uses Playwrite NO). That exposure was descoped by the requester. Also: clio.tests does not compile on master - 54 CS0121 Assert.Throws/DoesNotThrow ambiguities from the nunit 4.6.1 pin (Directory.Packages.props:96, bumped in ebce394c), proven pre-existing by stash-and-rebuild; this blocks the AGENTS.md pre-commit targeted-test gate for every change, not just this one. Bisected: pinning nunit 4.5.0 compiles clio.tests with 0 errors, so the ambiguity is introduced somewhere in 4.6.x - a one-line pin change unblocks the whole repo. Under 4.5.0 the targeted suites pass clean (Category=Unit&Module=Theming 95/95, Module=Command 2764 passed / 15 skipped) including the 9 tests added here; the pin was reverted to 4.6.1 afterwards so this change carries no dependency edit. The diary note claiming clio.mcp.e2e cannot run locally is stale: its TargetFrameworks are conditional and resolve to net8.0 under SDK 8.0.423, and the suite runs fine.

The security lens independently proved no CSS injection is reachable through the allowlist path — every allowlist-accepted string would have passed FontImportBuilder's regex anyway — and trimming in Normalize additionally closes the pre-existing untrimmed-token sink.

## 2026-07-29 16:40 – ENG-93985 reworked: ask Google Fonts instead of curating an OS-font allowlist
Context: The allowlist approach (SystemFontFamilies + ThemeFontClassifier, 45 curated names, drift oracle, grammar invariant, ~530 changed lines) was judged too large. Requested flow: keep master's behaviour, still tell the user when a font is not in Google Fonts, and after an explicit confirmation apply it as a locally installed font with a warning that it only renders where installed. clio should hold a small check, not a big file.
Decision: Deleted SystemFontFamilies, ThemeFontClassifier and their tests; reverted ThemeCssBuilder, BuildThemeCommand, the MCP tool, guidance, help and docs to master. Added clio/Theming/GoogleFontsCatalog.cs (36 lines): one GET to fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts/<Family>, 200 -> InCatalog, 404 -> NotInCatalog, anything else or a throw -> Unverified. Registered as a typed client (AddHttpClient<IGoogleFontsCatalog, GoogleFontsCatalog>, 10s timeout) beside IContainerRegistryPreflightService. build-theme reports the result through its existing CollectWarnings channel, and a new --local-font-families list marks families the user confirmed, which ApplyFonts skips when assembling the import. No new MCP tool and no separate check verb.
Discovery: The obvious implementation is wrong. fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Verdana answers 200 and serves a metric-compatible SUBSTITUTE under the requested name, so a css2-based existence check reports Verdana as a Google font and the original bug survives. The authoritative source is the metadata endpoint: /metadata/fonts/<Family> answers 404 for Verdana, Arial, Georgia, Calibri and 200 for Roboto, Lato, Inter, Noto Sans, Cascadia Code — which also removes the two traps that defeated the allowlist heuristics (Lato is a real family that css2 serves at one weight; Noto Sans and Cascadia Code ship with some OSes yet are genuinely Google). The per-family endpoint returns 12-27 KB versus 2.7 MB for the full catalogue, so no caching or JSON array parsing is needed. Two gotchas: the endpoint is CASE-SENSITIVE (roboto -> 404, Roboto -> 200), which the guidance now states rather than papering over with title-casing that would break "PT Sans"; and Uri.ToString() unescapes percent-encoding, so the encoding test must assert against AbsoluteUri. Also note TryNormalizeOptions rebuilds BuildThemeOptions field by field — a new option silently vanishes unless added there, which cost a debugging cycle.

Decision: FontImportBuilder gained ValidateFamily(string) — the pattern stays in the class that already owns it — and ThemeCssBuilder.ApplyFonts now calls it for every non-default family BEFORE the import decision, so validation is no longer a side effect of building the import. FontImportBuilder.BuildFamilyParam's regex is the ONLY font-family validation in the codebase, and on master it was unavoidable because every non-default family entered `families` and BuildRule always ran. NeedsImport removed confirmed-local families from that list, so BuildRule was never called while ReplaceFontFamily still wrote the raw string — verified: `--heading-font "Evil'; } body { background-image: url(...) } .z { a: b"` with the same value in --local-font-families exited 0 and emitted a token that closes the theme rule, injecting UNSCOPED global CSS into a stylesheet served to every user; the identical input without the flag exits 1 with INVALID_FONT_FAMILY. The round-2 diary had recorded that the allowlist's grammar test was "the only thing keeping the allowlist in step with the validation it now bypasses", and the rework diary then concluded no grammar invariant was needed. That was inverted: the bypass survived the rework and became open to arbitrary caller input, so the invariant became MORE necessary. The allowlist version did not have this hole because its bypass set was closed and grammar-checked. Also validated: `css2?family=roboto` returns 400 (so a wrong-case import fails outright — but that is pre-existing master behaviour, only the warning wording was ours); `Uri.EscapeDataString("..")` leaves the dot segments and System.Uri collapses them to /metadata/, which the new grammar check now blocks before any request.

## 2026-07-30 00:20 – ENG-93985: --local-font-families alone was a silent no-op
Context: Asked whether the guidance said where a system font must be passed, and it did not. Every surface described --local-font-families as the thing that "applies the family through the font token", when the family is actually applied by --heading-font/--body-font and this list only suppresses the import. A literal reading produces a theme that keeps its default font.
Decision: Mirrored the existing FontWeightsWithoutFamily advisory with LocalFontFamiliesWithoutFamily, so the ignored-input case warns instead of passing silently, and reworded all five surfaces (MCP theming guide, CAADT branding skill, CLI HelpText, help/en/build-theme.txt, docs/commands/build-theme.md) to state that the family goes to the font parameters AND is additionally listed here.
Discovery: Verified from the CLI before touching anything: `build-theme --primary ... --caption t --local-font-families Verdana` with no font parameter exits 0, emits no @import, emits NO warning, and writes --crt-font-family-heading/body: 'Montserrat'. ToBuilderOptions only constructs FontsInput when hasCustomFont is true, so LocalFontFamilies is discarded before it can reach the builder — the input is dropped at the seam that decides whether fonts are configured at all, which is exactly the shape the weights advisory already existed to cover. The wording defect was uniform across all five surfaces because each was written from the implementation's point of view (suppressing the import) rather than the caller's (applying a font), so no single surface contradicted another and review never caught it.
