## 2026-07-28 13:00 – CAADT collector: review fixes (sanitizer, severity, runbook)
Context: External review of prod/values-prod.yaml + manifests-prod.yaml raised 7 findings; all 7 verified correct against upstream sources before fixing.
Decision: Fixed 6, deferred the image bump by explicit recorded decision (prod launches on the verified 0.144.0; first monthly patch cycle after go-live bumps it, spec clock starts at go-live). Sanitizer + severity fixes applied to STAGE AND PROD together so they are not another unverified prod-only delta.
Discovery: OTTL trap — keep_matching_keys KEEPS what matches, and "^$" matches the empty string, so `keep_matching_keys(resource.attributes, "^$")` kept exactly the key it was meant to strip; a sender could POST attribute key "" with ~250 KB of text (resource/scope get no truncate_all, only log.attributes do). Correct idiom is `delete_matching_keys(..., ".*")` — ".*" matches the empty key too. Bug was present on stage and passed verification only because no probe ever sent an empty key. Also: filterprocessor's upstream default error_mode is `propagate`, not `ignore` (the comment claiming otherwise invited deleting a load-bearing line); severity_text/severity_number are sender-controlled and reach SeverityText LowCardinality(String) (dictionary bloat) — clio always sends INFO/9, so pinning is free; SeverityNumber is NOT a poison pill because the exporter does uint8() which wraps rather than failing the insert; chart exposes serviceAccount.automountServiceAccountToken (default true) and this collector needs no API access.

## 2026-07-28 - PR #937 review fixes: dangling-symlink confinement Blocker + TOCTOU + Minors
Context: /creatio-code-review (Mode 2, 5 lenses) on PR #937 head 754747ea posted request-changes with one Blocker + one Major. This entry is the fix pass.
Decision (BLOCKER, dangling symlink): `OutputPathConfinement.ResolveRealPath` walk-up loop gated only on `File.Exists`/`Directory.Exists`, which FOLLOW a link and both return false for a DANGLING symlink (target absent) — so a dangling terminal/intermediate link was treated as a plain not-yet-created tail segment, never canonicalized, and the later write followed it out of the allowed zone. Fixed: stop the walk at a reparse point too (`IsReparsePoint`/`TryReadLinkTarget` via `FileSystemInfo.LinkTarget`, which reports a link even when its target is absent), and rewrote `ResolveSymlink` to read `LinkTarget` FIRST (resolving dangling links + relative targets) with bounded recursion. Because the escape is now rejected at `Resolve` time (before any write), the fix is fully contained to OutputPathConfinement.cs — no caller/command-test churn. Confirmed with real symlinks: terminal + intermediate dangling escapes rejected.
Decision (fail-closed): a CONFIRMED link whose chain cannot resolve (cycle / depth > 40) now throws a private `UnresolvableLinkException` that `Resolve` catches → rejects, instead of the old broad-catch lexical degrade (which was fail-OPEN). The lexical degrade is kept ONLY for genuine no-link-support (mock FS) where `TryReadLinkTarget` returns false without confirming a link.
Decision (MAJOR, TOCTOU): added `OutputPathConfinement.WriteAtomic` (FileMode.CreateNew) and wired it into the two schema tools that write via the System.IO.Abstractions `_ioFileSystem` with real-FS tests (get-sql-schema, get-schema) — zero test churn. CreateNew is the atomic gate: fails if the target exists (subsumes the exists-check, keeps Destructive=false honest against a race) and on POSIX O_EXCL refuses a final-component symlink. get-client-unit-schema + get-classic-page-sources write via the behavior-mock `Clio.Common._fileSystem` (30+ `_writtenContent` capture sites); their write was left on the resolve-time confinement (now hardened) to avoid a large test refactor — full write-time atomicity for those two is a noted follow-up.
Discovery: on Windows .NET, `File.Exists` returns TRUE for a dangling FILE symlink (the reparse-point node occupies the path), so Resolve refuses a dangling-inside link as "already exists"; on POSIX File.Exists follows the link → false → allowed. Outcome is platform-divergent, so the "inside" regression test asserts only the cross-OS no-escape invariant, not a single verdict. (The escape cases are caught by the confinement check on the resolved real path BEFORE the exists-check, so they're deterministic on both platforms.)

## 2026-07-29 13:10 – PR #985: Codex review round (restart readiness wait)
Context: Codex posted 3 inline findings on PR #985 against ENG-91315 code. Verified all three against source before touching anything.
Decision (P2, ServerReadinessWaiter): CONFIRMED and fixed. HealthCheckOptions inherits RemoteCommandOptions' DefaultTimeout=100_000 ms with MaxAttempts=3/RetryDelay=1, and the loop checks `deadlineUtc` only AFTER Execute returns — so an instance that accepts the connection and then stalls (the normal warm-up shape, not connection-refused) pins the wait for minutes past a small waitTimeoutSeconds. Each probe now gets TimeOut = clamp(remaining budget, 1s, 100s) and MaxAttempts=1 (the waiter loop IS the retry; the inner retry multiplied the overshoot while hiding it from the budget arithmetic). Verified via RemoteCommand.cs:171-173 that TimeOut/MaxAttempts/RetryDelay actually reach the probe — they do.
Decision (P2, credentials-path poll guidance): CONFIRMED, and stronger than Codex stated. Codex said restart-status "will not match unless registered"; it can NEVER match. ToolCommandResolver.BuildCacheKey builds identity as `options.Environment ?? settings.Uri`, restart-status requires environment-name, restart-by-credentials has none -> two structurally disjoint key spaces. The lie was NOT only in the [Description]: BuildInProgressMessage is shared by both tools and unconditionally emitted "Poll restart-status with the same environment-name (or operation-id 'X')". Made it path-aware off waitContext.EnvironmentName (already null on the credentials path); the credentials branch now points at healthcheck / restart-by-environment-name instead of a poll target that always answers not-found. Also corrected both [Description]s.
Decision (P1, "pending reported as success"): NOT fixed, deliberately. Ring's ClioWorkflowViewModel.cs:281 does set RunState from result.IsError only, but pre-ENG-91315 restart returned exit 0 immediately after the request -> Ring already showed Success while the instance warmed up. The display gap is pre-existing, not introduced. The minimal provider-side fix (a pending marker in the `note` field) is result content on a Ring-consumed tool and pulls the full ClioRing compatibility gate — not something to land inside a 14-ticket integration PR.
Discovery (the blocking check that could have flipped P1): ModelContextProtocol .NET SDK 1.4.1 `RequestOptions` exposes only Meta/ProgressToken/JsonSerializerOptions — there is NO per-request timeout, and Ring passes no client-level one either (only StdioClientTransportOptions.ShutdownTimeout=750ms and McpClientOptions.ClientInfo). So making waitReady=true the default cannot make Ring time out a restart it previously reported Success; Ring simply waits up to the ~150s deadline. Had the SDK had a sub-150s default, P1 would have been a real blocking regression rather than a display nit.
Discovery: ClioRing.Tests has 1 pre-existing macOS failure — ResolveContainedReceiptPath_...WhenRunKeyIsHostile expects `x\..\..\evil` to be traversal, but `\` is a legal filename character on POSIX. ClioRing.Tests has no ProjectReference to clio, so it cannot be affected by clio-side changes. The win-x64 NativeAOT publish step of the Ring gate is UNRUNNABLE on macOS ("Cross-OS native compilation is not supported") — no DTO/serialization path was touched, but that step is unverified locally.
Files: clio/Common/ServerReadinessWaiter.cs, clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/{RestartTool,RestartStatusTool}.cs, clio.tests/Common/ServerReadinessWaiterTests.cs, clio.tests/Command/McpServer/RestartToolTests.cs
Impact: a short --ready-timeout is now actually honored; the agent is no longer told to poll a target that structurally cannot answer. Validated: dotnet test --filter "Category=Unit" -> 19 failed / 7789 passed, failure set identical to the pre-fix trx (0 regressions); dotnet test clio-ring/ClioRing.Tests -c Release -> 151/152 (the 1 pre-existing macOS failure above).

## 2026-07-29 22:40 – PR #984 round 3 follow-up: anti-vacuity anchor on the new create-surface schema guards
Context: self-check on the two tests added for review Minor #3. `RequiredNames()` returns `[]` when the object has no `required` property, and both new tests were all-negative (`NotContain` x4) — so if the emitted column item carried no `required` array at all, they would pass over an empty set and prove nothing.
Decision: probed the real emitted schema — the column item's `required` IS empty (every parameter on `CreateEntitySchemaColumnArgs` is nullable-with-default by design). The negatives are nevertheless the correct guard: reverting `Name` to non-nullable-non-defaulted puts "name" back into `required` and makes BOTH create tests fail (verified, then restored). Added an explicit `RequiredNames(columnSchema).Should().BeEmpty()` so the empty set is a stated fact rather than an inference a reader has to make, with the reasoning recorded in the assertion comment. Also renamed `CreateEntitySchema_Should_Fail_With_ColumnCode_Message_...` to `..._ColumnIdentity_Message_...` (its Description still described the pre-unification "missing the column code" wording — the same drift Minor #5 was about) and pinned the canonical noun "missing the target column" so the three single-sourced throw sites cannot diverge again.
Discovery: an all-negative assertion set over a JSON `required` array is only non-vacuous if the array can be non-empty in the defect state — which here it can, so the guard holds. The distinction worth writing down: "passes over an empty set" is not the same as "cannot fail"; the empirical revert is what tells them apart, and a stated `BeEmpty()` removes the ambiguity for the next reader. Repo-wide grep confirmed `#954` now appears only in the doc comment and a test Description (both maintainer-facing) — no guidance resource or user-visible text carries it.

Discovery (self-inflicted, worth the warning): resolving the diary conflict with a regex line filter silently left all three of the middle (all-equals) markers in the file and they were committed in the merge commit. Root cause: the diary is uniformly CRLF, so splitting on "\n" leaves a trailing "\r" on every line; the two prefix alternatives (which were not anchored) still matched, but the middle form was written with a "$" anchor and therefore never matched a line ending in "\r". The visible tell was the script's own report - "stripped 6 marker lines" for 3 conflicts, when 9 was the only correct number. When stripping conflict markers: assert on all THREE marker forms after the edit, and count 3 per region. Resolution: the merge commit was AMENDED to drop them (49ba23cd -> 3f4cea2b) rather than patched in a follow-up, since it had not been pushed - verified afterwards that the amended commit differs from the original in that one file only (0 added / 3 removed), both merge parents survived, and a repo-wide git grep over the committed tree finds zero markers. So no marker ever existed in pushed history; the lesson above is why the amend was needed, not a description of the current tree. Second-order trap found while doing it: writing the diary back as CRLF made git report a whole-file rewrite (7260/7254) that completely hid the real 3-line delta - this repo stores the diary as LF, so always match the stored form, and read --numstat before believing a diff.

## 2026-08-04 – Branding target package: agent cannot resolve CurrentPackageId
Context: toolkit PR #65 told the branding skill to name the target package by reading CurrentPackageId with `get-sys-setting` and matching it against `list-packages`.
Discovery: that resolution cannot work. MCP `get-sys-setting` returns the All-Users default (SysSettingsCommand.TryGetSysSetting -> GetAllUsersDefaultWithType), while the binder reads the per-developer value (GetSysSettingValueByCode); the setting normally has no All-Users default at all (empty on two live envs). `get-sys-setting` is also non-resident, and `list-packages` exposes name/version/maintainer/uId — no SysPackage.Id to join the setting's value on.
Decision: the branding guide now requires an explicitly chosen package on every call (user's, the app's, or one picked from `list-packages` and confirmed) and forbids naming a raw id or guessing; the skill delegates the whole package decision instead of restating a procedure.

## 2026-07-31 00:00 – ENG-94419: post-timeout section-create verification now polls with backoff
Context: create-app-section returned exit 1 (creatio-timeout, section-created:false) for sections that actually committed. Repro was 3-for-3 in one session (2 concurrent + 1 serial, no parallelism needed): the 90s insert budget (lowered 300->90s in ENG-91540) expires while the ApplicationSection row is still committing, and the post-timeout readback fired a SINGLE immediate check that saw nothing.
Decision: replaced the single-shot verify in RecoverFromInsertTimeout with a bounded backoff poll. Generalized the existing contention settle (TryVerifySectionExistsWithSettle, 3x fixed PollDelay) into TryVerifySectionExistsPolling(attempts, backoffForAttempt); the wrapper keeps the contention path byte-identical, the timeout path uses TimeoutRecoveryVerifyAttempts=6 with a doubling backoff 2s/4s/8s capped at 8s (~30s total window, matching the documented "post-timeout recovery readback (30s)" budget). Discovery (AC#3, the open question in the ticket): the serializer wait is NOT charged to the insert budget. SectionCreateSerializationGuard.Run does gate.Wait(waitTimeout) BEFORE invoking work(), and the insert HTTP call inside TryCommitAttempt receives a FRESH insertTimeoutMs via ExecutePostRequest(url, body, insertTimeoutMs) only after the lock is acquired — two sequential independent timers. The guard wait (MaxSerializationWaitMs=120s) counts only against the end-to-end MCP response deadline (150s), which is why it is deliberately < 150s. Note: the recovery poll runs INSIDE the guard, but that path only triggers when the insert times out at ~90s, which in practice is the CLI path (uncontended) or a bare MCP call without insertTimeoutMsOverride; the concurrent MCP path passes a 600s override so it never reaches the 90s-timeout recovery.

Impact: a section that commits just after the budget expires is now recovered as success instead of a spurious failure. MCP reviewed, no update required (creatio-timeout error-class contract unchanged). Context: Codex bot left one P2 inline comment on PR #1002 — the post-timeout recovery poll (ENG-94419) makes up to 6 verify HTTP calls, each independently bounded by VerificationTimeoutMs=30s, so a stalled server could stretch recovery to 6x30s + ~30s sleeps (~210s) and, with the 90s insert, push the whole call to ~300s past the ~180s client ceiling. DI is plain AddTransient type registration, and the pre-existing optional contentionDelay param proves MS DI uses defaults for unresolved optional ctor params, so the new optional param is safe. New test injects a clock that jumps 1h/read -> poll stops after exactly 1 verify.

Decision:

No correctness reason to hold the lock during an id-matched read-only poll. Updated guard-scope + RecoverFromInsertTimeout docs (INSIDE->OUTSIDE).
- RC-4/RC-7 (weak test): verifyCalls>1 ran at zero real delay, couldn't pin count/schedule. Discovery: the budget must exceed the backoff sum or the cap silently drops attempts on the responsive path — the exact case the poll exists for. Checking the cap after-verify/before-sleep (not loop-top) both guarantees the final attempt and eliminates the wasted trailing sleep in one move.

## 2026-07-31 20:30 – PR #927 brought current: content-drift reconciliation before accepting the deletions
Context: PR #927 (externalize guidance delivery) sat 329 commits behind master and CONFLICTING. It deletes 55 of 61 guidance resource classes, so the merge had to be preceded by a producer-side reconciliation — otherwise "accept the deletion" silently discards whatever master wrote after the migration snapshot.
Decision: Three-way classify every article — snapshot baseline (merge-base 5587a46 C# literal) vs. published clio-knowledge article vs. current master C# literal — and act per bucket rather than copying in one direction. Result: 21 identical, 22 clio-only (ported), 4 knowledge-only (kept), 2 both-edited (hand-merged), 6 clio-added (published). Only then were the 27 modify/delete conflicts resolved as deletions.
Discovery: (1) The published articles are the C# raw string literal verbatim, minus the closing-delimiter indent — so base==published proves the extractor is lossless for that file, which makes the "safe to port" bucket self-verifying; a lossy parse can only over-report "both edited", never under-report. (2) Guide bodies embed JS containing `};`, so a non-greedy object-initializer regex truncates the text — scan for the raw-literal closing line instead. (3) `OracleCapture` (reflection over the built clio.dll) is the independent check on that extractor: 51 of 68 resources matched byte-for-byte, and every one of the 17 differences was an already-classified producer edit. (4) master retired `run-process-button` into `when-to-use-requests`, and clio-knowledge kept it — a fourth category the classifier did not anticipate. (5) `FreedomToMobileConversionGuidanceResource` carries `[FeatureToggle("mobile-page-converter")]`; publishing the article without `requiredFeatures` would have un-gated it.

Any future "delete an embedded catalog" PR should run the same three-way pass before trusting a modify/delete resolution. macOS baseline for this branch: 19 pre-existing master failures + 5 pre-existing branch failures (4 knowledge trust-store, 1 process-env), all path/shell specific and green in CI.

## 2026-08-02 19:30 – Built-in knowledge moves from Git checkout to signed GitHub Release asset
Context: the built-in `creatio-curated` source required a Git CLI, read a mutable
`master` at runtime, and carried no publisher signature. All three are unfixable
inside the Git transport.
Decision: added a third artifact transport, `github-release`
(`KnowledgeGitHubReleaseTransport`), alongside `git` and `nuget`, and flipped the
built-in source onto it. Discovery is `releases/latest`, revision is the release
tag (kept identical to the bundle's `libraryVersion`, which the runtime already
enforces), and the bundle runtime does signature/contract/sequence verification
unchanged. Generic Git and NuGet sources are untouched. Trust for
`com.creatio.clio` is pinned in the binary (`BuiltInKnowledgeBundleTrustStore`)
and consulted BEFORE configured material, and the composed store refuses to fall
through for that library — a settings entry cannot substitute its own key.
Producer half is `clio-knowledge` branch `feature/github-release-delivery`
(release workflow + `verify` verb + `ReleaseArtifactTests`).
Discovery: three traps worth remembering.
(1) `CuratedKnowledgeBootstrapService` had exactly one no-network fast exit, and
it was Git-shaped (`IsGitRepositoryInstalled`). Flipping the transport without an
artifact-shaped probe would have made EVERY warm MCP start call api.github.com
inside the 5s pre-serve budget, and no unit test would have failed. Added
`IsBundleGenerationInstalled` (marker existence only — no lock, no parse, no
network); `ReadCurrent` is NOT usable there because its crash-recovery path can
take the source mutation lock.
(2) `HttpMessageHandler` stubs must override the synchronous `Send`, not only
`SendAsync`: the knowledge transports call `HttpClient.Send`, and the base
`Send` throws `NotSupportedException`, which the transport catch turns into a
plain `Failed` — every case "fails correctly" for the wrong reason.
(3) The knowledge e2e suite was unrunnable on macOS: clio refuses a knowledge
root or key path with a reparse point in its ancestry, and `Path.GetTempPath()`
resolves through the `/var` symlink. Fixed in the fixtures with
`PhysicalPath.Resolve`, not by weakening the production rule.
Also: `KnowledgeSourceType.ToString()` yields `githubrelease`, which is neither
the persisted token nor what `--type` accepts — use `KnowledgeSourceTypeNames.Format`.
Files: clio/Command/McpServer/Knowledge/KnowledgeGitHubReleaseTransport.cs,
KnowledgeSourceConfiguration.cs, KnowledgeBundleContracts.cs,
CuratedKnowledgeBootstrapService.cs, KnowledgeSourceInstallationStore.cs,
KnowledgeSourceManagementService.cs, clio/Command/KnowledgeCommands.cs,
clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/KnowledgeManagementTools.cs, clio/BindingsModule.cs,
clio.tests/Command/McpServer/KnowledgeGitHubReleaseTransportTests.cs,
clio.mcp.e2e/KnowledgeGuidanceGitHubReleaseE2ETests.cs,
clio.mcp.e2e/Support/Knowledge/*, clio.mcp.e2e/Support/PhysicalPath.cs,
spec/knowledge-bundle-runtime/knowledge-bundle-runtime-github-release-delivery.md
Impact: a future transport can be added by implementing
`IKnowledgeArtifactTransport` plus a validator branch, a `ParseType` token, a DI
registration, and a bootstrap probe — but the bootstrap probe is the one that is
silent when forgotten, so check it first.

Other divergences pinned by tests: `showSuccessMessage` is web-only, mobile discards `parameters` and accepts a legacy top-level `updateCache` alias, and mobile's RefreshAll does NOT skip dynamic data sources (TODO RND-79185) so its description must not claim it.

Serving `static-files-mcp/latest/` over `python -m http.server` with `CLIO_COMPONENT_REGISTRY_CDN_BASE_URL` pointed at it proves the doc paths resolve (8975 / 9533 chars fetched) without waiting for the academy mirror. ## 2026-08-03 16:50 – ENG-93878: TC results on krestov-test (7 cases passed)
Context: Ran the ticket's runtime cases against the fixture via the Playwright+clio-session harness.
Results: TC-02 PASS (RefreshAll on a crt.Button with NO showSuccessMessage key -> "Data has been refreshed" IS shown, so the default-on contract holds). TC-03 PASS (explicit false -> silent). TC-04 PASS (excludedDataSourceNames omits IndepDS; PDS+DepDS reload). TC-05 PASS (RefreshSpecific one name -> only that source). TC-07 step 2 PASS (dependent source named ALONE reloads - the crux; old wording predicted no request at all). Discovery: The toast detector cost 4 failed iterations; each failure was a different artifact, and all produced a plausible-looking "no message" that would have been recorded as a TC-02 failure. What finally worked: snapshot body text BEFORE the click, then poll every 250ms starting IMMEDIATELY after it, and report any NEW line. Guessing the wording failed; matching /refresh/i matched the app name "Clio Refresh Test"; sampling once after a 9s settle wait always missed the ~1s toast. Lesson: for transient UI assertions use a before/after text diff with immediate polling, never a phrase guess or a late single sample.
Still not discriminable: the dependent-source DROP rule. ["PDS","DepDS"] reloads both, and so would a no-drop implementation, because a dropped dependent still reloads as a cascade of the source it depends on. SelectQuery counts cannot separate direct from cascaded. Needs model-level load counters or instrumenting refreshModelNames. The ticket's TC-07 step 3 additionally assumes the dependent depends on the INDEPENDENT list; in any real detail it depends on PDS, so that step as written tests nothing.

## 2026-07-31 12:40 – ENG-94418 create-app-section cache poisoning: harden + escalate (Scope A)
Context: Concurrent create-app-section can leave the Creatio server-side schema-manager cache holding a phantom for an abandoned half-created section. Two later symptoms: (1) page-schema-hierarchy read fails with the empty-IN() SqlException `Incorrect syntax near ')'`; (2) a later save is blocked with `Item with name … not found` (environment-wide blast radius). TRUE root cause is server-side — clio only surfaces the symptoms and drives the concurrency. Engineer approved Scope A (harden + escalate), NOT Scope B (cross-process CLI lock, declined).
Decision: (R4/S2, the ONE code change) new additive helper `PageHierarchyRecoveryHint.Append` (clio/Command/PageHierarchyRecoveryHint.cs) — pure string→string, mirrors the existing PageUpdateCommand.AppendActionableHint save-path pattern. Appends a phantom-cache recovery hint ONLY when the error carries a poisoned-cache signature (`Incorrect syntax near ')'` OR "hierarchy is empty"); leaves every other error verbatim. Wired into BOTH hierarchy-read surfacing seams that consume IPageDesignerHierarchyClient.GetParentSchemas: get-page (PageGetCommand.TryGetPage — empty-hierarchy branch + broad catch, clio/Command/PageGetOptions.cs) and update-page (PageUpdateCommand.TryGetHierarchy — read-failure catch + empty branch, clio/Command/PageUpdateOptions.cs). Hint worded as ESCALATING options with "Restart Creatio" as the GUARANTEED fallback; clear-redis-db-by-environment / sync-schemas offered as "may help" only (Q1/RISK1 — which lighter recovery actually clears the server phantom is unconfirmed until a live-stand check in verification, so do NOT assert it works). Did NOT touch AppendActionableHint (existing save-path branches unchanged by construction).
Discovery: TWO serialization layers already protect the create path (both left intact — no create/serialize behavior changed): the per-tenant MCP execution lock (BaseTool.ExecuteWithCleanLog → ExecuteUnderTenantLock over McpToolExecutionLock/TenantExecutionLockProvider) and the per-env+app SectionCreateSerializationGuard (ENG-93089). T1 targets the FORMER. RunWithProgressAndDeadlineAsync starts work on Task.Run even with server=null, and the tenant lock is taken INSIDE that work delegate — so two concurrent create-app-section calls genuinely contend on the process-global TenantExecutionLockProvider.Shared; a deterministic active-counter (max==1) is the robust regression assertion. Existing PageToolsTests `TryGetPage_WhenHierarchyReadFails_ReturnsReadableError` asserts `.Be("Failed to load page schema hierarchy")` for a GENERIC failure → stays green because the hint is scoped to the poisoned-cache signatures only (doubles as an over-fire guard). Proved T1's regression value by temporarily removing the lock in BaseTool.ExecuteUnderTenantLock → serialize test went red (max→2) → reverted.

## 2026-08-04 15:30 – ENG-94417 review round 2: the authenticated readiness gate was itself unbounded and broke token auth
Context: PR #1000 came back CHANGES_REQUESTED (1 Blocker + 5 Major, incl. a codex bot P2 on the same head). Re-read the shipped gate against the DECOMPILED creatio.client 1.0.38 instead of reasoning from its interface.
Discovery (why the first pass was wrong, from IL): `CreatioClient.Login()` (parameterless) sets no `HttpWebRequest.Timeout`, so it inherits the ~100s default and a 300s response-stream read timeout on top — the readiness call's FIRST step was the one step nothing bounded. Its `Login(int)` overload exists but `IApplicationClient` does not expose it. Worse: `Login()` posts `_userName`/`_userPassword`, which are NULL on the OAuth (`CreateOAuth20Client`) and bearer-passthrough (`new CreatioClient(uri, token, isNetCore)`) constructors — so the explicit `Login()` threw `UnauthorizedAccessException` on every poll for those environments, i.e. `restart --wait-ready` burned the full 600s and reported failure for a HEALTHY token-authenticated instance. Strictly worse than the false-ready bug being fixed, and no reviewer caught it.
Decision: DELETE the explicit `Login()`. `ExecutePostRequest` establishes the session on demand (`InitAuthCookie` → login+ping) and `ReauthExecutor` re-establishes a stale one, so login is redundant for forms auth and actively wrong for token auth — one deletion closes the Blocker's first step, the per-iteration re-login cost, and the token-auth regression. `ExecutePostRequest` DOES honor `requestTimeout` (`httpClient.Timeout = ...`), contradicting the PR body's B2 risk; but its lazy `InitAuthCookie` login+3-pings is not covered by that timeout, so the whole round-trip still runs under `Task.Run` + `Wait(probeTimeoutMs)` — the abandoned thread ends on the client's own internal timeouts.
Decision: classifier is now POSITIVE (JObject carrying `rows`/`rowsAffected`/`success`/`errorInfo`) instead of "any JSON that is not a login page" — a gateway answering `{"error":"502"}` was passing the old gate, i.e. the same false-ready class, JSON-shaped. Also added a tri-state outcome so a REFUSED credential (`UnauthorizedAccessException`) fails fast after 2 consecutive rejections instead of consuming the whole budget; 2 not 1, so a transient rejection during security-cache warm-up cannot abort a healthy wait.
Discovery (my own finding, unflagged by any reviewer): the new clio-owned healthcheck `HttpClientHandler` followed redirects by default, so a degraded stand whose ping 302s to the login page answered 200 and was reported HEALTHY — reproducing the exact false-healthy result AC2 removes (the ticket's own evidence has `/` → 302 in 25.1s). Set `AllowAutoRedirect = false` and classify 3xx unhealthy naming the `Location`.
Decision (declined): the `ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback => true` TLS bypass flagged as Major is PRE-EXISTING, untouched by any AC, and gating it means a new CLI option + docs + MCP review; kept, replied on the thread, separate hardening ticket proposed.

Impact: when an interface hides a timeout the implementation ignores, the interface is not the contract — decompile the NuGet before trusting `requestTimeout`. And an "authenticate to prove readiness" gate must never assume the client HAS credentials: clio has three auth shapes and only one of them can log in with a password. Drift guards added at both levels (unit reflection over the `waitReady` [Description], plus a live get-tool-contract e2e), because the stale parameter text that reviewers caught is exactly what nothing pinned.

## 2026-08-04 18:30 – ENG-93365 non-JSON DataService responses surface as typed errors
Context: `find-entity-schema schema-name=Contact` on a live stand leaked the raw parser text `'<' is an invalid start of a value` to the MCP agent, because the shared SelectQuery helper deserialized the body without guarding for HTML/empty/truncated content.
Decision: Added `Clio.Package.ServiceResponseJsonGuard` (try-deserialize → classify → typed message with URL, parser detail, bounded+redacted preview; HTML body deliberately NOT previewed) and routed `SelectQueryHelper.ExecuteSelectQuery` (~15 call sites incl. find-entity-schema) and `ApplicationInfoService.Deserialize` through it. Classification happens AFTER a failed parse rather than by sniffing the first byte: a truncated body starting with `{` is equally unparseable and must produce the same typed error. Left `PageSchemaMetadataHelper.ExecuteSelectQuery` alone (deliberately fail-soft) and kept `SchemaTemplateCatalog` as the reference shape.
Discovery: Three traps, each of which alone would have shipped a fix that does nothing or breaks something.
  1. The MCP boundary (`McpToolErrorFilter.GetInnermostMessage`, and the same helper in `ClioRunTool`) unwraps to the INNER-MOST exception — so a curated message with the parser failure kept as inner exception is replaced by the very raw text it was written to hide. Fixed with the marker interface `Clio.Common.IAuthoritativeErrorMessage`, which stops the unwrap at itself; the walk itself was extracted into `Clio.Common.SurfacedExceptionMessage.Resolve` so the filter and the `clio-run` dispatcher (Ring's entry point) cannot drift apart — two hand-copied loops would have let one silently revert while the other's test stayed green. The same latent defect was already hiding `RemoteEntitySchemaDesignerClient`'s package-dependency recovery guidance — that path now throws the marked type too.
  2. `BindingsModule.RegisterAssemblyInterfaceTypes` auto-registers every class implementing a `Clio.I*` interface, so an EXCEPTION carrying a marker interface got DI-registered, its `string message` ctor could not be resolved, ValidateOnBuild failed and `clio mcp-server` refused to start (exit 1, zero output). Added a blanket `typeof(Exception).IsAssignableFrom(type)` skip — an exception is never a service.
  3. `LookupDefaultDisplayValueResolver` distinguishes "server rejected the request" (`InvalidOperationException` → not-found marker) from "malformed response" (`JsonException` → GUID-only, no marker). Collapsing both into `InvalidOperationException` made a non-JSON body assert `not-found-or-no-access`, a claim the response never made — caught by its existing unit test. `NonJsonServiceResponseException` derives from `InvalidOperationException` (existing catch clauses keep working) and the resolver now catches it first.
  Also: at the MCP boundary `SensitiveErrorTextRedactor` rewrites the URL to `[redacted-uri]` (and eats the trailing `)`), same as the `list-page-templates` reference; the CLI keeps the full URL.

Impact: Reproduce a non-JSON response without a broken stand — the e2e stub now serves HTML for a SelectQuery keyed on the queried schema name (`HtmlSelectQuerySchemaName`), so runtime detection (which probes SysAdminUnit) still succeeds and environment registration is unaffected. Runtime-verified with a local HTTP stand-in: before the fix the CLI printed the ticket's parser message verbatim, after it prints the typed error; the e2e proves the same on the real mcp-server process.

## 2026-08-05 12:10 – build-theme: off the shared MCP lock instead of hoisting the probe
Context: PR 993 review — BuildThemeCommand exposed TryResolveFontAvailability plus a required probedFontAvailability parameter purely so the MCP tool could probe before ExecuteWithCleanLog; MCP lock semantics had leaked into the command's public API and its XML docs, including the CLI-facing overloads.
Decision: build-theme carries no tenant and acquires no session container, so it stops taking McpToolExecutionLock.SharedFallbackKey. New BaseTool.ExecuteWithCleanLogUnderToolLock (named after its ExecuteUnderTenantLock sibling) derives its lock key from the concrete tool type, so no tool carries a magic key constant; the clean-log scope was extracted into a private WithCleanLog shared by all three entry points. The command is back to one self-probing build path — TryResolveFontAvailability, probedFontAvailability, the ArgumentNullException guard and the lock remarks are gone.
Trap: TenantExecutionLockProvider.GetLock PINS the mapping (InUseCount++) and its contract requires a balancing MarkAvailable — the first cut of the per-tool lock omitted it and would have made that mapping permanently un-evictable, holding one of the provider's capacity slots forever. MobilePageConversionGuideTool has the same unbalanced GetLock on the shared key (pre-existing, not touched here).
Discovery: the lock is still needed, but only against build-theme itself — the injected command's IWorkspacePathBuilder.RootPath is shared by every call. Also, moving the probe back inside the build means a request rejected by the workspace/package checks now sends nothing outbound, so AC-7's accepted "fails late, probes first" caveat disappears. ResolveVersion still does a blocking HTTP round trip under the tool's lock; that was true before and is unchanged.

## 2026-08-03 – ENG-94402 follow-up: chunk the batched layer enumeration (uncapped fan-out consequence)

## 2026-08-05 – set-feature / set-syssetting: one contract, and two deliberate trades
Context: consolidating the feature-state write made three sub-paths of set-feature disagree — the per-role one raised an error on a rejected Save while the default-state one and the unknown-role one answered exit 0.
Decision: both FeatureCommand paths answer bool, Execute writes one error line and returns `applied ? 0 : 1`; SysSettingsCommand.Execute returns `UpdateSysSetting(opts) ? 0 : 1`. Exit codes documented in help/en and docs/commands for set-feature, set-syssetting and apply-manifest.
Decision (do not flip back): Execute clears the feature cache unconditionally, so a successful per-role write clears it twice — the service clears after its own write. A duplicate idempotent GET is the lesser evil against losing the invalidation when the row already holds the requested state, which is what scoping the call to the write branches caused.
Decision (do not flip back): the refused-update line stays a WriteError inside SysSettingsCommand.UpdateSysSetting and the command adds no second verdict line. Moving it to WriteWarning to separate "detail" from "verdict" read cleaner but silently downgraded the Program.cs Maintainer flow and split one sentence across two channels.
Discovery: chasing cross-command consistency is what produced most of the review rounds here. Every change to adjacent released code — a message channel, a cache call site, a method's virtuality — cost another round. Change the command the task owns; leave the neighbours unless a defect forces it.

The original "no restart" reading came from *the service answered afterwards*, which is equally consistent with a restart that already finished — it was never log-verified. The restart also OUTLIVES the install call: net472 logged its restart at 16:44:57,419, the install returned at 16:44:57,842, Application_Start followed at 16:44:58,735. So an immediate outcome probe lands inside the restart; the command reuses IServerReadinessWaiter (whose InitialDelay exists precisely because "the previous app domain may still answer briefly after a restart request") between installing and judging. Context: Pre-PR review gate (3 parallel reviewers over the full diff), then the fix the correctness lens' High finding actually needed. Branch feature/ENG-94385-bundle-process-builder-package; package side on ProcessBuilder feature/ENG-94385-rename-crt-process-builder (58dc0ea).
Decision (review fixes): MCP tool now runs under McpProgressHeartbeat.RunWithProgressAndDeadlineAsync — it previously held the per-tenant lock through a up-to-600s readiness wait with no heartbeat, the exact pattern RestartTool.cs:141-165 documents as forbidden. Kept the work UNDER the lock unlike RestartTool, and said why: its phase 2 is a read-only poll after its write returned, here the long part IS the write. Destructive false -> true (compile-creatio and restart-by-environment-name are both true and this tool causes the effects of both; install-gate's false is not the precedent — it ships a prebuilt assembly and never makes the target rebuild). Added a SHA-256 pin on the committed .gz plus a check that the shipped sources carry the CanManageProcessDesign gate on the handlers. Corrected help/docs/curated-contract, which stated the wrong authorization model ("gated on CanManageSolution" — it is CanManageProcessDesign + General user, verified by extracting the archive; adr-ENG-90883 §82 says CanManageSolution is deliberately NOT used).
Discovery (THE one worth remembering — two separate DB limitations, not one):
  1. A failed configuration build is invisible from the database. The platform records the descriptor version when it ACCEPTS an archive and keeps serving the assembly it last built successfully, so both sides of any DB-only comparison come from the descriptor.
  2. The recorded version is INERT, not merely lagging: Creatio does not update it when re-installing a package it already has (matched by UId), so it stays at whatever the FIRST install wrote. Verified on both runtimes on 2026-08-05: after installing the 1.1.0.0 archive, ProcessDesignService.GetVersion reported 1.1.0.0 while `clio list-packages` still reported 1.0.0.0 on studioenu-15832585 (net472) AND studionet8enu-15832863 (web02:8530).
  Consequences, all observed before being understood: bumping BundledPackages.ProcessBuilderVersion to 1.1.0.0 made the installer reinstall on EVERY invocation (the re-run took the full 76s install path instead of short-circuiting), and would have made the five [RequiresPackage] gates refuse forever on any environment that already had the package. So the [RequiresPackage] floor is effectively FROZEN — it can only move when the UId changes, i.e. for a genuinely different package — and the two questions need two constants: ProcessBuilderVersion (is it installed at all; read from the DB) vs ProcessBuilderBuildVersion (did the target compile what we ship; read from the service).
Decision (GetVersion): package-side ProcessDesignConstants.PackageVersion compiled into the assembly + an UNGATED GetVersion operation returning it, and clio's post-install check compares the SERVING version against ProcessBuilderBuildVersion. Ungated on purpose: installing a package and designing processes are different rights, ListUserTasks goes through the guard, and the guard's rejection comes back as an unsuccessful envelope — i.e. an administrator who may deploy but lacks CanManageProcessDesign would fail the post-install check in the most misleading way available. GetVersion also replaced the SKIP decision (was IRequiredPackageChecker.IsCompatible, now the service's own report), which removed IRequiredPackageChecker from the command entirely and made the "present but never compiled" state self-healing: it no longer satisfies the short-circuit, so an ordinary re-run reinstalls it with no flag.
Discovery (rejected alternative, do not re-propose): GlobalContext.FailOnError is NOT a way to make a failed configuration build fail the install. CheckLogsOnSuccessMessage => GlobalContext.FailOnError (BasePackageInstaller.cs:85) switches success to `completeInstallLog.Contains("application installed successfully")`, and the 16:44 live install never emitted that phrase — only the 12:54/12:58 Hub installs did. Setting it would report failure on a successful install. It is also a process-global static, and the MCP server is long-lived.
Discovery (bundling): clioignore does NOT filter Files/Bin — `**/CrtProcessBuilder/Files/Bin/**` was tried and the built DLL still landed in the archive (342610 bytes). Delete the directory before `clio compress`, as cliogate's build.ps1 does. And do NOT exclude ErrorOr.dll / ATF.Repository.dll by file name: Files/Libs carries them, the package depends on them, the platform core does not, and doing so halved the archive to 94007 bytes — shipping source that cannot compile. Correct archive: 189144 bytes, exactly 2 dlls both under Files/Libs. Recorded in the package repo as docs/bundling-into-clio.md; the hop into clio had been an unrecorded manual step.
Discovery (process): a stale `testhost` silently holds clio.dll, the copy fails, and the suite then runs against the PREVIOUS build — reporting failures whose cause is not in the code. Twice today. `Get-Process testhost | Stop-Process -Force` before a rerun, and treat an implausible test COUNT (192 instead of 7158) as the tell that the run is not what it claims.

Impact: `clio list-packages` is NOT a way to verify what is serving — documented on both surfaces with the GetVersion call-service command instead. Live-verified end to end: upgrade 1.0.0.0 -> 1.1.0.0 on net472 (87s) and .NET 8 (73s), both exit 0 with GetVersion reporting 1.1.0.0; then a re-run on both short-circuited with "already installed and serving". Context: Closing out ENG-94385 before the PR. RETRACTION (read this before trusting the 20:20 entry): "The recorded version is INERT — Creatio does not update it when re-installing a package it already has" is FALSE. The row IS rewritten, whenever the descriptor's ModifiedOnUtc moves. PackageStorageComposer.ApplySourcePackageChanges compares ModifiedOnUtc (and the repo revision) and sets IsPackageDescriptorChanged; without that flag PackageDBStorage.SavePackageDescriptor returns early at its GetIsPackageDescriptorModified guard and never reaches the SysPackage.Version assignment. PackageVersion is NOT part of that comparison. So: the DATE decides WHETHER the row is rewritten, the VERSION decides WHAT lands in it. Proven live on both stands 2026-08-05 in both directions (1.1.0.0 -> 1.1.0.1 once the date moved; stuck when only the version moved).
Root cause of the wrong conclusion, worth more than the conclusion: the test install read the archive from the BUILD OUTPUT directory (IWorkingDirectoriesProvider.ExecutingDirectory) while clio compress -d had written to the repo path. So every "the version did not move" observation was made against the PREVIOUS archive. ALWAYS rebuild clio between repacking and verifying — this invalidated an entire experiment and put a wrong claim into the codebase and this diary before it was caught.
Consequences of the retraction, all reverted: the ProcessDesignService.GetVersion operation (package side) and the two-constant split (ProcessBuilderVersion vs ProcessBuilderBuildVersion) are GONE. Do not re-propose a per-package version endpoint: it does not scale (every bundled package re-implements it), and a second bundled package was already inbound. One constant, which IS the [RequiresPackage] floor, plus a mandatory paired ModifiedOnUtc bump via clio set-pkg-version (it writes both fields, so only a hand edit can separate them). Also found and fixed at the root while establishing this: PackageDescriptor.ClearMilliseconds dropped DateTime.Kind, so a DateTime.UtcNow value serialized as if local — a 3-hour shift in every descriptor clio writes from a UTC source.
Discovery (review gate, the reason to re-run it rather than trust the earlier pass): 6 commits had landed since the previous gate, so its verdict no longer covered the diff. The correctness lens found 3 High, ALL in the MCP wrapper and all reachable in the real path (clio-run resolves the tool from the registry and calls tool.InvokeAsync in-process, so the heartbeat+lock path is what actually runs):
  1. CommandExecutionResult.FromInfo IS exit 0, and its documented contract is "accepted and still running, with poll-for-status guidance". Here the deadline race covered the whole operation — archive check, upload, install, a 600 s readiness wait, the probe — so nothing was accepted yet. Worse, the command reports failure by RETURNING a code rather than throwing, so McpProgressHeartbeat.ObserveInBackground (OnlyOnFaulted) never saw it: a post-deadline failure was completely silent.
  2. The detached work held the broad per-tenant monitor (BaseTool.InternalExecute wraps command.Execute in lock(GetLock)) for its whole duration, i.e. long after the caller was answered — so every unrelated same-tenant tool, read-only included, stalled behind work nobody awaits. CompileCreatioTool.cs:174 names this a review Blocker (ENG-91315) and takes no GetLock. ## 2026-08-06 17:05 – Dropped the served version: outcome check is now liveness-only (Ping)
Context: ENG-94385 — the install command verified its outcome by asking the package which VERSION was serving, which forced a hand-maintained copy of the version inside the shipped C# sources. Spent the session establishing, by measurement on ts1-web01-15837616, whether any other carrier exists. None does; the duplicate was then dropped along with the version check.
Decision: `ProcessDesignService.GetApiVersion` → `Ping` returning only `success`; `ProcessDesignConstants.PackageVersion` and the csproj `<Version>` deleted; `IsPackageOperational(packageName, out diagnosis)` (no expectedVersion); `KnownRoute.ProcessBuilderPing` → `/rest/ProcessDesignService/Ping`. The version now lives ONLY in `descriptor.json` and reaches clio through `SysPackage` + the `[RequiresPackage]` floors. Accepted limit, disclosed in tool description / help / docs / ADR / test-plan risk table: on a failed UPGRADE the stale assembly still answers and passes.
Discovery (all measured on the stand, each was a hypothesis first):
- The package DOES get its own assembly on the target (`probeAssembly = CrtProcessBuilder`), so "our code lands in Terrasoft.Configuration" is FALSE.
- The platform overrides `$(Version)`, not the attribute: a literal `<AssemblyVersion>` set in the shipped `Files/Directory.Build.targets` survives (1.1.0.1) while `$(Version)`-derived does not (10.1.453.0). So `<Version>` in a package csproj is decorative.
- `descriptor.json` is NOT on the target's disk at build time (two independent path forms both 0), and `$(PkgPath)` is EMPTY there — meaning the `Condition="'$(PkgPath)' != ''"` ItemGroup in our own Directory.Build.targets is inert on the target. Build-time generation from the descriptor is therefore impossible.
- `<GenerateAssemblyInfo>false</GenerateAssemblyInfo>` does not break compilation — it breaks SERVICE DISCOVERY, because MSBuild materializes the csproj's `<AssemblyAttribute Include="…PackageReferenceAssemblyAttribute">` only via `GetAssemblyAttributes`, which that switch disables. Install logged `Configuration build finished` with no errors and left the route absent; the verifier caught it (exit 1) — the silent-failure case it exists for, observed live.
- cliogate's identical csproj switch + `[assembly: AssemblyVersion("1.1.1.2")]` is safe ONLY because cliogate ships a PREBUILT dll — the target copies it and never recompiles. Parity with cliogate is unavailable to a source-only package, not merely superficial.
- Corrected a wrong claim in `BundledPackages.cs`: `cliogate/version.txt` (1.1.1.2) is the ASSEMBLY version and `CheckApiVersion` compares it against `rest/CreatioApiGateway/GetApiVersion`, which also returns the assembly version — the nudge is consistent and works. Do not "fix" it to the package version 2.0.0.44.
- Pre-existing defect found and NOT yet fixed: `clio set-pkg-version <path>` with no `-v` writes `"PackageVersion": null`, still moves `ModifiedOnUtc`, and returns 0. Reproduced on a throwaway copy.

## 2026-08-06 17:55 – Re-measured the ModifiedOnUtc rule; SysPackage.Version is NOT monotonic
Context: After removing the version from the service response, `SysPackage.Version` became the only path by which a version reaches clio — so the "ModifiedOnUtc decides whether the row is rewritten" rule became load-bearing. Re-ran it on ts1-web01-15837616 (net472). Note it had ALREADY been verified on 2026-08-05 on two stands and recorded in docs/agent-instructions/bundled-packages.md; this run corroborates it and adds one property.
Decision: Recorded the new property in bundled-packages.md section 2 rather than anywhere new.
Discovery:
- Positive path: `clio set-pkg-version -v 1.1.0.2` (writes both fields) -> install -> `list-packages` shows 1.1.0.2. Confirmed.
- Negative control: hand-edited the descriptor to 1.1.0.3 leaving ModifiedOnUtc untouched -> install returned exit 0 and "Done" -> recorded version STAYED 1.1.0.2. So the failure is completely silent from the install's point of view.
- NEW: the comparison is "differs", not "is later". Restoring the committed descriptor (1.1.0.1, with a timestamp EARLIER than the recorded one) rewrote the row DOWNWARD, 1.1.0.2 -> 1.1.0.1. `SysPackage.Version` is therefore not monotonic and is not "the highest version ever installed" — it is whatever the last descriptor with a different timestamp said. Any future "has this been upgraded" check must not assume forward-only movement.
- Incidental but useful: `clio compress` is deterministic given identical inputs — after the experiment, restoring descriptor.json from git and repacking reproduced the pinned SHA D234B196… byte for byte, so an experiment on the descriptor needs no pin churn to undo.
Files: docs/agent-instructions/bundled-packages.md
Impact: Removes the temptation to treat the recorded version as a monotonic upgrade marker, and documents that a descriptor experiment is fully reversible without touching the SHA pin.

## 2026-08-07 09:57 – MCP Git bootstrap stream drain is bounded across Windows and Linux
Context: Issue #1018 reproduced an MCP startup hang after the immediate Git process exited while a descendant retained redirected stdout or stderr handles beyond the five-second curated-knowledge budget.
Decision: Apply one linked operation token to stdin, process waiting, both stream readers, and resource monitoring; close Clio's redirected endpoints on cancellation; preserve partial output plus CR/LF/CRLF real-time boundaries; and expose `DescendantTerminationUncertain` instead of adding Windows Job Objects or Unix process-group ownership.
Discovery: A bootstrap E2E that fails before Git is a false positive. The deterministic `clio.process.fixture` must be first on the MCP child's `PATH`, record its invocation and descendant PID, exit its Git parent, and keep inherited pipes open for thirty seconds. The real server then warns and initializes in about six seconds. Linux uses the same pipe semantics and passes the identical four-case integration fixture in Docker. Broad desktop unit execution can invoke the production wiki help viewer, so final local validation stayed on safe targeted filters after that earlier browser leak.

## 2026-08-07 10:19 – Final review hardened post-exit resource enforcement
Context: The comprehensive pre-PR review found that an uncancellable final directory scan could exceed the operation deadline and that directory monitoring stopped when the immediate parent exited, before inherited-pipe draining completed.
Decision: Preserve the first cancellation cause atomically, keep the directory monitor active until redirected readers settle, make recursive traversal lazy and cancellation-aware, flush pending real-time fragments in a finally block, and verify recorded descendant identity before test cleanup kills a PID.
Discovery: Bounding stream reads alone is insufficient when a descendant can keep mutating the checkout after its parent exits. The monitor and the final filesystem scan are both part of the same operation deadline, and every uncertain failure diagnostic must disclose the portable cleanup limitation.

## 2026-08-04 13:05 – Make the branch measurable: global clio must BE the branch build (ENG-88474)
Context: Two behavioural runs looked like they measured this branch and did not. Both spawned `clio` from PATH, so they got released 8.1.0.96. One run said so outright — "No workplaces guide in this build" — and therefore concluded from RELEASED guidance that a workplace is UI-only, recommending browser automation for exactly the case this branch adds an odata recipe for. Patching the plugin `.mcp.json` to a snapshot path does not help: agents launch `clio mcp-server`, not the config's path.
Decision: Install the branch as the global tool (`dotnet pack -p:Version=8.1.0.98-eng88474` + `dotnet tool update -g clio --configfile <standalone config>`) and restore both plugin `.mcp.json` files to the canonical `"command": "clio"` form, which the toolkit's own `test_mcp_config_runs_global_clio_mcp_server` pins.
Discovery: Three traps, all silent. (1) `--add-source` is rejected outright when the user's NuGet config uses package source mapping; the way through is `--configfile` with a standalone config, which replaces rather than merges the machine/user configs. (2) That config must have NO BOM — NuGet reports a BOM as "NuGet.Config is not valid XML", naming the path and nothing else. (3) clio is multi-TFM (net8.0 + net10.0) and the tool shim runs net10.0, so building only `-f net8.0` produces a package whose net8.0 payload carries the change and whose net10.0 payload is stale from an older commit — the install "succeeds", `clio --version` prints the OLD assembly version, and every guidance probe comes back False. Always `dotnet build -c Release` for all TFMs, then verify the packed payload per TFM before installing (byte-search the UTF-16LE string inside each `tools/<tfm>/any/clio.dll` in the nupkg). Also note `clio --version` prints AssemblyVersion (8.1.0.95), NOT the tool package version (8.1.0.98-eng88474) — a version mismatch there is expected and is not evidence of a stale install.

Impact: Behavioural measurement of MCP guidance is only valid if the GLOBAL clio is the build under test. Verify the claim before trusting a run — ask the MCP server for a guide that exists only on the branch. Roll back with `dotnet tool update -g clio --version 8.1.0.96`.

## 2026-08-04 17:35 – Publish navigation changes without a re-login (ENG-88474)
Context: The guide could only tell users to log out and back in after a workplace change, which the ticket wanted removed. Creatio Compass surfaced the mechanism: the `Workplace` package caches workplace/section/edit-page lists PER SESSION (`WorkplaceRepository`, `SectionCacheManager`, `PageEntityRepository`), and its invalidation contract is `IWorkplaceManager.ReloadWorkplaces()`, reached from an entity event listener on `SysUserInRole` / `SysAdminUnitInWorkplace` insert+delete ONLY.
Decision: Add a cliogate endpoint that calls that contract directly, plus `clio reload-workplaces` (aliases `reload-navigation`, `rlwp`), an MCP tool, and a guide rule to run it as the LAST step of any navigation change. Rejected relying on the platform listener alone: it fires for a role grant but not for a workplace create, a section move, or a `HomePageUId` change, and the binding tools write through `Terrasoft.Core.DB`, which raises no entity events at all.
Discovery: `IWorkplaceManager` lives in the `Workplace` package's `WorkplaceApi` assembly, which cliogate must not reference (SDK-only), so it is resolved reflectively — verified working on a live .NET Framework stand. Two traps found by live failure, both now handled: (1) `ClassFactory.Get<T>()` is declared with a `params` array, so a "zero parameters" filter finds nothing and the call silently reports "no overload"; accept the params shape and pass an empty array of its element type. (2) `install-gate` ships the `cliogate.gz` EMBEDDED IN THE CLIO BUILD OUTPUT, so regenerating the package after building clio installs the OLD gate and the new endpoint answers "Endpoint not found" — this is exactly why `build.ps1` rebuilds clio at the end. Always: build cliogate -> compress -> rebuild clio -> install-gate. Also: adding an MCP tool requires a `PassthroughToolClassificationRegistry` row or the discovery-drift guard fails the FULL unit suite, and a new command needs all four doc artifacts (`Commands.md` index link, `help/en/<verb>.txt`, `docs/commands/<verb>.md`, `WikiAnchors.txt`) or `Command_ShouldHave_DescriptionBlock_InReadmeFile` fails. `WikiAnchors.txt` is NOT strictly sorted, so do not insert by naive comparison.

## 2026-08-10 – ENG-94385: where a "forbid this input" rule may live, and the two places it may not
Context: Review found the bundled package's version could carry a pre-release suffix, which two version rules ordered in opposite directions. Forbidding the suffix was the agreed fix. Placing that refusal took three attempts, and BOTH wrong placements passed their own tests and a full review round — recording them because the reasoning generalises well beyond this package.
Decision: Three parts, one rule. `IBundledPackageCatalog.TryGetVersion` READS and never judges. `InstallProcessBuilderCommand.ShouldRefuseInstall` REFUSES (loudly, `--force` overrides, CLI-only). `BundledPackageConvergence` ABSTAINS — warns "cannot compare" and allows.
Discovery 1 — a reader must not refuse, because its `false` is already spoken for. Enforcing the rule in the catalog looked right and was the worst option: a refusal returns `false`, which already meant "I could not read it", and BOTH consumers answer that with "proceed with a warning" — correct for a truncated archive, catastrophic for a malformed VERSION. It switched off the downgrade guard, so a distribution stamped `1.0.1.0-rc` installed over an environment recording `9.9.9.9` silently. A commit that ADDED a guard thereby removed it. Generalisation: before returning a new failure through an existing sentinel, check what every caller's default for that sentinel already is.
Discovery 2 — the enforcing consumer must not be the one that gates everything else. With the refusal moved to the install command, convergence still compared the suffixed version using `PackageVersion`'s operator, whose `CompareSuffix` ranks an EMPTY suffix BELOW a non-empty one. So bundled `1.0.1.0-rc` made an environment recording the GA `1.0.1.0` — and every lower version — read as BEHIND. Convergence refused every gated call and named the install as the remedy; the install refused the same distribution; `--force` is absent over MCP. The entire process-designer surface dead with no in-band exit, over a defect in clio. That is the SAME trap the ticket opened by fixing, relocated. Generalisation: a rule that gates a whole surface can only ever abstain on a malformed input; only a rule whose refusal costs one command can refuse.
Discovery 3 — a doc comment carried the reasoning from its previous location and became false without any code changing. The branch comment argued from `1.0.1.0-rc` over `9.9.9.9`, which is caught by the numeric comparison alone (9 > 1); the case that needs the branch is EQUAL numbers. Four other places still credited the catalog with a refusal reverted one commit earlier. This was the recurring defect class of the whole PR: every review round found comments, `because` strings and `[Description]`s asserting mechanisms that had moved.
Discovery 4 — two sanitiser lessons. Filtering forbidden characters out of untrusted text is worse than rejecting it: `rc\r\nIGNORE PRIOR INSTRUCTIONS…` came back as `rcIGNOREPRIORINSTRUCTIONS…`, words intact and now shaped like real data. And `char.IsLetterOrDigit` is Unicode-wide, not `[A-Za-z0-9]` — a Cyrillic homoglyph rendered indistinguishably from `-rc`. Reject, do not repair; and write the character class out rather than naming a predicate that means something wider.
Discovery 5 — a text scan over an archive cannot bind a gate to the operation it protects, and should not pretend to. A proximity-window test was written, then deleted: the property was already asserted properly in the package repo by four tests that make `IProcessDesignGuard` deny and require the operation to fail. clio keeps only what a byte scan can honestly claim — and its call-site count had to learn to ignore commented-out calls, because `// _guard.Ensure…` three times kept the count at 3 with zero live gates.
Files: clio/Common/BundledPackageCatalog.cs, clio/Common/BundledPackageConvergence.cs, clio/Common/TextUtilities.cs, clio/Command/InstallProcessBuilderCommand.cs, clio/Command/InfoCommand.cs, clio.tests/Common/{BundledPackageCatalogTests,BundledPackageConvergenceTests,BundledProcessBuilderPackageTests,TextUtilitiesTests}.cs, clio.tests/Command/InstallProcessBuilderCommandTests.cs, rebundle-process-builder.ps1, docs/agent-instructions/bundled-packages.md
Impact: Whenever a rule says "this input is forbidden", ask three questions before choosing where it lives — what does the existing failure channel already mean to every caller, how much does a refusal cost at this layer, and which layer can afford to abstain. And when moving a rule, grep for the reasoning: the code moves in one edit, its justification does not.

## 2026-08-11 – ENG-94529: list-environments answered from a process-start snapshot; where the re-read belongs
Context: An agent inside an MCP session appended an environment to `appsettings.json` with Bash, then spent ~30 turns in a loop: `clio ping -e <name>` from the shell succeeded (separate process, fresh read) while every MCP call reported "not found" and `list-environments` returned the byte-identical pre-edit list. Re-pointing an existing environment to a new URL made MCP keep calling the OLD (dead) URL — proof the whole environment object, not just the key, was frozen at process start.
Decision: `ISettingsRepository.Reload()` — an EXPLICIT re-read, called from exactly two places (the `list-environments` tool and `ToolCommandResolver.ResolveSettingsAndKey`), never as a side effect of an ordinary settings read. Reads stay on the in-memory snapshot: making every getter reload would put the cross-process settings lock plus a full deserialize on every settings read of every command.
Discovery 1 — extending the re-read to environment RESOLUTION cost no extra disk read. `ResolveSettingsAndKey` already called `settingsBootstrapService.GetReport()` → `GetResult()` → full file read under the settings lock on every resolve; only the following `IsEnvironmentExists`/`FindEnvironment` looked at the stale snapshot. `Reload()` returns that same report, so the resolver consumes one read instead of two. This is what turned the choice "fix the list vs. document the divergence" into "fix both".
Discovery 2 — the staleness is localised to the ROOT singleton. Per-environment child containers (`new BindingsModule().Register(settings)`) construct their own `SettingsRepository`, so anything resolved inside them already reads the file at build time. Only the startup singleton — used by `ToolCommandResolver` and by the startup-injected commands behind `BaseTool.InternalExecute(options)` (the non-generic overload) — is frozen. Hence the error text still names the loaded copy: the fix cannot honestly claim "always fresh".
Discovery 3 — a reload must repeat the constructor's post-load normalization (`EnsureSettingsCollections` + `AttachDbServers`), or a hand-edited file leaves `Features` null and silently drops the `OrdinalIgnoreCase` rebuild, making feature keys case-sensitive. `TrySaveSchema` must NOT be repeated — that is a write on a read path.
Discovery 4 — `SettingsBootstrapService.GetResult()` never caches and never throws on a corrupt file: it returns `Report.Status == "broken"` with an EMPTY `Settings`. So the degrade rule is one condition — on "broken" do not assign `_settings` at all, keep the previous state, return the reason as a warning.
Discovery 5 — the audience of the "not found" message cannot be decided per call site: the same command classes serve CLI and MCP. It is a property of the process, so `EnvironmentNotFoundError.Build` defaults to the ambient `Program.IsMcpServerMode` (the marker `ConsoleLogger` already branches on) with an explicit `isMcpContext` parameter so tests pin either text deterministically. MCP text routes to `clio-run reg-web-app` (the only path that moves the file and the running process together); CLI text keeps the shell command.

Impact: `list-environments` now returns `{environments, settingsFilePath, warnings}` (Ring's `CollectEnvNames` already tolerates an object with `environments`; the e2e parser was extended). When a long-lived host answers a question about its own configuration, ask where the answer is read from — and if a message tells the caller how to fix something, check that the advice works from the surface the caller is on.

## 2026-08-11 – ENG-94529 follow-up: two defects the first pass left in place
Context: Review of the first ENG-94529 commit found two problems, both confirmed by running the code rather than by reading it.
Discovery 1 — the re-read wrote to the file it was reading. `SettingsBootstrapService.GetResult()` applies repairs when constructed with `applyRepairs: true`: it rewrites `appsettings.json` when a migration is pending, and CREATES it with defaults when it is missing. `Reload()` is called by a `ReadOnly = true` MCP tool and by every environment resolution, so a read path could write. Fix: `ISettingsBootstrapService.GetResultWithoutRepairs()`, threading the flag through `Load`/`LoadUnlocked` instead of reading the field; `Reload()` uses only that overload. Test: a file with a pending migration must come back byte-identical after `Reload()`.
Discovery 2 — the settings reload alone did NOT fix a re-pointed environment, because the container cache undid it. `BuildCacheKey` used `options.Environment ?? settings.Uri` as the identity: with a name supplied, the uri never entered the key, so an environment re-pointed to a new uri kept its cached container and its `IApplicationClient` bound to the OLD uri. Proven live: re-pointing to `nonexistent-host-xyz.invalid` still produced `Connection refused` (the old socket) before the fix and `nodename nor servname provided` (DNS lookup of the new host) after. Fix: the identity is `name|uri`. This only refines the key — identical settings still share one authenticated session.
Discovery 3 — a live probe needs a discriminating target. Two refused ports produce the same message ("Connection refused", with the address dropped on some paths), so the first attempt could not tell a stale client from a fresh one. Pointing the second target at an unresolvable HOST made the two cases produce different error classes.

Impact: When adding a re-read to a long-lived host, check BOTH directions — that the read does not write, and that no cache downstream of the read is keyed on something coarser than what was re-read.

## 2026-08-11 – ENG-94529: a red PR check that was a runner, not a change
Context: The "TeamCity MCP e2e" check on PR #1026 failed with `404 Not Found` from nginx while POSTing to `/app/rest/buildQueue?moveToTop=true`. Four failures over two days, all on branches unrelated to each other.
Discovery 1 — the discriminator was the RUNNER, and it was in the logs all along. Every failure ran on `K-KRYLOV-NB`, every success on `TS1-MRKT-WEB01` (`gh run view <id> --log | grep "Runner name"`). `teamcity-mcp-e2e.yml` uses `runs-on: self-hosted`, which matches every runner in the Default group, so the job lands on a random one.
Discovery 2 — the nginx 404 is a DNS story, and `dig` proves it in one line. `dig +short teamcity-rnd.bpmonline.com @1.1.1.1` returns a CNAME chain to `bpmonline.com` (52.31.26.85); internally the same name is `10.48.14.99`. A runner without corporate DNS therefore reaches the PUBLIC Creatio web tier, whose nginx has no `/app/rest/...` route. That is the 404 — not a TeamCity permission problem (that would be 401/403 with a `TeamCity-Node-Id` header) and not a wrong build-type id (TeamCity answers those itself).
Discovery 3 — the same defect was leaking the CI token. The old step attached `Authorization: Bearer $TEAMCITY_TOKEN` to a request aimed at whatever the name resolved to, so on the out-of-network runner the corporate TeamCity token was posted to a public web front end. The preflight now proves the target first, WITHOUT the token: an unauthenticated `GET /app/rest/server` returns 401 with header `TeamCity-Node-Id` on the real server and a header-less 404 on the public host.
Discovery 4 — `Invoke-WebRequest` cannot express "I expect a non-2xx". It throws `System.Net.WebException` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and `HttpResponseException` on PowerShell 7, exposing the response headers differently, so a typed catch silently works on one host and kills the script on the other (reproduced under pwsh 7). `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` never throws on a status code and reads identically on both.
Decision: preflight + two parallel attempt jobs (either may defer with `queued=false`; a gate job fails only when neither queued and names the runners tried) + one shared script in `.github/scripts/queue-teamcity-build.ps1` checked out sparsely, so there is one copy of the logic rather than two inline duplicates. The structural fix is a runner label plus `runs-on: [self-hosted, <label>]` and needs a runner admin; the fallback exists only until that lands, and the preflight stays regardless.
Files: .github/workflows/teamcity-mcp-e2e.yml, .github/scripts/queue-teamcity-build.ps1
Impact: When a CI step fails with an HTTP status that does not match the service it is supposed to be talking to, compare the runners of the passing and failing runs before reading the code, and resolve the hostname the way the failing host resolves it. And never send a secret to a name before proving what answers at it.

## 2026-08-11 – ENG-94529: the first shape of the CI fix queued two 45-minute builds
Context: The preflight-plus-retry fix went in with TWO PARALLEL attempt jobs, on the assumption that a self-hosted runner takes one job at a time so two concurrent jobs land on two different runners and only one of them can reach TeamCity. Run 31489635011 proved the assumption wrong in the expensive direction.
Discovery 1 — the runner pool was bigger than the two runners the logs had shown. Attempt 1 ran on `TS1-MRKT-WEB01`, attempt 2 on `TS1-CORE-DEV24` - both in-network, both queued a build (#15860714, #15860715). Two concurrent full-Creatio e2e builds for one commit. Never infer a pool's membership from the runs you happened to look at.
Discovery 2 — the "is one already queued?" guard could not save it, because a queued build stops being queued almost immediately. With `moveToTop=true` and a free agent the build starts within seconds, so it is in `/app/rest/builds?running:true` and NOT in `/app/rest/buildQueue`. A queue-only check 27 s later read as "nothing there". Both states have to be inspected.
Discovery 3 — deduplicating on the BRANCH would have introduced a silent accuracy bug. A RUNNING build has already checked its sources out, so it cannot stand in for a commit pushed afterwards: branch-keyed dedupe would let an older build publish the status for newer code. The key is the commit, which travels in the build comment (the `BranchNameClio` parameter carries only the branch).
Decision: the attempts are now a SEQUENTIAL chain (attempt N runs only when no earlier attempt queued anything), so a duplicate is impossible by construction rather than by a check; no `always()` on the chain, so a genuine TeamCity error stops it instead of being retried twice; the commit-keyed queued-or-running check stays as the guard against a re-run (an automation re-running a red check produced a third build, #15860716, on a superseded commit).
Discovery 4 — `Invoke-WebRequest` cannot express "I expect a non-2xx" portably: `System.Net.WebException` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 versus `HttpResponseException` on 7, with headers exposed differently. `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` never throws on a status code and reads identically on both.
Files: .github/workflows/teamcity-mcp-e2e.yml, .github/scripts/queue-teamcity-build.ps1
Impact: A retry that fans out has to answer "what stops two of them from both succeeding?" before it ships, and the answer should be the control flow, not a race-prone lookup. Cancelling the strays cost two stands for ~10 minutes; the fix costs one extra sub-second job.

## 2026-08-11 – ENG-94529: a sparse checkout in a shared runner workspace broke an unrelated job
Context: The TeamCity-trigger workflow started checking out `.github/scripts` sparsely so the trigger script could live in one file instead of being inlined per attempt job. The next run's Unit Tests job - a different workflow - failed in 23 s with `MSBUILD : error MSB1009: Project file does not exist. Switch: .\clio.tests\clio.tests.csproj`, on the same runner the sparse checkout had used (`TS1-CORE-DEV24`).
Discovery: a self-hosted runner reuses ONE working directory per repository across every workflow (`_work\clio\clio`). A sparse checkout there narrows the tree for whatever runs next in that directory; `actions/checkout` does run `git sparse-checkout disable` on its next full checkout, and the log shows it did - yet the tree the build step saw still had no `clio.tests`. Whatever the exact git-level mechanism, the shared directory is not a safe place to narrow.
Decision: check out into `path: .teamcity-trigger`, a directory this workflow owns, and source the script from there. Inlining the script into all three attempt jobs was the alternative and was rejected: three copies of a credential-handling script is worse than one isolated checkout.
Files: .github/workflows/teamcity-mcp-e2e.yml
Impact: On self-hosted runners, treat the repository working directory as SHARED STATE. Anything that changes its shape - sparse checkout, a different ref, submodule config, a stray clean - can surface as a failure in an unrelated workflow, on that runner only, which reads as flakiness. Use `path:` for anything that is not the build itself.

## 2026-08-11 – ENG-94529: a "healthy" report that meant "there is no file"
Context: Review of PR #1026 found two Major defects in the new `SettingsRepository.Reload()` read path, both about what the non-repairing read hands back.
Discovery 1 — the missing-file case was indistinguishable from an empty configuration. `LoadUnlocked` returned status `"healthy"` with an empty `Settings` whether or not it had just CREATED the file. With `applyRepairs: false` nothing is created, so `Reload()` passed the `status == "broken"` guard, published the empty snapshot and `list-environments` answered with zero environments until the process restarted — the exact state the documented invariant promises never to reach. A read path that shares a loader with a repairing one must be able to tell "I fixed it" from "I only looked".
Discovery 2 — the post-load normalization ran after the settings lock was released. `_settings = result.Settings; EnsureSettingsCollections(); AttachDbServers(_settings);` publishes the object BEFORE initializing it, so a concurrent `GetAllEnvironments()`/`IsEnvironmentExists()` could see `Environments`/`Features` still null. The constructor gets away with the same three lines only because it runs once, single-threaded.
Decision: a dedicated `file-missing` status from the non-repairing read (the repairing path keeps `"healthy"`, which is true once it has written the file), handled by `Reload()` like `"broken"`; and `NormalizeSettings(Settings)` taking the instance as a parameter so the replacement snapshot is finished on a local variable and published with one reference assignment. `EnsureSettingsCollections()` is now a thin wrapper over it, so the ~15 existing call sites are unchanged.
Files: clio/Environment/SettingsBootstrapService.cs, clio/Environment/ConfigurationOptions.cs, clio/Environment/ISettingsRepository.cs, clio.tests/Command/SettingsRepositoryReloadTests.cs
Impact: When a field holds a snapshot that readers touch without a lock, normalize a local copy and publish once — the "assign then fix up" order is invisible in single-threaded tests and always wrong. And when adding a no-side-effects variant of a loader, check every status it can return: the status was written for the side-effecting path.
